sentences.zh: 陳獻章，字公甫，新會人。

translations.literal: Chen Xianzhang, style name Gongfu, was a native of Xinhui.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianzhang, styled Gongfu, came from Xinhui.

sentences.zh: 舉正統十二年鄉試，再上禮部，不第。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination in the twelfth year of Zhengtong, then went up to the Ministry of Rites again and failed to graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the twelfth year of the Zhengtong reign and later presented himself at the Ministry of Rites, but failed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 從吳與弼講學。

translations.literal: He followed Wu Yubi to study.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Wu Yubi.

sentences.zh: 居半載歸，讀書窮日夜不輟。

translations.literal: After half a year he returned home and read books day and night without ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: After six months he went home and read without pause, day and night.

sentences.zh: 築陽春臺，靜坐其中，數年無戶外跡。

translations.literal: He built the Yangchun Terrace and sat quietly within it; for several years there was no trace of him outside his door.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Yangchun Terrace and meditated there in seclusion; for years he scarcely set foot beyond his gate.

sentences.zh: 久之，復遊太學。

translations.literal: After a long while he again went to the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he returned to study at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 祭酒邢讓試和楊時《此日不再得》詩一篇，驚曰：「龜山不如也。

translations.literal: Director Xing Rang tested him with a matching poem to Yang Shi's 《This Day Will Not Come Again》, and in astonishment said, "Guiding Mountain falls short of this."
translations.idiomatic: When Director Xing Rang set him to compose a matching poem to Yang Shi's 《This Day Will Not Come Again》, he exclaimed in wonder, "Even Yang Shi could not match this."

sentences.zh: 」揚言於朝，以為真儒復出。

translations.literal: He proclaimed it at court, taking it as the reappearance of a true Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed this at court, declaring that a true Confucian had appeared again.

sentences.zh: 由是名震京師。

translations.literal: Thereupon his fame shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: From this his reputation resounded throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 給事中賀欽聽其議論，即日抗疏解官，執弟子禮事獻章。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary He Qin heard his discourse and that same day submitted a memorial resigning office, then served Xianzhang with the rites due a teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary He Qin heard him lecture and that very day memorialized to resign his post, thereafter honoring Xianzhang with the deference due a master.

sentences.zh: 獻章既歸，四方來學者日進。

translations.literal: After Xianzhang returned home, students came from all directions day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xianzhang had gone home, students flocked to him from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 廣東布政使彭韶、總督朱英交薦。

translations.literal: Guangdong Provincial Administration Commissioner Peng Shao and Grand Coordinator Zhu Ying jointly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Shao, administration commissioner of Guangdong, and Grand Coordinator Zhu Ying both recommended him.

sentences.zh: 召至京，令就試吏部。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital and ordered to take the Ministry of Personnel examination.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital and told to undergo examination at the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 屢辭疾不赴，疏乞終養，授翰林院檢討以歸。

translations.literal: He repeatedly pleaded illness and did not go; he memorialized begging to care for his mother to the end and was appointed Hanlin Academician-Compiler before returning home.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly pleaded illness and declined to attend; he memorialized asking to spend his mother's remaining years at her side and was granted the post of Hanlin Academician-Compiler before returning home.

sentences.zh: 至南安，知府張弼疑其拜官，與與弼不同。

translations.literal: When he reached Nan'an, Prefect Zhang Bi doubted that he had accepted office; what he said to Bi was not what Bi had expected.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Nan'an, Prefect Zhang Bi questioned why he had accepted office, since that seemed at odds with his principles.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「吳先生以布衣為石亨所薦，故不受職而求觀秘書，冀在開悟主上耳。

translations.literal: He replied, "Master Wu, as a commoner recommended by Shi Heng, therefore did not take office but sought to view the secret archives, hoping only to enlighten the sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Master Wu was a commoner whom Shi Heng recommended; he therefore refused an appointment and asked only to consult the palace archives, hoping to enlighten the emperor."

sentences.zh: 時宰不悟，先令受職然後觀書，殊戾先生意，遂決去。

translations.literal: The chief ministers did not understand; they first made him take office and only then view the books, greatly contrary to the Master's intent, so he resolved to leave.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers failed to understand; they insisted he take office before he might read the archives, which was utterly contrary to the Master's purpose, and so he left for good.

sentences.zh: 獻章聽選國子生，何敢偽辭釣虛譽。

translations.literal: Xianzhang was a National University student awaiting selection—how would he dare feign refusal to fish for empty reputation?
translations.idiomatic: As for myself, I was a National University student awaiting appointment—how could I feign refusal merely to win a hollow reputation?

sentences.zh: 」自是屢薦，卒不起。

translations.literal: From then on he was repeatedly recommended but in the end never took office.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he was recommended again and again, but in the end he never accepted office.

sentences.zh: 獻章之學，以靜為主。

translations.literal: Xianzhang's learning took stillness as its foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhang's teaching centered on stillness.

sentences.zh: 其教學者，但令端坐澄心，於靜中養出端倪。

translations.literal: In instructing students he only had them sit upright and clarify the mind, nurturing the first signs within stillness.
translations.idiomatic: He taught his disciples simply to sit upright and clear the mind, cultivating the first stirrings of insight in quietude.

sentences.zh: 或勸之著述，不答。

translations.literal: When some urged him to write books, he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: When others urged him to write, he would not comply.

sentences.zh: 嘗自言曰：「吾年二十七，始從吳聘君學，於古聖賢之書無所不講，然未知入處。

translations.literal: He once said of himself, "At twenty-seven I first studied with Master Wu the Recluse; there was nothing in the books of the ancient sages that I did not discuss, yet I still did not know how to enter."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "At twenty-seven I first studied with Master Wu; I read everything the ancient sages had written, yet I still could not find my way in."

sentences.zh: 比歸白沙，專求用力之方，亦卒未有得。

translations.literal: When I returned to Baisha I devoted myself to seeking the method of exertion, yet in the end still had no attainment.
translations.idiomatic: When I returned to Baisha I searched only for a method of real effort, yet still found nothing.

sentences.zh: 於是舍繁求約，靜坐久之，然後見吾心之體隱然呈露，日用應酬隨吾所欲，如馬之禦勒也。

translations.literal: Thereupon I abandoned the complex and sought the simple; after sitting quietly for a long time, I then saw the substance of my mind faintly revealed; in daily dealings it answered as I wished, like a horse under the bridle.
translations.idiomatic: So I set aside complexity for simplicity and sat in quiet for a long while, until the substance of my mind faintly disclosed itself; in daily affairs I could respond as I wished, like a horse that answers the rein.

sentences.zh: 」其學灑然獨得，論者謂有鳶飛魚躍之樂，而蘭溪姜麟至以為「活孟子」雲。

translations.literal: His learning was free and uniquely attained; commentators said it had the joy of kites flying and fish leaping, and Jiang Lin of Lanxi even called him a "living Mencius."
translations.idiomatic: His learning was attained with an unforced clarity of his own; critics said it held the joy of kites soaring and fish leaping, and Jiang Lin of Lanxi went so far as to call him a "living Mencius."

sentences.zh: 獻章儀幹修偉，右頰有七黑子。

translations.literal: Xianzhang's bearing was tall and imposing, and he had seven black moles on his right cheek.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhang was tall and imposing in bearing, with seven black moles on his right cheek.

sentences.zh: 母年二十四守節，獻章事之至孝。

translations.literal: His mother preserved her chastity at twenty-four; Xianzhang served her with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had been widowed at twenty-four; Xianzhang served her with the utmost filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 母有念，輒心動，即歸。

translations.literal: Whenever his mother had a thought of him his heart would stir and he would return at once.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his mother thought of him his heart would stir, and he would return home at once.

sentences.zh: 弘治十三年卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: He died in the thirteenth year of Hongzhi, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year of the Hongzhi reign, at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，從祀孔廟，追謚文恭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli he was enshrined in the Confucian temple and posthumously given the title Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign he was admitted to sacrifice in the Confucian temple and posthumously honored as Wengong.

sentences.zh: 門人李承箕，字世卿，嘉魚人。

translations.literal: His disciple Li Chengqi, style name Shiqing, was a native of Jiayu.
translations.idiomatic: His disciple Li Chengqi, styled Shiqing, came from Jiayu.

sentences.zh: 成化二十二年舉鄉試。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Chenghua he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of the Chenghua reign he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 往師獻章，獻章日與登涉山水，投壺賦詩，縱論古今事，獨無一語及道。

translations.literal: He went to take Xianzhang as teacher; day after day Xianzhang climbed hills and crossed waters with him, played pitch-pot and composed poetry, and discoursed freely on affairs ancient and modern—yet not a single word touched the Way.
translations.idiomatic: He went to study with Xianzhang, who day after day took him hiking among hills and streams, played pitch-pot and composed verse with him, and discoursed freely on past and present—yet never once spoke of the Way.

sentences.zh: 久之，承箕有所悟，辭歸，隱居黃公山，不復仕。

translations.literal: After a long while Chengqi had an awakening, took leave to return, and lived in seclusion on Mount Huangong, never again taking office.
translations.idiomatic: In time Chengqi came to an inner understanding, took his leave, and retired to Mount Huangong, never entering official life again.

sentences.zh: 與兄進士承芳，皆好學，稱嘉魚二李。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother, jinshi Chengfang, both loved learning and were called the Two Lis of Jiayu.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother Chengfang, who had passed the metropolitan examination, were both devoted to learning and were known as the Two Lis of Jiayu.

sentences.zh: 卒年五十四。

translations.literal: He died aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 張詡，字廷實，南海人，亦師事獻章。

translations.literal: Zhang Xu, style name Tingshi, was a native of Nanhai and also took Xianzhang as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xu, styled Tingshi, came from Nanhai and likewise studied under Xianzhang.

sentences.zh: 成化二十年舉進士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Chenghua he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of the Chenghua reign he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 尋丁憂，累薦不起。

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning; he was repeatedly recommended but would not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he entered mourning for a parent; though repeatedly recommended, he would not serve.

sentences.zh: 正德中，召為南京通政司參議，一謁孝陵即告歸。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde period he was summoned as Vice Commissioner of the Nanjing Office of Transmission; after one visit to the Xiaoling tomb he asked to return home.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he was summoned to serve as vice commissioner of the Nanjing Office of Transmission; after paying one visit to the Xiaoling Mausoleum he asked to go home.

sentences.zh: 獻章謂其學以自然為宗，以忘己為大，以無欲為至。

translations.literal: Xianzhang said his learning took the natural as its foundation, forgetting self as its greatness, and freedom from desire as its ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhang said his learning took nature as its foundation, self-forgetting as its height, and freedom from desire as its perfection.

sentences.zh: 卒年六十。

translations.literal: He died aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 婁諒，字克貞，上饒人。

translations.literal: Lou Liang, style name Kezhen, was a native of Shangrao.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Liang, styled Kezhen, came from Shangrao.

sentences.zh: 少有誌絕學。

translations.literal: From youth he aspired to supreme learning.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he aspired to master the highest learning.

sentences.zh: 聞吳與弼在臨川，往從之。

translations.literal: Hearing that Wu Yubi was at Linchuan, he went to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Wu Yubi was at Linchuan, he went to study with him.

sentences.zh: 一日，與弼治地，召諒往視，雲學者須親細務。

translations.literal: One day Yubi was working the land and summoned Liang to come look, saying a student must personally attend to small tasks.
translations.idiomatic: One day, as Yubi was working the fields, he called Liang over and said that a scholar must attend personally even to humble tasks.

sentences.zh: 諒素豪邁，由此折節。

translations.literal: Liang had always been bold and unrestrained; from this he restrained himself.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had always been proud and free-spirited; from this he learned to humble himself.

sentences.zh: 雖掃除之事，必身親之。

translations.literal: Even sweeping and cleaning he must do in person.
translations.idiomatic: Even sweeping and cleaning he would do with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 景泰四年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingtai he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Jingtai reign he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 天順末，選為成都訓導。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianshun he was selected as Instructor at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tianshun reign he was appointed instructor at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 尋告歸，閉門著書，成《日錄》四十卷、《三禮訂訛》四十卷。

translations.literal: Soon he asked to return home, closed his door and wrote books, completing forty juan of 《Daily Records》 and forty juan of 《Corrections to Errors in the Three Rites》.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he asked leave to return home, shut his door to write, and completed forty juan of 《Daily Records》 and forty juan of 《Corrections to Errors in the Three Rites》.

sentences.zh: 謂《周禮》皆天子之禮，為國禮。

translations.literal: He held that the 《Rites of Zhou》 were all rites of the Son of Heaven and constituted state rites.
translations.idiomatic: He held that the 《Rites of Zhou》 were entirely the ceremonial of the Son of Heaven and constituted the rites of the state.

sentences.zh: 《儀禮》皆公卿大夫士庶人之禮，為家禮。

translations.literal: The 《Ceremonies》 were all rites of dukes, ministers, grand masters, officers, and commoners, and constituted family rites.
translations.idiomatic: The 《Ceremonies》, he argued, were the rites of nobles, ministers, officers, and commoners, and constituted the rites of the household.

sentences.zh: 以《禮記》為二經之傳，分附各篇，如《冠禮》附《冠義》之類。

translations.literal: He took the 《Record of Rites》 as commentary to the two classics, dividing and attaching it to each section, as attaching the 《Meaning of the Capping Ceremony》 to the 《Capping Ceremony》.
translations.idiomatic: He treated the 《Record of Rites》 as commentary on the two classics, attaching each passage to its proper section—as, for example, attaching the 《Meaning of the Capping Ceremony》 to the 《Capping Ceremony》 itself.

sentences.zh: 不可附各篇者，各附一經之後。

translations.literal: What could not be attached to individual sections was each attached after one classic.
translations.idiomatic: Passages that could not be attached to a particular section he placed after the relevant classic as a whole.

sentences.zh: 不可附一經者，總附二經之後。

translations.literal: What could not be attached to one classic was altogether attached after the two classics.
translations.idiomatic: Passages that could not be assigned to either classic he placed after both classics together.

sentences.zh: 其為諸儒附會者，以程子論黜之。

translations.literal: Passages that were forced interpretations by the various Ru he rejected according to Master Cheng's discussions.
translations.idiomatic: Interpretations he judged to be forced concoctions of later scholars he set aside, following the arguments of Master Cheng.

sentences.zh: 著《春秋本意》十二篇，不采三傳事實，言：「是非必待三傳而後明，是《春秋》為棄書矣。

translations.literal: He wrote twelve chapters of 《Original Meaning of the Spring and Autumn》; he did not adopt factual accounts from the Three Commentaries, saying: "If right and wrong must wait for the Three Commentaries to become clear, then the 《Spring and Autumn》 becomes a discarded book."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote twelve chapters of 《Original Meaning of the Spring and Autumn》, taking no factual material from the Three Commentaries, and declared: "If right and wrong can be known only after the Three Commentaries, then the 《Spring and Autumn》 itself is a book cast aside."

sentences.zh: 」其學以收放心為居敬之門，以何思何慮、勿忘勿助為居敬要旨。

translations.literal: His learning took recovering the straying mind as the gateway to reverent composure, and "what thinking, what deliberating; do not forget, do not assist" as the essential purport of reverent composure.
translations.idiomatic: In his teaching, recovering the straying mind was the gateway to reverent composure, and "What thinking? What deliberating? Do not forget; do not assist" was its essential purport.

sentences.zh: 然其時胡居仁頗譏其近陸子，後羅欽順亦謂其似禪學雲。

translations.literal: Yet at that time Hu Juren rather mocked him as close to Master Lu; later Luo Qinshun also said his learning resembled Chan Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Hu Juren openly mocked him as too close to Master Lu; later Luo Qinshun likewise judged his learning akin to Chan Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 子忱，字誠善，傳父學。

translations.literal: His son Chen, styled Chengshan, transmitted his father's learning.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chen, styled Chengshan, carried on his father's learning.

sentences.zh: 女為寧王宸濠妃，有賢聲，嘗勸王毋反。

translations.literal: His daughter was consort to Prince Ning Chen Hao; she had a reputation for virtue and once urged the prince not to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter became consort to Prince Ning Chen Hao. Renowned for her virtue, she once urged the prince not to rebel.

sentences.zh: 王不聽，卒反。

translations.literal: The prince would not listen and ultimately rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The prince refused to listen and in the end rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 諒子姓皆捕系，遺文遂散軼矣。

translations.literal: All of Liang's sons and clansmen were arrested and imprisoned, and his surviving writings were scattered and lost.
translations.idiomatic: All of Liang's sons and kinsmen were arrested and imprisoned, and his surviving writings were scattered and lost.

sentences.zh: 門人夏尚樸，字敦夫，廣信永豐人。

translations.literal: His disciple Xia Shangpu, styled Dunfu, was a native of Yongfeng in Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: His disciple Xia Shangpu, styled Dunfu, came from Yongfeng in Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 正德初，會試赴京。

translations.literal: Early in the Zhengde reign he went to the capital for the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign he traveled to the capital for the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 見劉瑾亂政，慨然嘆曰：「時事如此，尚可幹進乎？

translations.literal: Seeing Liu Jin's perverse governance, he sighed deeply and said: "When affairs are like this, how can one still seek advancement?
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Liu Jin's corrupt rule, he sighed and said: "When the times are like this, how can one still pursue office?

sentences.zh: 」不試而歸。

translations.literal: " He did not take the examination and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: " He did not sit for the examination and returned home.

sentences.zh: 六年成進士，授南京禮部主事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he became a presented scholar and was appointed a principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he passed as a presented scholar and was appointed a principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，條上救荒數事。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he submitted in detail several measures for relieving distress.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year he submitted in detail several proposals for famine relief.

sentences.zh: 再遷惠州知府，投劾歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to be prefect of Huizhou, then submitted an impeachment of himself and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to serve as prefect of Huizhou, then impeached himself and retired.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，起山東提學副使。

translations.literal: Early in the Jiajing reign he was recalled as Vice Education Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he was recalled to serve as Vice Education Commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 擢南京太仆少卿，與魏校、湛若水輩日相講習。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud, and daily discoursed and studied with Wei Xiao, Zhan Ruoshui, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud, where he daily lectured and studied with Wei Xiao, Zhan Ruoshui, and others.

sentences.zh: 言官劾大學士桂萼，語連尚樸。

translations.literal: Censorial officials impeached Grand Secretary Gui E, and their language implicated Shangpu as well.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials impeached Grand Secretary Gui E, and their accusations implicated Shangpu as well.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書方獻夫白其無私，尋引疾歸。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Fang Xianfu cleared him of any partiality, but soon afterward he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Fang Xianfu testified to his integrity, but soon afterward he cited illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 早年師諒，傳主敬之學，常言「才提起，便是天理。

translations.literal: Early on he studied under Liang and transmitted the learning of reverent composure, often saying: "The moment you lift it up, that is the Principle of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he studied under Liang and carried forward the teaching of reverent composure, often saying: "The instant you lift it up, that is the Principle of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 才放下，便是人欲」。

translations.literal: The moment you put it down, that is human desire."
translations.idiomatic: The instant you put it down, that is human desire."

sentences.zh: 魏校亟稱之。

translations.literal: Wei Xiao praised him highly.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiao praised him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 所著有《中庸語》《東巖文集》。

translations.literal: His writings include 《Words on the Mean》 and 《Collected Works from Eastern Cliff》.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include 《Words on the Mean》 and 《Collected Works from Eastern Cliff》.

sentences.zh: 王守仁少時，亦嘗受業於諒。

translations.literal: When Wang Shouren was young, he also once received instruction from Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouren, too, in his youth once studied under Liang.

sentences.zh: 賀欽，字克恭，義州衛人。

translations.literal: He Qin, styled Kecong, was a native of Yizhou Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He Qin, styled Kecong, came from Yizhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 少好學，讀《近思錄》有悟。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning; reading the 《Nearness to Everyday Life》 he gained enlightenment.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning; reading the 《Nearness to Everyday Life》, he found enlightenment.

sentences.zh: 成化二年以進士授戶科給事中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua, as a presented scholar he was appointed a supervising secretary in the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chenghua he passed as a presented scholar and was appointed a supervising secretary in the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 已而師事陳獻章。

translations.literal: Before long he took Chen Xianzhang as his master.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he took Chen Xianzhang as his teacher.

sentences.zh: 既歸，肖其像事之。

translations.literal: After returning home, he had a portrait made in likeness of him and served it.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home, he had a portrait made in his likeness and venerated it.

sentences.zh: 弘治改元，用閣臣薦，起為陜西參議。

translations.literal: When the Hongzhi era began anew, on recommendation of grand secretaries he was recalled as Administration Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hongzhi reign began, on the recommendation of grand secretaries he was recalled as Administration Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 檄未至而母死，乃上疏懇辭，且陳四事。

translations.literal: The appointment letter had not arrived when his mother died; he thereupon memorialized earnestly declining and also set forth four matters.
translations.idiomatic: Before the appointment letter arrived, his mother died. He memorialized earnestly to decline the post and set forth four matters.

sentences.zh: 一，謂今日要務莫先經筵，當博訪真儒，以資啟沃。

translations.literal: First: he said that among present urgent tasks nothing comes before the classics lecture; true Confucians should be broadly sought to aid instruction and nurture.
translations.idiomatic: First, he argued that among the urgent tasks of the day nothing should precede the classics lecture, and that true Confucians should be widely sought to aid the ruler's instruction.

sentences.zh: 二，薦檢討陳獻章學術醇正，稱為大賢，宜以非常之禮起之，或俾參大政，或任經筵，以養君德。

translations.literal: Second: he recommended Compiler Chen Xianzhang, whose learning was pure and upright and whom he called a great worthy; he should be summoned by extraordinary rites, either to participate in great affairs of state or to serve at the classics lecture, so as to nurture the ruler's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Second, he recommended Compiler Chen Xianzhang, whose learning was pure and upright and whom he hailed as a great worthy. He should be summoned by extraordinary rites, either to share in great affairs of state or to serve at the classics lecture, so as to nurture the ruler's virtue.

sentences.zh: 三，內官職掌，載在《祖訓》，不過備灑掃、司啟閉而已。

translations.literal: Third: the duties of inner eunuchs, as recorded in the 《Ancestral Instructions》, were nothing more than providing sweeping and attendance, and managing opening and closing.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the duties of inner eunuchs, as recorded in the 《Ancestral Instructions》, were no more than sweeping, attendance, and the opening and closing of gates.

sentences.zh: 近如王振、曹吉祥、汪直等，或參預機宜，幹政令，招權納寵，邀功啟釁。

translations.literal: Recently such men as Wang Zhen, Cao Jixiang, and Wang Zhi either participated in state secrets, meddled in government orders, gathered power and received favor, or sought merit and provoked conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Recently men such as Wang Zhen, Cao Jixiang, and Wang Zhi have either joined in state secrets, meddled in government orders, gathered power and courted favor, or sought merit and provoked strife.

sentences.zh: 或引左道，進淫巧，以蕩上心。

translations.literal: Or they introduced heterodox ways and presented licentious artifices to distract the ruler's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Others have introduced heterodox teachings and licentious arts to unsettle the ruler's mind.

sentences.zh: 誤國殃民，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: To harm the state and afflict the people—nothing exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing has done more harm to the state and the people.

sentences.zh: 宜慎飭將來，內不使干預政事，外不使鎮守地方掌握兵權。

translations.literal: Future conduct should be strictly regulated: inwardly they must not be allowed to intervene in government; outwardly they must not be allowed to garrison regions and hold military power.
translations.idiomatic: Future conduct should be strictly regulated: inwardly they must not intervene in government; outwardly they must not garrison the provinces and hold military power.

sentences.zh: 四，興禮樂以化天下。

translations.literal: Fourth: raise rites and music to transform the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, rites and music should be revived to transform the realm.

sentences.zh: 「陛下紹基之初，舉行朱子喪葬之禮，而頹敗之俗因仍不改，乞申明正禮，革去教坊俗樂，以廣治化。

translations.literal: "At the beginning of Your Majesty's succession, the Zhu Xi rites for mourning and burial were implemented, yet decadent custom continued unchanged. I beg that the proper rites be clarified and vulgar music of the Music Office be abolished, to extend the reach of governance and transformation.
translations.idiomatic: "At the outset of Your Majesty's succession, the Zhu Xi rites for mourning and burial were enacted, yet decadent custom persists unchanged. I beg that the proper rites be clarified and the vulgar music of the Music Office abolished, so that governance and transformation may reach farther.

sentences.zh: 」疏凡數萬言。

translations.literal: " The memorial ran to tens of thousands of characters.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial ran to tens of thousands of characters.

sentences.zh: 奏入，報聞。

translations.literal: It was submitted and acknowledged.
translations.idiomatic: It was submitted and acknowledged.

sentences.zh: 正德四年，劉瑾括遼東田，東人震恐，而義州守又貪橫，民變，聚眾劫掠。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengde, Liu Jin seized Liaodong fields; easterners were shaken with fear, and the Yizhou prefect was also greedy and brutal. The people rose in revolt and gathered to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhengde, Liu Jin seized Liaodong fields and the people of the east were shaken with fear. The Yizhou prefect, too, was greedy and brutal; the people rose in revolt and gathered to plunder.

sentences.zh: 顧相戒曰：「毋驚賀黃門。

translations.literal: They mutually admonished one another, saying: "Do not alarm He the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: They warned one another, saying: "Do not alarm He the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 」欽聞之，急諭禍福，以身任之，亂遂定。

translations.literal: " Qin heard of it, hurriedly expounded fortune and disaster, took personal responsibility, and the disorder was settled.
translations.idiomatic: " When Qin heard of it, he hurriedly preached the consequences of fortune and disaster, took personal responsibility, and the disorder was settled.

sentences.zh: 欽學不務博涉，專讀《四書》、《六經》、《小學》，期於反身實踐。

translations.literal: Qin's learning did not pursue broad exposure; he read exclusively the 《Four Books》, the 《Six Classics》, and the 《Lesser Learning》, with the aim of turning back upon himself and putting practice into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Qin did not pursue wide reading. He devoted himself to the 《Four Books》, the 《Six Classics》, and the 《Lesser Learning》, aiming to turn inward and put what he learned into practice.

sentences.zh: 謂為學不必求之高遠，在主敬以收放心而已。

translations.literal: He held that in learning one need not seek what is lofty and distant; it lies simply in reverent composure to recover the straying mind.
translations.idiomatic: He held that learning need not reach for what is lofty and remote; it consists simply in reverent composure and recovering the straying mind.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十四。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 子士諮，鄉貢士，嘗陳十二事論王政，不報。

translations.literal: His son Shizi, a provincial graduate, once submitted twelve matters discussing royal governance; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shizi, a provincial graduate, once submitted twelve proposals on royal governance, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 終身不仕。

translations.literal: He never held office throughout his life.
translations.idiomatic: He never held office all his life.

sentences.zh: 陳茂烈，字時周，莆田人。

translations.literal: Chen Maolie, styled Shizhou, was a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Maolie, styled Shizhou, came from Putian.

sentences.zh: 年十八，作《省克錄》，謂顏之克己，曾之日省，學之法也。

translations.literal: At eighteen he wrote the 《Record of Reflection and Self-Restraint》, holding that Yan's self-conquest and Zeng's daily self-examination are the methods of learning.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he wrote the 《Record of Reflection and Self-Restraint》, holding that Yan's self-conquest and Zeng's daily self-examination are the true methods of learning.

sentences.zh: 弘治八年舉進士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Hongzhi he passed the imperial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Hongzhi he passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 奉使廣東，受業陳獻章之門，獻章語以主靜之學。

translations.literal: On a mission to Guangdong he received instruction at Chen Xianzhang's gate; Xianzhang spoke to him of the learning of maintaining stillness.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Guangdong he studied at Chen Xianzhang's gate, where Xianzhang taught him the learning of maintaining stillness.

sentences.zh: 退而與張詡論難，作《靜思錄》。

translations.literal: On returning he debated with Zhang Xu and wrote the 《Record of Quiet Reflection》.
translations.idiomatic: After returning he debated with Zhang Xu and wrote the 《Record of Quiet Reflection》.

sentences.zh: 尋授吉安府推官，考績過淮，寒無絮衣，凍幾殆。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed investigating prefect of Ji'an Prefecture. While passing Huai on performance review, the cold found him without padded clothing and he nearly perished from freezing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed investigating prefect of Ji'an Prefecture. While traveling through Huai on performance review, he had no padded coat against the cold and nearly died of exposure.

sentences.zh: 入為監察御史，袍服樸陋，乘一疲馬，人望而敬之。

translations.literal: He entered service as an investigating censor; his robes were plain and shabby and he rode a single worn-out horse—people looked upon him and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as an investigating censor. His robes were plain and shabby, and he rode a single worn-out horse; all who saw him treated him with respect.

sentences.zh: 以母老終養。

translations.literal: Because his mother was aged he retired to care for her until the end.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was old, he retired to care for her until her death.

sentences.zh: 供母之外，不辦一帷。

translations.literal: Apart from providing for his mother he kept not even a single curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from what he needed to support his mother, he kept not even a single curtain.

sentences.zh: 治畦汲水，身自操作。

translations.literal: He tended garden beds and drew water, performing the labor with his own body.
translations.idiomatic: He tended his garden beds and drew water, doing the work with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 太守聞其勞，進二卒助之，三日遣之還。

translations.literal: The prefect heard of his toil and sent two soldiers to assist him; after three days he sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect heard of his labors and sent two soldiers to help him, but after three days Maolie sent them back.

sentences.zh: 吏部以其貧，祿以晉江教諭，不受。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel, on account of his poverty, granted him salary as Instructor at Jinjiang, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel, seeing his poverty, offered him the salary of an instructor at Jinjiang, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 又奏給月米，上書言：「臣素貧，食本儉薄，故臣母自安於臣之家，而臣亦得以自逭其貧，非有及人之廉，盡己之孝也。

translations.literal: They also memorialized to grant him monthly rice. He submitted a memorial saying: "I have always been poor, and my salary is meager by nature, so my mother is content in my home and I am able to bear my poverty myself. This is not extraordinary integrity toward others, but simply doing my utmost in filial duty.
translations.idiomatic: The court also proposed granting him monthly rations of rice. He memorialized: "I have always been poor, and my salary is naturally meager, yet my mother is content in my home and I am able to endure my poverty on my own. This is not some extraordinary integrity shown toward others, but simply the fulfillment of filial duty.

sentences.zh: 古人行傭負米，皆以為親，臣之貧尚未至是。

translations.literal: In antiquity men worked as hired laborers and carried rice on their backs—all for their parents' sake; my poverty has not yet reached that point.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity men hired themselves out and carried rice on their backs—all for their parents' sake. My poverty has not yet reached that point.

sentences.zh: 而臣母鞠臣艱苦，今年八十有六，來日無多。

translations.literal: Yet my mother reared me through hardship; this year she is eighty-six and her remaining days are not many.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my mother reared me through hardship. This year she is eighty-six, and her remaining days are not many.

sentences.zh: 臣欲自盡心力，尚恐不及，上煩官帑，心竊未安。

translations.literal: I wish to exhaust myself in her service and still fear I may not suffice; to trouble the public treasury unsettles my heart.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to exhaust myself in her service and still fear I may not suffice. To trouble the public treasury would weigh on my conscience.

sentences.zh: 」奏上不允。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted and not approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was submitted and denied.

sentences.zh: 母卒，茂烈亦卒。

translations.literal: His mother died, and Maolie died as well.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died, Maolie died as well.

sentences.zh: 茂烈為諸生時，韓文問莆田人物於林俊，曰：「從吾。

translations.literal: When Maolie was a student, Han Wen asked Lin Jun about notable men of Putian; he said: "Congwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Maolie was still a student, Han Wen asked Lin Jun about notable men of Putian. Lin Jun said: "Congwu.

sentences.zh: 」謂彭時也。

translations.literal: " He meant Peng Shi.
translations.idiomatic: " He meant Peng Shi.

sentences.zh: 又問，曰：「時周。

translations.literal: Asked again, he said: "Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Asked again, he said: "Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 」且曰：「與時周語，沈屙頓去。

translations.literal: " And he added: "When I speak with Shizhou, my deep illness suddenly departs.
translations.idiomatic: " And he added: "When I speak with Shizhou, my lingering illness suddenly lifts.

sentences.zh: 」其為所重如此。

translations.literal: " He was held in such esteem.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 湛若水，字元明，增城人。

translations.literal: Zhan Ruoshui, styled Yuanming, was a native of Zengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Ruoshui, styled Yuanming, came from Zengcheng.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年舉於鄉，從陳獻章遊，不樂仕進。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Hongzhi he passed the provincial examination; he followed Chen Xianzhang and did not delight in seeking office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Hongzhi he passed the provincial examination and followed Chen Xianzhang, taking no pleasure in pursuing office.

sentences.zh: 母命之出，乃入南京國子監。

translations.literal: When his mother ordered him to go forth, he entered the Nanjing Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother ordered him to enter public life, he enrolled in the Nanjing Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 十八年會試，學士張元禎、楊廷和為考官，撫其卷曰：「非白沙之徒不能為此。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year at the metropolitan examination, Academicians Zhang Yuanzhen and Yang Tinghe were examiners; stroking his examination paper, one said: "No one but a disciple of Baisha could write this.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, at the metropolitan examination, Academicians Zhang Yuanzhen and Yang Tinghe served as examiners. Stroking Ruoshui's paper, one said: "Only a disciple of Baisha could write this.

sentences.zh: 」置第二。

translations.literal: " He was placed second.
translations.idiomatic: " He was ranked second.

sentences.zh: 賜進士，選庶吉士，授翰林院編修。

translations.literal: He was granted the title of presented scholar, selected as a probationary academician, and appointed compiling secretary of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the title of presented scholar, selected as a probationary academician, and appointed a compiling secretary in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 時王守仁在吏部講學，若水與相應和。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Shouren lectured at the Ministry of Personnel, and Ruoshui responded in harmony with him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Shouren was lecturing at the Ministry of Personnel, and Ruoshui responded in harmony with him.

sentences.zh: 尋丁母憂，廬墓三年。

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning for his mother and dwelled by the grave for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his mother and lived by her grave for three years.

sentences.zh: 築西樵講舍，士子來學者，先令習禮，然後聽講。

translations.literal: He built a lecture hall at Xiqiao; for students who came to study, he first had them practice rites, and only then allowed them to hear lectures.
translations.idiomatic: He built a lecture hall at Xiqiao. For every student who came to study, he first required the practice of rites and only then allowed them to hear lectures.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，入朝，上經筵講學疏，謂聖學以求仁為要。

translations.literal: Early in the Jiajing reign he entered court and submitted a memorial on lecturing at the classics lecture, holding that sage learning takes seeking benevolence as its essential.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign he entered court and submitted a memorial on lecturing at the classics lecture, arguing that sage learning takes the pursuit of benevolence as its essential.

sentences.zh: 已復上疏言：「陛下初政，漸不克終。

translations.literal: Then he again memorialized, saying: "Your Majesty's initial governance is gradually failing to reach completion.
translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized again, saying: "Your Majesty's early governance is gradually failing to reach its proper end.

sentences.zh: 左右近侍爭以聲色異教蠱惑上心。

translations.literal: Those close at hand and in attendance compete to use sensual pleasures and heterodox teachings to bewitch the ruler's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Those close at hand and in attendance vie to beguile the ruler's mind with sensual pleasures and heterodox teachings.

sentences.zh: 大臣林俊、孫交等不得守法，多自引去，可為寒心。

translations.literal: Grand ministers such as Lin Jun and Sun Jiao cannot uphold the law and mostly withdraw on their own—it is enough to chill the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Grand ministers such as Lin Jun and Sun Jiao cannot uphold the law and mostly withdraw on their own—a sight chilling to the heart.

sentences.zh: 亟請親賢遠奸，窮理講學，以隆太平之業。

translations.literal: I urgently beg that you be close to the worthy and distant from the wicked, exhaust principle and lecture on learning, to elevate the enterprise of great peace.
translations.idiomatic: I urgently beg that Your Majesty draw near the worthy and keep the wicked at a distance, exhaust principle and lecture on learning, and so raise up the cause of great peace.

sentences.zh: 」又疏言日講不宜停止，報聞。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized that daily lectures ought not be stopped; acknowledgment was received.
translations.idiomatic: " He also memorialized that daily lectures ought not be suspended; the memorial was acknowledged.

sentences.zh: 明年進侍讀，復疏言：「一二年間，天變地震，山崩川湧，人饑相食，殆無虛月。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Reader; he again memorialized, saying: "In the past year or two there have been celestial omens, earthquakes, mountains collapsing and rivers surging, people starving until they eat one another—hardly a month without such events.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was promoted to Reader and again memorialized, saying: "In the past year or two there have been celestial omens, earthquakes, mountains collapsing and rivers surging, and people starving until they eat one another—hardly a month without such calamities.

sentences.zh: 夫聖人不以屯否之時而後視賢之訓，明醫不以深錮之疾而廢元氣之劑，宜博求修明先王之道者，日侍文華，以裨聖學。

translations.literal: A sage does not only then regard worthy instruction when times are stagnant and blocked; a skilled physician does not abandon medicines that restore vital force because the illness is deeply entrenched. Those who broadly expound and clarify the Way of the former kings should be sought, to attend daily at Wenhua Palace and support sage learning.
translations.idiomatic: A sage does not wait for times of stagnation and distress before heeding worthy instruction; a skilled physician does not abandon restorative medicines because the illness runs deep. Those who broadly expound and clarify the Way of the former kings should be sought to attend daily at Wenhua Palace and support the ruler's sage learning.

sentences.zh: 」已，遷南京國子監祭酒，作《心性圖說》以教士。

translations.literal: " Soon after he was transferred to be Chancellor of the Nanjing Directorate of Education and wrote the 《Diagrammatic Treatise on Nature and Mind》 to instruct scholars.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward he was transferred to Chancellor of the Nanjing Directorate of Education and wrote the 《Diagrammatic Treatise on Nature and Mind》 to instruct scholars.

sentences.zh: 拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 仿《大學衍義補》，作《格物通》，上於朝。

translations.literal: Following the model of the 《Supplement to the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning》, he wrote the 《General Treatise on Investigating Things》 and submitted it to court.
translations.idiomatic: Following the model of the 《Supplement to the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning》, he wrote the 《General Treatise on Investigating Things》 and submitted it to court.

sentences.zh: 歷南京吏、禮、兵三部尚書。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Minister of the Nanjing Ministries of Personnel, Rites, and War.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Minister of the Nanjing Ministries of Personnel, Rites, and War.

sentences.zh: 南京欲尚侈靡，為定喪葬之制頒行之。

translations.literal: As Nanjing tended toward extravagant display, he fixed regulations for funerals and burials and promulgated them.
translations.idiomatic: As Nanjing tended toward extravagant display, he fixed regulations for funerals and burials and promulgated them.

sentences.zh: 老，請致仕。

translations.literal: In old age he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 年九十五卒。

translations.literal: He died at ninety-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of ninety-five.

sentences.zh: 若水生平所至，必建書院以祀獻章。

translations.literal: Wherever Ruoshui went in life, he invariably built an academy to sacrifice to Xianzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Ruoshui went in life, he invariably built an academy to honor and sacrifice to Xianzhang.

sentences.zh: 年九十，猶為南京之遊。

translations.literal: At ninety he still made the journey to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: At ninety he still made the journey to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 過江西，安福鄒守益，守仁弟子也，戒其同誌曰：「甘泉先生來，吾輩當憲老而不乞言，慎毋輕有所論辨。

translations.literal: Passing through Jiangxi, Zou Shouyi of Anfu—a disciple of Shouren—admonished his fellow students, saying: "Mr. Ganquan is coming; we should revere the aged without begging instruction, and must not lightly engage in debate.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Jiangxi, Zou Shouyi of Anfu—a disciple of Shouren—warned his fellow students: "Mr. Ganquan is coming. We should revere the aged without begging instruction, and must not lightly enter into debate.

sentences.zh: 」若水初與守仁同講學，後各立宗旨，守仁以致良知為宗，若水以隨處體驗天理為宗。

translations.literal: " Ruoshui had at first lectured together with Shouren, but later each established his own teaching: Shouren took extending innate knowledge as his principle, while Ruoshui took experiencing the Principle of Heaven everywhere as his principle.
translations.idiomatic: " Ruoshui had at first lectured together with Shouren, but later each established his own teaching: Shouren made extending innate knowledge his principle, while Ruoshui made experiencing the Principle of Heaven everywhere his principle.

sentences.zh: 守仁言若水之學為求之於外，若水亦謂守仁格物之說不可信者四。

translations.literal: Shouren said Ruoshui's learning seeks externally; Ruoshui also held that there were four points on which Shouren's doctrine of investigating things could not be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren charged that Ruoshui's learning looked outward for what should be found within; Ruoshui, in turn, identified four reasons why Shouren's theory of investigating things could not be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「陽明與吾言心不同。

translations.literal: He also said: "Yangming and I speak of the mind differently."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Yangming and I do not mean the same thing when we speak of the mind."

sentences.zh: 陽明所謂心，指方寸而言。

translations.literal: The mind that Yangming speaks of refers to the square inch.
translations.idiomatic: What Yangming calls the mind is the mind confined to the square inch of the heart.

sentences.zh: 吾之所謂心者，體萬物而不遺者也，故以吾之說為外。

translations.literal: The mind I speak of is that which embodies all things without omitting any; hence they take my teaching to be external.
translations.idiomatic: What I call the mind is that which embraces all things and leaves nothing out—so they dismiss my teaching as outward-looking.

sentences.zh: 」一時學者遂分王、湛之學。

translations.literal: At that time scholars thereupon divided into the schools of Wang and Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: For a time, scholars split into followers of Wang and followers of Zhan.

sentences.zh: 湛氏門人最著者，永豐呂懷、德安何遷、婺源洪垣、歸安唐樞。

translations.literal: Among Zhan's most prominent disciples were Lü Huai of Yongfeng, He Qian of De'an, Hong Yuan of Wuyuan, and Tang Shu of Gui'an.
translations.idiomatic: The most notable of Zhan's disciples were Lü Huai of Yongfeng, He Qian of De'an, Hong Yuan of Wuyuan, and Tang Shu of Gui'an.

sentences.zh: 懷之言變化氣質，遷之言知止，樞之言求真心，大約出入王、湛兩家之間，而別為一義。

translations.literal: Huai spoke of transforming temperament; Qian spoke of knowing where to stop; Shu spoke of seeking the true mind—broadly moving between the Wang and Zhan schools, yet each setting forth a separate meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Huai taught the transformation of one's temperament; Qian taught knowing where to stop; Shu taught seeking the true mind. Broadly, they moved between the Wang and Zhan schools, yet each carved out a doctrine of his own.

sentences.zh: 垣則主於調停兩家，而互救其失。

translations.literal: Yuan, for his part, chiefly sought to mediate between the two schools, each remedying the other's failings.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan took reconciliation as his aim, mediating between the two schools and correcting each where the other fell short.

sentences.zh: 皆不盡守師說也。

translations.literal: None fully adhered to their master's teachings.
translations.idiomatic: None of them wholly kept to their master's doctrine.

sentences.zh: 懷，字汝德，南京太仆少卿。

translations.literal: Huai, courtesy name Rude, was Vice Minister of the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Huai, styled Rude, served as Vice Minister of the Nanjing Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 遷，字益之，南京刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Qian, courtesy name Yizhi, was Vice Minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, styled Yizhi, was Vice Minister of the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 垣，字峻之，溫州府知府。

translations.literal: Yuan, courtesy name Junzhi, was Prefect of Wenzhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, styled Junzhi, was Prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 樞，刑部主事，疏論李福達事，罷歸，自有傳。

translations.literal: Shu, a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice, memorialized on the Li Fuda affair, was dismissed and returned home; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice, submitted a memorial on the Li Fuda case, was dismissed, and returned home; he has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 蔣信，字卿實，常德人。

translations.literal: Jiang Xin, courtesy name Qingshi, was a native of Changde.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xin, styled Qingshi, came from Changde.

sentences.zh: 年十四，居喪毀瘠。

translations.literal: At fourteen, while in mourning he wasted away from grief.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen, while mourning his parents, he was so stricken with grief that his body wasted away.

sentences.zh: 與同郡冀元亨善，王守仁謫龍場，過其地，偕元亨事焉。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Ji Yuanheng of the same prefecture; when Wang Shouren was exiled to Longchang and passed through the region, he and Yuanheng together went to serve him.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Ji Yuanheng, a fellow townsman. When Wang Shouren was banished to Longchang and passed through the area, Jiang and Yuanheng went together to attend him.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，貢入京師，復師湛若水。

translations.literal: In the early Jiajing era he entered the capital as a tribute student and again took Zhan Ruoshui as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Jiajing reign he went to the capital as a tribute student and once more became a disciple of Zhan Ruoshui.

sentences.zh: 若水為南祭酒，門下士多分教。

translations.literal: Ruoshui served as Chancellor of the Southern National Academy, and his disciples were largely dispersed to teach in various posts.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruoshui was Chancellor of the Southern National Academy, most of his disciples were sent out to teach in separate appointments.

sentences.zh: 至十一年，舉進士，累官四川水利僉事。

translations.literal: By the eleventh year he passed the jinshi examination and rose through offices to Assistant Commissioner for Water Conservancy in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he passed the jinshi examination and eventually rose to Assistant Commissioner for Water Conservancy in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 卻播州土官賄，置妖道士於法。

translations.literal: He refused bribes from the native official of Bozhou and had a sorcerer-priest punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He turned back bribes from the Bozhou native chieftain and had a rogue Daoist priest dealt with by law.

sentences.zh: 遷貴州提學副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of Education in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of Education in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 建書院二，廩群髦士其中。

translations.literal: He built two academies and supported outstanding scholars within them.
translations.idiomatic: He founded two academies and maintained a company of gifted scholars in them.

sentences.zh: 龍場故有守仁祠，為置祠田。

translations.literal: Longchang already had a shrine to Shouren; he endowed it with shrine lands.
translations.idiomatic: Longchang already had a shrine to Shouren; he set aside land to support it.

sentences.zh: 坐擅離職守，除名。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office and struck from the rolls for leaving his post without authorization.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of his name from the register for abandoning his post without leave.

sentences.zh: 信初從守仁遊時，未以良知教。

translations.literal: When Xin first followed Shouren, the teaching of innate knowing had not yet been given.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin first studied under Shouren, the doctrine of innate knowing had not yet been taught.

sentences.zh: 後從若水遊最久，學得之湛氏為多。

translations.literal: Later he followed Ruoshui longest, and what he learned came mostly from the Zhan school.
translations.idiomatic: He later studied longest under Ruoshui, and most of what he gained came from the Zhan school.

sentences.zh: 信踐履篤實，不事虛談。

translations.literal: Xin was earnest and solid in practice, and did not indulge in empty talk.
translations.idiomatic: Xin was steadfast in conduct and would not waste words on idle speculation.

sentences.zh: 湖南學者宗其教，稱之曰正學先生。

translations.literal: Scholars in Hunan looked to his teaching and called him Master of Correct Learning.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars in Hunan took his teaching as their standard and honored him as Master of Correct Learning.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十九。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 時宜興周沖，字道通，亦遊王、湛之門。

translations.literal: At that time Zhou Chong of Yixing, courtesy name Daotong, also studied under both Wang and Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, Zhou Chong of Yixing, styled Daotong, also studied in the circles of both Wang and Zhan.

sentences.zh: 由舉人授高安訓導，至唐府紀善。

translations.literal: Starting as an appointed instructor in Gao'an, he rose to Record-keeper of the Tang princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: From an instructor's post in Gao'an he advanced to Record-keeper in the household of the Prince of Tang.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「湛之體認天理，即王之致良知也。

translations.literal: He once said: "Zhan's embodying of Heavenly principle is Wang's extending of innate knowing."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Zhan's inward apprehension of Heavenly principle is the same thing as Wang's extension of innate knowing."

sentences.zh: 」與信集師說為《新泉問辨錄》。

translations.literal: Together with Xin he compiled the masters' teachings into the Records of Inquiry at Xin Spring.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xin gathered their teachers' teachings into the Records of Inquiry at Xin Spring.

sentences.zh: 兩家門人各相非笑，沖為疏通其旨焉。

translations.literal: Disciples of the two schools mocked one another; Chong worked to clarify their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Disciples on both sides derided each other; Chong set himself to opening a path between their intentions.

sentences.zh: 鄒守益，字謙之，安福人。

translations.literal: Zou Shouyi, courtesy name Qianzhi, was a native of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Shouyi, styled Qianzhi, came from Anfu.

sentences.zh: 父賢，字恢才，弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: His father Xian, courtesy name Huicai, passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xian, styled Huicai, became a jinshi in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 授南京大理評事，數有條奏，歷官福建僉事，擒殺武平賊渠黃友勝。

translations.literal: Appointed Evaluating Secretary in the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review, he submitted many well-reasoned memorials; in office he rose to Assistant Commissioner in Fujian and captured and killed the bandit chieftain Huang Yousheng of Wuping.
translations.idiomatic: Made Evaluating Secretary in the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review, he submitted many pointed memorials; rising through office to Assistant Commissioner in Fujian, he captured and killed the Wuping bandit leader Huang Yousheng.

sentences.zh: 居家以孝友稱。

translations.literal: At home he was known for filial piety and brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: In private life he was praised for filial devotion and brotherly kindness.

sentences.zh: 守益舉正德六年會試第一，出王守仁門。

translations.literal: Shouyi placed first in the metropolitan examination of the sixth year of Zhengde and was a disciple of Wang Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi ranked first in the metropolitan examination of the sixth year of Zhengde and was a pupil of Wang Shouren.

sentences.zh: 以廷對第三人授翰林院編修。

translations.literal: For placing third in the palace examination he was appointed Compiler in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Placing third in the palace examination, he was appointed a Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 逾年告歸，謁守仁，講學於贛州。

translations.literal: The next year he asked to return home, visited Shouren, and lectured at Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he sought leave to go home, visited Shouren, and lectured at Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 宸濠反，與守仁軍事。

translations.literal: When Chen Hao rebelled, he took part in Shouren's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Ning rebelled, he served with Shouren in the field.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，始赴官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, he at last took up his appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Emperor Shizong took the throne did he finally assume office.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年二月，帝欲去興獻帝本生之稱。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Jiajing, the Emperor wished to remove the title referring to the Xingxian Emperor as his biological father.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year of Jiajing, the Emperor wished to drop the designation of the Xingxian Emperor as his biological father.

sentences.zh: 守益疏諫，忤旨，被責。

translations.literal: Shouyi memorialized in remonstrance, offended the imperial will, and was rebuked.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi remonstrated by memorial, ran against the imperial will, and was reprimanded.

sentences.zh: 逾月，復上疏曰：

translations.literal: After more than a month he again submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later he submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 陛下欲隆本生之恩，屢下群臣會議，群臣據禮正言，致蒙詰讓，道路相傳，有孝長子之稱。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty wishes to exalt the favor owed to your biological father and has repeatedly ordered the ministers to confer; the ministers, citing ritual, spoke uprightly, yet were rebuked and reproached. It is said in the streets that Your Majesty is a filial eldest son."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty wishes to magnify the debt owed to your biological father and has repeatedly called the ministers into conference; they answered according to ritual, only to be questioned and reproached. Word in the streets has it that you are a filial eldest son."

sentences.zh: 昔曾元以父寢疾，憚於易簀，蓋愛之至也。

translations.literal: "In antiquity, when Zeng Yuan's father lay ill, he shrank from changing the mat—such was the depth of his love."
translations.idiomatic: "Long ago, when Zeng Yuan's father lay ill, he could not bear to change the mat beside him—love pushed him that far."

sentences.zh: 而曾子責之曰：「姑息」。

translations.literal: "Yet Zengzi rebuked him, saying 'This is indulgence.'"
translations.idiomatic: "Yet Zengzi rebuked him with the word 'indulgence.'"

sentences.zh: 魯公受天子禮樂，以祀周公，蓋尊之至也。

translations.literal: "The Duke of Lu received from the Son of Heaven the rites and music with which to sacrifice to the Duke of Zhou—such was the height of honor."
translations.idiomatic: "The Duke of Lu received from the Son of Heaven the rites and music for sacrificing to the Duke of Zhou—honor could go no higher."

sentences.zh: 而孔子傷之曰「周公其衰矣」。

translations.literal: "Yet Confucius mourned this, saying, 'The Duke of Zhou must be in decline.'"
translations.idiomatic: "Yet Confucius grieved over it, saying, 'Alas for the decline of the Duke of Zhou.'"

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下勿以姑息事獻帝，而使後世有其衰之嘆。

translations.literal: "Your servant begs Your Majesty not to treat the Xingxian Emperor with indulgence, lest later ages sigh over your decline."
translations.idiomatic: "I beg Your Majesty not to show the Xingxian Emperor the indulgence that invites later ages to lament your decline."

sentences.zh: 且群臣援經證古，欲陛下專意正統，此皆為陛下忠謀，乃不察而督過之，謂忤且慢。

translations.literal: "Moreover, the ministers cite the classics and prove by antiquity that Your Majesty should fix his mind on the legitimate succession; all this is loyal counsel on Your Majesty's behalf, yet without discernment you reprove them, calling it defiance and disrespect."
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover, the ministers appeal to the classics and the past because they want Your Majesty to hold fast to the legitimate line of succession. That is loyal counsel offered for your sake—yet you fail to see it and instead rebuke them as defiant and disrespectful."

sentences.zh: 臣歷觀前史，如冷褒、段猶之徒，當時所謂忠愛，後世所斥以為邪媚也。

translations.literal: "Your servant has looked through the histories: men such as Leng Bao and Duan You were then called loyal and loving, but later ages condemned them as sycophantic."
translations.idiomatic: "I have read the histories: men like Leng Bao and Duan You were praised in their day as loyal and devoted, yet posterity condemned them as flatterers."

sentences.zh: 師丹、司馬光之徒，當時所謂欺慢，後世所仰以為正直也。

translations.literal: "Men such as Shi Dan and Sima Guang were then called deceitful and disrespectful, yet later ages revered them as upright."
translations.idiomatic: "Men like Shi Dan and Sima Guang were denounced in their day as deceitful and insolent, yet posterity honors them as upright."

sentences.zh: 後之視今，猶今之視古。

translations.literal: "Those who come after will view the present as the present views antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: "Posterity will judge our age as we judge the ages before us."

sentences.zh: 望陛下不吝改過，察群臣之忠愛，信而用之，復召其去國者，無使奸人動搖國是，離間宮闈。

translations.literal: "Your servant hopes Your Majesty will not be sparing in correcting error, will discern the ministers' loyal devotion, trust and employ them, recall those who have left office, and not let wicked men shake the nation's settled course or sow discord within the palace."
translations.idiomatic: "I pray Your Majesty will not refuse to amend your course, will recognize the ministers' loyal devotion, trust and use them, recall those who have gone into exile, and not allow schemers to unsettle the nation's settled policy or drive wedges into the inner court."

sentences.zh: 昔先帝南巡，群臣交章諫阻，先帝赫然震怒，豈不謂欺慢可罪哉。

translations.literal: "Formerly, when the late Emperor made his southern tour, the ministers submitted memorial after memorial to dissuade him; the late Emperor was greatly enraged and surely thought such deceit and disrespect punishable."
translations.idiomatic: "When the late Emperor toured the south, the ministers piled memorial upon memorial to stop him; he flared with anger and no doubt judged such counsel deceitful and punishable."

sentences.zh: 陛下在藩邸聞之，必以是為盡忠於先帝。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty, then in the princely residence, hearing this, must have taken it for perfect loyalty to the late Emperor."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty, then still in the princely residence, must have taken that to be the measure of loyalty to the late Emperor."

sentences.zh: 今入繼大統，獨不容群臣盡忠於陛下乎。

translations.literal: "Now that you have succeeded to the great succession, will you alone not allow the ministers to show perfect loyalty to Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: "Now that you have entered the great succession, will you alone refuse the ministers the same perfect loyalty they owe to you?"

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，下詔獄拷掠，謫廣德州判官。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged, had him thrown into the imperial prison and tortured, and demoted him to Assistant Magistrate of Guangde Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage, had him thrown into the imperial prison and tortured, and banished him to the post of Assistant Magistrate of Guangde.

sentences.zh: 廢淫祠，建復初書院，與學者講授其間。

translations.literal: He abolished licentious shrines, built the Fuchu Academy, and lectured to scholars there.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished illicit shrines, founded the Fuchu Academy, and lectured to scholars within it.

sentences.zh: 稍遷南京禮部郎中，州人立生祠以祀。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites; the people of the prefecture erected a living shrine in his honor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites, and the people of Guangde raised a living shrine to honor him.

sentences.zh: 聞守仁卒，為位哭，服心喪，日與呂柟、湛若水、錢德洪、王畿、薛侃輩論學。

translations.literal: When he heard that Shouren had died, he set up a mourning seat and wept, observed the heart-mourning rites, and daily discussed learning with Lü Kun, Zhan Ruoshui, Qian Dehong, Wang Ji, Xue Kan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing of Shouren's death he set up a place to mourn, wept for him, observed heart-mourning rites, and each day debated learning with Lü Kun, Zhan Ruoshui, Qian Dehong, Wang Ji, Xue Kan, and the like.

sentences.zh: 考滿入都，即引疾歸。

translations.literal: When his term of service was complete he entered the capital, then immediately pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When his term was complete he went to the capital, then at once pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 久之，以薦起南京吏部郎中，召為司經局洗馬。

translations.literal: After a long while, on recommendation he was recalled as Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, then summoned as Reader in the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was recommended back to service as Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, then summoned to be Reader in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 守益以太子幼，未能出閣，乃與霍韜上《聖功圖》，自神堯茅茨土階，至帝西苑耕稼蠶桑，凡為圖十三。

translations.literal: Shouyi, seeing the crown prince still young and not yet installed in his own palace, together with Huo Tao submitted the Diagram of Sagely Achievement, from the thatched halls and earthen steps of the Divine Yao down to the Emperor's plowing and sericulture in the Western Park—altogether thirteen illustrations.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the crown prince still young and not yet installed in his own quarters, Shouyi joined Huo Tao in presenting the Diagram of Sagely Achievement—thirteen illustrations running from the thatched halls and earthen steps of the Divine Yao down to the Emperor's farming and sericulture in the Western Park.

sentences.zh: 帝以為謗訕，幾得罪，賴韜受帝知，事乃解。

translations.literal: The Emperor took it for slander and he nearly fell into guilt; only because Huo Tao enjoyed the Emperor's trust was the affair resolved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor read it as slander and Shouyi nearly came to grief; only Huo Tao's standing with the Emperor saved the matter.

sentences.zh: 明年遷太常少卿兼侍讀學士，出掌南京翰林院，夏言欲遠之也。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Ceremonies and Concurrent Reader, and sent out to head the Nanjing Hanlin Academy—Xia Yan wished to keep him at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Vice Minister of Ceremonies and Concurrent Reader and sent out to head the Nanjing Hanlin Academy—Xia Yan wanted him far from court.

sentences.zh: 御史毛愷請留侍東宮，被謫。

translations.literal: Censor Mao Kai asked that he be kept to attend the Eastern Palace and was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Mao Kai petitioned that Shouyi be kept to serve the Eastern Palace and was himself demoted.

sentences.zh: 尋改南京祭酒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was changed to Chancellor of the Nanjing National Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reassigned as Chancellor of the Nanjing National Academy.

sentences.zh: 九廟災，守益陳上下交修之道，言：「殷中宗、高宗，反妖為祥，亨國長久。

translations.literal: When the Nine Temples burned, Shouyi set forth the way of mutual cultivation above and below, saying: "The Middle and High Ancestors of Yin turned evil omens into blessings and long preserved the realm."
translations.idiomatic: When fire destroyed the Nine Temples, Shouyi laid out the path of mutual reform above and below, saying, "The Middle and High Ancestors of Yin turned evil portents into blessings and held the realm for ages."

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，落職歸。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged and dismissed him from office to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and stripped him of office, sending him home.

sentences.zh: 守益天姿純粹。

translations.literal: Shouyi's native endowment was pure and unmixed.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi's nature was pure and unclouded.

sentences.zh: 守仁嘗曰：「有若無，實若虛，犯而不校，謙之近之矣。

translations.literal: Shouren once said: "Having yet seeming not to have, full yet seeming empty, wronged yet not contending—Qianzhi comes close to this."
translations.idiomatic: Shouren once said of him, "To possess yet seem not to possess, to be full yet seem empty, to be wronged yet not strike back—Qianzhi comes near to this."

sentences.zh: 」裏居，日事講學，四方從遊者踵至，學者稱東廓先生。

translations.literal: Living in retirement, he lectured daily; followers from the four quarters came in succession, and scholars called him Master Dongkuo.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he lectured every day; students from every quarter flocked to him, and scholars honored him as Master Dongkuo.

sentences.zh: 居家二十余年卒。

translations.literal: After more than twenty years at home he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home after more than twenty years in retirement.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈南京禮部右侍郎，謚文莊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was posthumously made Vice Minister of Rites in Nanjing, with the posthumous title Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Longqing he was posthumously made Nanjing Vice Minister of Rites, with the posthumous title Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 先是，守仁主山東試，堂邑穆孔暉第一，後官侍講學士，卒，贈禮部右侍郎，謚文簡。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shouren presided over the Shandong provincial examination, Mu Konghui of Tangyi placed first; he later served as Reader and died; posthumously he was made Vice Minister of Rites, with the posthumous title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shouren supervised the Shandong provincial examinations, Mu Konghui of Tangyi ranked first; he later served as Reader, and after death was posthumously made Vice Minister of Rites with the title Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 孔暉端雅好學，初不肯宗守仁說，久乃篤信之，自名王氏學，浸淫入於釋氏。

translations.literal: Konghui was dignified and fond of learning; at first he would not adopt Shouren's teaching, but in time came to believe in it deeply, styled himself a follower of the Wang school, and gradually drifted into Buddhist teachings.
translations.idiomatic: Konghui was refined and devoted to learning; at first he refused Shouren's doctrine, but in time came to embrace it wholeheartedly, took the name of the Wang school, and little by little sank into Buddhist ideas.

sentences.zh: 而守益於戒懼慎獨，蓋兢兢焉。

translations.literal: Shouyi, by contrast, in vigilance, fear, and careful solitude was ever watchful.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi, by contrast, lived in constant vigilance—wary, reverent, and scrupulous in solitude.

sentences.zh: 子善，嘉靖三十五年進士。

translations.literal: His son Shan passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shan became a jinshi in the thirty-fifth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 以刑部員外郎恤刑湖廣，矜釋甚眾。

translations.literal: As an Outer Section Secretary in the Ministry of Justice he conducted the mourning circuit in Huguang and released a great many prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: As an Outer Section Secretary in the Ministry of Justice, he carried out the autumn review in Huguang and showed mercy to a great many prisoners.

sentences.zh: 擢山東提學僉事，時與諸生講學。

translations.literal: Promoted to Assistant Commissioner of Education in Shandong, he lectured to the students of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Assistant Commissioner of Education in Shandong, he lectured regularly to the students there.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，累官廣東右布政使，謝病歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli he rose through offices to Right Administration Commissioner of Guangdong, then asked leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Wanli reign he rose to Right Administration Commissioner of Guangdong, then retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 久之，以薦即家授太常卿，致仕。

translations.literal: After a long while, on recommendation he was appointed from home as Minister of Ceremonies, then retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, on recommendation, he was appointed Minister of Ceremonies without leaving home, then formally retired.

sentences.zh: 子德涵、德溥。

translations.literal: His sons were Dehan and Debo.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Dehan and Debo.

sentences.zh: 德涵，字汝海，隆慶五年進士。

translations.literal: Dehan, courtesy name Ruhai, passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: Dehan, styled Ruhai, became a jinshi in the fifth year of Longqing.

sentences.zh: 歷刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He served as Outer Section Secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He served as an Outer Section Secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 張居正方禁講學，德涵守之自若。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng had just forbidden public lecturing, Dehan continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng first banned public lecturing, Dehan kept teaching just as he had.

sentences.zh: 御史傅應禎、劉臺相繼論居正，皆德涵裏人，疑為黨，出為河南僉事。

translations.literal: Censors Fu Yingqi and Liu Tai successively impeached Juzheng; both were fellow townsmen of Dehan, and he was suspected of faction, so he was sent out as Assistant Commissioner in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Fu Yingqi and Liu Tai impeached Zhang Juzheng in turn; both were Dehan's fellow townsmen, he was suspected of belonging to their faction, and was posted out as Assistant Commissioner in Henan.

sentences.zh: 御史承風指劾之，貶秩歸。

translations.literal: A censor, catching the prevailing wind, impeached him further, and he was demoted in rank and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Another censor, reading the mood of the court, piled on accusations, and Dehan was reduced in rank and sent home.

sentences.zh: 善服習父訓，踐履無怠，稱其家學。

translations.literal: Shan practiced his father's instruction without slackening and was praised for the learning handed down in the family.
translations.idiomatic: Shan lived by his father's teaching without slackening and was praised for sustaining the family's scholarly tradition.

sentences.zh: 而德涵從耿定理遊，定理不答。

translations.literal: Dehan studied under Geng Dingli, but Dingli would not take him as a disciple.
translations.idiomatic: Dehan sought instruction from Geng Dingli, but Dingli would not accept him.

sentences.zh: 發憤湛思，自覺有得，由是專以悟為宗，於祖父所傳，始一變矣。

translations.literal: Burning with resolve and plunging into deep thought, he felt he had gained understanding; from then on he made enlightenment his sole aim, and what he had received from his grandfather and father changed for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: Stung to resolve and plunged into hard thinking, he came to feel he had grasped something; from then on he made sudden awakening his sole standard, and for the first time broke with what his grandfather and father had handed down.

sentences.zh: 德溥，由萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: Debo passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Debo became a jinshi in the eleventh year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 歷司經局洗馬。

translations.literal: He served as Reader in the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Reader in the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 善從子德泳，萬歷十四年進士。

translations.literal: Shan's nephew De Yong passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Shan's nephew De Yong became a jinshi in the fourteenth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 官御史。

translations.literal: He served as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a censor.

sentences.zh: 給事中李獻可請預教太子，斥為民。

translations.literal: The supervising secretary Li Xianké requested that the crown prince be given preliminary instruction in advance and was dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Li Xianké petitioned for the crown prince to receive instruction in advance and was stripped of office and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 德泳偕同官救之，亦削籍。

translations.literal: De Yong joined his fellow officials in pleading for him and was likewise struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: De Yong joined his colleagues in defending Li and was stripped of office and removed from the register as well.

sentences.zh: 家居三十年，言者交薦。
