translations.literal: He lived at home for thirty years, and memorialists repeatedly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: He remained at home for thirty years, while censors and officials one after another recommended him for recall.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，起尚寶少卿，歷太常卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong acceded, he was recalled as Vice Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Treasures and rose to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong took the throne, he was recalled as Vice Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Treasures and eventually rose to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢用事，乞休歸。

translations.literal: When Wei Zhongxian held power, he requested retirement and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wei Zhongxian came to power, he asked to retire and went home.

sentences.zh: 所司將為忠賢建祠，德泳塗毀其募籍，乃止。

translations.literal: The relevant office was about to build a shrine for Wei Zhongxian; De Yong smeared over its donation register, and only then was it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the authorities were about to erect a shrine to Wei Zhongxian, De Yong defaced its subscription register, and the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 錢德洪，名寬，字德洪，後以字行，改字洪甫，余姚人。

translations.literal: Qian Dehong, personal name Kuan, courtesy name Dehong, later known by that name, later changed his courtesy name to Hongfu, was a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Dehong—born Kuan, courtesy name Dehong, later known by that name and then as Hongfu—was from Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 王守仁自尚書歸裏，德洪偕數十人共學焉。

translations.literal: When Wang Shouren returned from the Ministry to his home district, Dehong joined several dozen others in studying under him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shouren came home from the Ministry of War, Dehong was among several dozen who gathered to study with him.

sentences.zh: 四方士踵至，德洪與王畿先為疏通其大旨，而後卒業於守仁。

translations.literal: Scholars from the four quarters came in succession; Dehong and Wang Ji first helped clarify the main outlines, and afterward completed their studies under Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars from every quarter soon followed; Dehong and Wang Ji first helped open the great themes of the teaching, then finished their training under Shouren himself.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年舉會試，徑歸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiajing he passed the metropolitan examination and went straight home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiajing he passed the metropolitan examination and returned home without waiting for the palace audience.

sentences.zh: 七年冬，偕畿赴廷試，聞守仁訃，乃奔喪至貴溪。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventh year he and Ji went to the palace examination; hearing of Shouren's death, he rushed to the funeral at Guixi.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventh year he and Ji went up for the palace examination; on hearing that Shouren had died, he hurried to Guixi for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 議喪服，德洪曰：「某有親在，麻衣布绖弗敢有加焉。

translations.literal: When they discussed mourning dress, Dehong said: "I have a living parent; I do not dare wear more than hemp garments and a hemp sash."
translations.idiomatic: When they debated mourning dress, Dehong said, "I still have a parent living—I dare not wear more than plain hemp and a mourning sash."

sentences.zh: 」畿曰：「我無親。

translations.literal: Ji said: "I have no living parent."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "I have no parent left alive."

sentences.zh: 」遂服斬衰。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wore the severest mourning.
translations.idiomatic: So he put on the full mourning of a bereaved son.

sentences.zh: 喪歸，德洪與畿築室於場，以終心喪。

translations.literal: After the funeral he returned home; Dehong and Ji built a hut at the graveside to complete their heart-mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When the funeral was over and they had returned home, Dehong and Ji built a hut at the burial ground to fulfill their heart-mourning.

sentences.zh: 十一年始成進士。

translations.literal: Not until the eleventh year did he finally attain jinshi rank.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the eleventh year did he at last complete his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 累官刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He rose through office to Director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 郭勛下詔獄，移部定罪，德洪據獄詞論死。

translations.literal: When Guo Xun was imprisoned in the imperial prison and the case was transferred to the Ministry for sentencing, Dehong, relying on the confession, argued for the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Xun was held in the imperial prison and the case was sent to the Ministry of Punishments for judgment, Dehong, going by the prison confession, argued that he should die.

sentences.zh: 廷臣欲坐以不軌，言德洪不習刑名。

translations.literal: Court officials wished to charge him with treason, saying Dehong was not versed in penal law.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials wanted to convict Guo of treason, but objected that Dehong was no expert in penal matters.

sentences.zh: 而帝雅不欲勛死，因言官疏，下德洪詔獄。

translations.literal: Yet the Emperor had never wished Guo Xun to die; on the strength of a censor's memorial, he sent Dehong to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, however, had no wish to see Guo Xun die; acting on a censor's memorial, he sent Dehong to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 所司上其罪，已出獄矣。

translations.literal: The office submitted his crimes, but he had already been released from prison.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities reported his offenses, yet by then he had already been released.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「始朕命刑官毋梏勛，德洪故違之，與勛不領敕何異。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "At first I ordered the penal officials not to shackle Guo Xun; Dehong deliberately disobeyed—how is that different from Guo's not receiving the edict?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I had first ordered the penal officials not to shackle Guo Xun, yet Dehong deliberately defied me—how is that different from Guo's refusing to accept the edict?"

sentences.zh: 」再下獄。

translations.literal: He was sent to prison again.
translations.idiomatic: Dehong was thrown back into prison.

sentences.zh: 御史楊爵、都督趙卿亦在系，德洪與講《易》不輟。

translations.literal: Censor Yang Jue and Regional Commander Zhao Qing were also imprisoned; Dehong continued lecturing on 《Changes》 with them without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yang Jue and Regional Commander Zhao Qing were imprisoned as well, and Dehong kept lecturing on the 《Classic of Changes》 with them without pause.

sentences.zh: 久之，斥為民。

translations.literal: After a long while he was dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: After a long imprisonment he was dismissed and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 德洪既廢，遂周遊四方，講良知學。

translations.literal: Once Dehong was disgraced, he traveled throughout the four quarters lecturing on the learning of innate knowing.
translations.idiomatic: Once disgraced, Dehong wandered the realm lecturing on the doctrine of innate knowing.

sentences.zh: 時士大夫率務講學為名高，而德洪、畿以守仁高第弟子，尤為人所宗。

translations.literal: At the time literati mostly pursued lecturing for the sake of reputation, but Dehong and Ji, as Shouren's leading disciples, were especially revered.
translations.idiomatic: In those days scholars mostly lectured to burnish their names, yet Dehong and Ji—as Shouren's foremost disciples—were revered above all others.

sentences.zh: 德洪徹悟不如畿，畿持循亦不如德洪，然畿竟入於禪，而德洪猶不失儒者矩矱雲。

translations.literal: Dehong's thorough enlightenment was not equal to Ji's, nor was Ji's steadfast adherence equal to Dehong's; yet Ji in the end drifted into Chan, while Dehong still did not depart from the Confucian measure.
translations.idiomatic: Dehong's sudden insight did not match Ji's, nor did Ji's steady discipline match Dehong's; yet Ji in the end slipped into Chan, while Dehong never lost the Confucian rule.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，復官，進階朝列大夫，致仕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong acceded, he was restored to office, advanced to Grand Master of the Court for Official Reception, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Dehong was restored to office, promoted to Grand Master of the Court for Official Reception, and then retired.

sentences.zh: 神宗嗣位，復進一階。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong succeeded, he was advanced one further rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong succeeded, he was given one further promotion in rank.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十九。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 學者稱緒山先生。

translations.literal: Scholars called him Master Xushan.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars honored him as Master Xushan.

sentences.zh: 初，守仁倡道其鄉，鄰境從遊者甚眾，德洪、畿為之首。

translations.literal: At first, when Shouren pioneered the Way in his home district, many from neighboring regions followed him to study; Dehong and Ji were their leaders.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouren first began to teach the Way in his own country, students from neighboring districts flocked to him in great numbers, with Dehong and Ji at their head.

sentences.zh: 其最初受業者，則有余姚徐愛，山陰蔡宗袞、朱節及應良、盧可久、應典、董涷之屬。

translations.literal: Among the very first to receive instruction were Xu Ai of Yuyao, Cai Zongdu and Zhu Jie of Shanyin, along with Ying Liang, Lu Kejiu, Ying Dian, and Dong Dong, among others.
translations.idiomatic: The earliest to take instruction included Xu Ai of Yuyao; Cai Zongdu and Zhu Jie of Shanyin; and Ying Liang, Lu Kejiu, Ying Dian, Dong Dong, and the like.

sentences.zh: 愛，字曰仁，守仁女弟夫也。

translations.literal: Ai, courtesy name Yueren, was Shouren's brother-in-law through his younger sister.
translations.idiomatic: Ai, styled Yueren, was married to Shouren's younger sister.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 官至南京工部郎中。

translations.literal: He rose to Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 良知之說，學者初多未信，愛為疏通辨析，暢其指要。

translations.literal: At first many scholars did not trust the doctrine of innate knowing; Ai clarified and analyzed it, setting forth its essentials.
translations.idiomatic: At first many scholars did not accept the teaching of innate knowing; Ai clarified and argued its points until its essentials stood plain.

sentences.zh: 守仁言：「徐生之溫恭，蔡生之沈潛，朱生之明敏，皆我所不逮。

translations.literal: Shouren said: "Xu's gentleness and reverence, Cai's depth and reserve, and Zhu's clarity and quickness—all surpass what I can do."
translations.idiomatic: Shouren said, "Xu's warmth and courtesy, Cai's depth and quiet strength, Zhu's bright quickness—each is beyond me."

sentences.zh: 」愛卒，年三十一，守仁哭之慟。

translations.literal: When Ai died at the age of thirty-one, Shouren wept for him in deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: When Ai died at thirty-one, Shouren mourned him with anguished weeping.

sentences.zh: 一日講畢，嘆曰：「安得起曰仁九泉聞斯言乎！

translations.literal: One day, after finishing a lecture, he sighed: "If only Yueren could rise from the nine springs to hear these words!"
translations.idiomatic: One day, when a lecture was done, he sighed, "If only Yueren could rise from the underworld and hear this!"

sentences.zh: 」率門人之其墓所，酹酒告之。

translations.literal: He led his disciples to Ai's grave to pour a libation and tell him of it.
translations.idiomatic: He took his disciples to Ai's tomb, poured wine in offering, and told him what he had said.

sentences.zh: 蔡宗袞，字希淵。

translations.literal: Cai Zongdu, courtesy name Xiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Zongdu, styled Xiyuan.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the twelfth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the twelfth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 官至四川提學僉事。

translations.literal: He rose to Educational Intendant in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Educational Intendant in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 朱節，字守中。

translations.literal: Zhu Jie, courtesy name Shouzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jie, styled Shouzhong.

sentences.zh: 正德八年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the eighth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the eighth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 為御史，巡按山東。

translations.literal: He served as censor, conducting inspections in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a censor on inspection tour in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 大盜起顏神鎮，蔓州縣十數。

translations.literal: A great bandit rose at Yanshen Town and spread through more than ten prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: A great outlaw rose at Yanshen Town and spread through a dozen or more prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 驅馳戎馬間，以勞卒。

translations.literal: He rushed about among the horses of war and died of exhaustion from the strain.
translations.idiomatic: He dashed back and forth in the saddle until exhaustion from the campaign killed him.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Vice Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously made Vice Commissioner of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 應良，字原忠，仙居人。

translations.literal: Ying Liang, courtesy name Yuanzhong, a native of Xianju.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Liang, styled Yuanzhong, was from Xianju.

sentences.zh: 正德六年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the sixth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the sixth year of Zhengde.

sentences.zh: 官編修。

translations.literal: He served as Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 守仁在吏部，良學焉。

translations.literal: When Shouren was in the Ministry of Personnel, Liang studied under him.
translations.idiomatic: While Shouren was at the Ministry of Personnel, Liang became his pupil.

sentences.zh: 親老歸養，講學山中者將十年。

translations.literal: When his parents grew old he returned to support them and lectured in the mountains for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents aged, he went home to care for them and lectured in the hills for nearly ten years.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，還任，伏闕爭大禮，廷杖。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing he resumed office, prostrated himself before the palace gate to oppose the Great Rites, and was beaten at court.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Jiajing he returned to office, knelt before the palace gate to protest the Great Rites, and was beaten in court.

sentences.zh: 張總黜翰林為外官，良得山西副使，謝病歸，卒。

translations.literal: When Zhang Cong demoted Hanlin scholars to external posts, Liang was assigned Vice Commissioner in Shanxi; he claimed illness and returned home, then died.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cong drove Hanlin scholars out to provincial posts, Liang was made Vice Commissioner in Shanxi; he pleaded illness, went home, and died there.

sentences.zh: 盧可久，字一松。

translations.literal: Lu Kejiu, courtesy name Yisong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kejiu, styled Yisong.

sentences.zh: 程粹，字養之。

translations.literal: Cheng Cui, courtesy name Yangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Cui, styled Yangzhi.

sentences.zh: 皆永康諸生。

translations.literal: Both were provincial graduates of Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: Both were licentiates of Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 與同邑應典，皆師守仁。

translations.literal: Together with their fellow townsman Ying Dian, both took Shouren as their teacher.
translations.idiomatic: They and their fellow townsman Ying Dian all studied under Shouren.

sentences.zh: 粹子正誼，歷順天府尹。

translations.literal: Cui's son Zhengyi rose to become Prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Cui's son Zhengyi rose to Prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 應典，字天彜。

translations.literal: Ying Dian, courtesy name Tianyi.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Dian, styled Tianyi.

sentences.zh: 進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He was a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 官兵部主事。

translations.literal: He served as Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 居家養母，不希榮利。

translations.literal: At home he supported his mother and did not covet glory or profit.
translations.idiomatic: At home he cared for his mother and never sought rank or gain.

sentences.zh: 通籍三十年，在官止一考。

translations.literal: Though on the rolls for thirty years, he served in office for only one evaluation period.
translations.idiomatic: Though registered for office for thirty years, he actually served for only one term of evaluation.

sentences.zh: 可久傳東陽杜惟熙，惟熙傳同邑陳時芳、陳正道。

translations.literal: Kejiu transmitted the teaching to Du Weixi of Dongyang; Weixi transmitted it to Chen Shifang and Chen Zhengdao, fellow townsfolk.
translations.idiomatic: Kejiu's line passed to Du Weixi of Dongyang, and Weixi's to his fellow townsman Chen Shifang and Chen Zhengdao.

sentences.zh: 惟熙以克己為要，嘗言：「學者一息不昧，則萬古皆通；

translations.literal: Weixi took self-restraint as essential and once said: "If a scholar for not one breath loses clear awareness, then all ages are open to him;"
translations.idiomatic: Weixi made self-restraint the heart of learning and once said, "Let the scholar keep every breath clear, and all ages lie open to him;"

sentences.zh: 一刻少寬，即終朝欠缺。

translations.literal: "let one moment ease, and from morning till evening one falls short."
translations.idiomatic: "let one moment slacken, and the whole day is lost."

sentences.zh: 」卒年八十余。

translations.literal: He died at over eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his eighties.

sentences.zh: 時芳博覽多聞，而歸於實踐。

translations.literal: Shifang was broadly read and learned, yet returned everything to practical cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Shifang read widely and knew much, yet brought it all back to practice.

sentences.zh: 歲貢不仕。

translations.literal: Recommended as tribute student, he never took office.
translations.idiomatic: Though recommended as a tribute student, he never entered office.

sentences.zh: 正道為建安訓導，年八十余，猶徒步赴五峰講會。

translations.literal: Zhengdao served as Instructor of Jian'an; though past eighty, he still walked on foot to the Wufeng lecture assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengdao served as Instructor at Jian'an; even past eighty he still walked on foot to the Wufeng lecture meetings.

sentences.zh: 其門人呂一龍，永康人，言動不茍，學者鹹宗之。

translations.literal: His disciple Lu Yilong of Yongkang was exact in word and deed; scholars all looked to him as a model.
translations.idiomatic: His disciple Lu Yilong of Yongkang was scrupulous in speech and conduct, and scholars everywhere looked to him as a model.

sentences.zh: 董涷，字子壽，海寧人。

translations.literal: Dong Dong, courtesy name Zishou, a native of Haining.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Dong, styled Zishou, was from Haining.

sentences.zh: 年六十八矣，遊會稽，肩瓢笠詩卷謁守仁，卒請為弟子。

translations.literal: At sixty-eight he traveled to Kuaiji, shouldering a gourd, a bamboo hat, and a bundle of poems to pay his respects to Shouren, and in the end asked to become his disciple.
translations.idiomatic: At sixty-eight he journeyed to Kuaiji with a gourd, bamboo hat, and roll of poems on his shoulder to call on Shouren, and in the end begged to become his disciple.

sentences.zh: 子谷，官知縣，亦受業守仁。

translations.literal: His son Gu served as magistrate and also received instruction from Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gu served as a county magistrate and also studied under Shouren.

sentences.zh: 王畿，字汝中，山陰人。

translations.literal: Wang Ji, courtesy name Ruzhong, a native of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, styled Ruzhong, was from Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉於鄉，跌宕自喜。

translations.literal: In his youth he passed the provincial examination and lived freely, pleased with himself.
translations.idiomatic: While still young he passed the provincial examination and lived with a free, self-satisfied air.

sentences.zh: 後受業王守仁，聞其言，無底滯，守仁大喜。

translations.literal: Later he received instruction from Wang Shouren; hearing his words he found no obstruction within, and Shouren was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Later he studied under Wang Shouren; hearing his teaching he felt no inner blockage, and Shouren was delighted.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年舉進士，與錢德洪並不就廷對歸。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination; he and Qian Dehong both skipped the palace audience and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiajing he passed the jinshi examination; he and Qian Dehong both declined the palace audience and went home.

sentences.zh: 守仁征思、田，留畿、德洪主書院。

translations.literal: When Shouren campaigned against the Si and Tian rebels, he left Ji and Dehong in charge of the academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouren marched against the rebels in Si and Tian, he left Ji and Dehong to run the academy.

sentences.zh: 已，奔守仁喪，經紀葬事，持心喪三年。

translations.literal: Not long after, they rushed to Shouren's funeral, managed the burial arrangements, and observed heart-mourning for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they hurried to Shouren's funeral, saw to the burial, and kept heart-mourning for three years.

sentences.zh: 久之，與德洪同第進士。

translations.literal: After a long interval he and Dehong both finally attained jinshi rank on the same round.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he and Dehong at last completed their jinshi degrees in the same round of examinations.

sentences.zh: 授南京兵部主事，進郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War and promoted to Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War and later promoted to Director.

sentences.zh: 給事中戚賢等薦畿。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Qi Xian and others recommended Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Qi Xian and others recommended Ji for office.

sentences.zh: 夏言斥畿偽學，奪賢職，畿乃謝病歸。

translations.literal: Xia Yan denounced Ji for false learning, stripped Qi Xian of his post, and Ji then claimed illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yan attacked Ji as a peddler of false learning, stripped Qi Xian of his post, and Ji then pleaded illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 畿嘗云：「學當致知見性而已，應事有小過不足累。

translations.literal: Ji once said: "Learning ought to be nothing more than extending knowledge and seeing one's nature; small faults in handling affairs should not count against one."
translations.idiomatic: Ji once said, "Learning is only a matter of extending knowledge and seeing one's nature; minor slips in daily affairs should not weigh against a man."

sentences.zh: 」故在官弗免幹請，以不謹斥。

translations.literal: Therefore in office he could not avoid improper requests and was dismissed for lack of discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, in office he could not keep free of improper solicitations and was dismissed for indiscretion.

sentences.zh: 畿既廢，益務講學，足跡遍東南，吳、楚、閩、越皆有講舍，年八十余不肯已。

translations.literal: Once disgraced, Ji devoted himself even more to lecturing; his footsteps ranged across the southeast, and lecture halls appeared in Wu, Chu, Min, and Yue—past eighty he still would not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Once out of office, Ji threw himself still more into teaching; his steps ranged across the southeast, and lecture halls sprang up in Wu, Chu, Min, and Yue—past eighty, he still would not rest.

sentences.zh: 善談說，能動人，所至聽者雲集。

translations.literal: He was skilled at discourse and could stir people's hearts; wherever he went hearers gathered like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: He was a gifted speaker who could move men's hearts; wherever he went, listeners gathered like clouds.

sentences.zh: 每講，雜以禪機，亦不自諱也。

translations.literal: In every lecture he mixed in Chan Buddhist turns of thought and did not conceal it.
translations.idiomatic: In every lecture he wove in Chan turns of phrase and made no secret of it.

sentences.zh: 學者稱龍溪先生。

translations.literal: Scholars called him Master Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars honored him as Master Longxi.

sentences.zh: 其後，士之浮誕不逞者，率自名龍溪弟子。

translations.literal: Afterward, flippant and unrestrained men mostly styled themselves disciples of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: After him, frivolous and unbridled men mostly called themselves disciples of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 而泰州王艮亦受業守仁，門徒之盛，與畿相埒，學者稱心齋先生。

translations.literal: Wang Gen of Taizhou also received instruction from Shouren; his disciples were as numerous as Ji's, and scholars called him Master Xinzhai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gen of Taizhou also studied under Shouren; his following was as great as Ji's, and scholars honored him as Master Xinzhai.

sentences.zh: 陽明學派，以龍溪、心齋為得其宗。

translations.literal: Within the Yangming school, Longxi and Xinzhai were regarded as having inherited the true lineage.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yangming school, Longxi and Xinzhai were held to have received the true transmission.

sentences.zh: 艮，字汝止。

translations.literal: Gen, courtesy name Ruzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Gen, styled Ruzhi.

sentences.zh: 初名銀，王守仁為更名。

translations.literal: Originally named Yin; Wang Shouren changed his name for him.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Yin; Wang Shouren gave him a new one.

sentences.zh: 七歲受書鄉塾，貧不能竟學。

translations.literal: At seven he began studying at the village school but was too poor to finish his education.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he began reading in the village school, but poverty kept him from finishing his studies.

sentences.zh: 父竈丁，冬晨犯寒，役於官。

translations.literal: His father was a kitchen conscript; on winter mornings braving the cold he labored for the government.
translations.idiomatic: His father served as a kitchen conscript, braving the winter cold each morning on corvée for the government.

sentences.zh: 艮哭曰：「為人子，令父至此，得為人乎！

translations.literal: Gen wept and said: "As a son, to have brought my father to this—can I still be called human!
translations.idiomatic: Gen wept and said, "As a son, to have brought my father to this—what kind of human being am I!

sentences.zh: 」出代父役，入定省，惟謹。

translations.literal: " He went out to replace his father in corvée, and when he returned home for morning and evening attendance to his parents, he was ever dutiful.
translations.idiomatic: " He went out to take his father's place in corvée, and whenever he came home to pay his respects morning and evening, he was unfailingly careful.

sentences.zh: 艮讀書，止《孝經》、《論語》、《大學》，信口談說，中理解。

translations.literal: Gen studied books, reading only the 《Classic of Filial Piety》, the 《Analects》, and the 《Great Learning》; speaking extemporaneously, he grasped the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Gen read only the 《Classic of Filial Piety》, the 《Analects》, and the 《Great Learning》, yet could speak extemporaneously and hit the meaning every time.

sentences.zh: 有客聞艮言，詫言：「何類王中丞語。

translations.literal: A guest who heard Gen speak exclaimed in wonder: "How like the words of Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang!
translations.idiomatic: A guest who heard Gen speak cried out in astonishment, "How like the words of Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang!

sentences.zh: 」艮乃謁守仁江西，與守仁辨久之，大服，拜為弟子。

translations.literal: " Gen thereupon visited Shouren in Jiangxi, debated with him at length, and was deeply convinced; he bowed and became Shouren's disciple.
translations.idiomatic: " Gen thereupon went to visit Shouren in Jiangxi, debated with him at length, and was utterly won over; he bowed and became his disciple.

sentences.zh: 明日告之悔，復就賓位自如。

translations.literal: The next day he told Shouren he regretted it and returned to the seat of a guest as before.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he told Shouren he had changed his mind and resumed his place among the guests as if nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 已，心折，卒稱弟子。

translations.literal: Before long his heart was won over, and at last he acknowledged himself a disciple.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his heart was won over, and in the end he acknowledged himself a disciple.

sentences.zh: 從守仁歸裏，嘆曰：「吾師倡明絕學，何風之不廣也！

translations.literal: Returning home with Shouren, he sighed and said: "My teacher has advocated and clarified the supreme learning—why does this teaching not spread more widely!
translations.idiomatic: On returning home with Shouren, he sighed and said, "My teacher has revived and clarified the supreme learning—why does this teaching not spread everywhere!

sentences.zh: 」還家，制小車北上，所過招要人士，告以守仁之道，人聚觀者千百。

translations.literal: " Back home, he built a small cart and traveled north; wherever he passed he invited and gathered men of stature, telling them Shouren's Way, and crowds of hundreds gathered to watch.
translations.idiomatic: " Back home he built a small cart and traveled north; wherever he passed he invited and gathered men of note, preaching Shouren's Way, and crowds of hundreds gathered to watch.

sentences.zh: 抵京師，同門生駭異，匿其車，趣使返。

translations.literal: Reaching the capital, fellow disciples were astonished and alarmed; they hid his cart and urged him to return.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the capital, his fellow disciples were shocked and alarmed; they hid his cart and pressed him to go back.

sentences.zh: 守仁聞之，不悅。

translations.literal: When Shouren heard of this, he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouren heard of it, he was displeased.

sentences.zh: 艮往謁，拒不見，長跪謝過乃已。

translations.literal: Gen went to pay a visit, but Shouren refused to see him; only after Gen knelt for a long time to apologize for his fault did Shouren relent.
translations.idiomatic: Gen went to call on him, but Shouren refused to receive him; only after Gen knelt for a long time to beg forgiveness did Shouren let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 王氏弟子遍天下，率都爵位有氣勢。

translations.literal: Disciples of the Wang school were spread across the land, and for the most part all held noble ranks and an imposing presence.
translations.idiomatic: Disciples of the Wang school were spread across the land, and for the most part all held noble titles and an imposing air.

sentences.zh: 艮以布衣抗其間，聲名反出諸弟子上。

translations.literal: Gen, in plain cloth, stood among them, yet his fame in fact surpassed that of the other disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Gen, a man in plain cloth, stood among them, yet his renown in fact surpassed that of the other disciples.

sentences.zh: 然艮本狂士，往往駕師說上之，持論益高遠，出入於二氏。

translations.literal: Yet Gen was by nature an unrestrained scholar; he often drove his master's teaching to extremes, his arguments growing ever more lofty and remote, drifting in and out of the two teachings of Daoism and Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gen was by nature a wild scholar; he often pushed his master's doctrine to extremes, his arguments growing ever loftier and more remote, drifting in and out of the two teachings of Daoism and Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 艮傳林春、徐樾，樾傳顏鈞，鈞傳羅汝芳、梁汝元，汝芳傳楊起元、周汝登、蔡悉。

translations.literal: Gen transmitted the teaching to Lin Chun and Xu Yue; Yue transmitted it to Yan Jun; Jun transmitted it to Luo Rufang and Liang Ruyuan; Rufang transmitted it to Yang Qiyuan, Zhou Rudeng, and Cai Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Gen passed the teaching to Lin Chun and Xu Yue; Yue passed it to Yan Jun; Jun passed it to Luo Rufang and Liang Ruyuan; and Rufang passed it to Yang Qiyuan, Zhou Rudeng, and Cai Xi.

sentences.zh: 樾，字子直，貴溪人。

translations.literal: Yue, courtesy name Zizhi, was a native of Guixi.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, styled Zizhi, was a native of Guixi.

sentences.zh: 舉進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 歷官雲南左布政使。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Left Administration Commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through office to Left Administration Commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 元江土酋那鑒反，詐降。

translations.literal: Na Jian, a tribal chieftain of Yuanjiang, rebelled and feigned surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Na Jian, a tribal chieftain of Yuanjiang, rebelled and feigned surrender.

sentences.zh: 樾信之，抵其城下，死焉。

translations.literal: Yue believed him, drew up to his city walls, and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Yue believed him, advanced to the foot of his walls, and was killed there.

sentences.zh: 詔贈光祿寺卿，予祭葬，任一子官。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, granted sacrificial rites and burial, and appointed one son to office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, granted him sacrificial rites and burial, and appointed one son to office.

sentences.zh: 春，字子仁，泰州人。

translations.literal: Chun, courtesy name Ziren, was a native of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chun, styled Ziren, was a native of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 聞良知之學，日以朱墨筆識臧否自考，動有繩檢，尺寸不逾。

translations.literal: When he heard the learning of innate knowing, each day he used red and black ink to mark right and wrong and examine himself; in every move he held to the measure, never overstepping by so much as an inch.
translations.idiomatic: When he encountered the learning of innate knowing, each day he used red and black ink to mark right and wrong and examine himself; in every act he held to the rule, never overstepping by a fraction.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年會試第一，除戶部主事，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Jiajing he placed first in the metropolitan examination; he was appointed a Director in the Ministry of Revenue and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Jiajing he ranked first in the metropolitan examination; he was appointed a Director in the Ministry of Revenue and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 縉紳士講學京師者數十人，聰明解悟善談說者，推王畿，誌行敦實推春及羅洪先。

translations.literal: Several dozen gentry and scholars lectured in the capital; for quick wits who understood well and spoke fluently, Wang Ji was chiefly praised, while for steadfast conduct Lin Chun and Luo Hongxian were chiefly praised.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen gentry and scholars lectured in the capital; for quick wits who grasped things readily and spoke well, Wang Ji was chiefly praised, while for steadfast conduct Lin Chun and Luo Hongxian were chiefly praised.

sentences.zh: 進文選郎中，卒官，年四十四。

translations.literal: He rose to Director of the Bureau of Civil Appointments and died in office at the age of forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director of the Bureau of Civil Appointments and died in office at forty-four.

sentences.zh: 發其篋，僅白金四兩，僚友棺斂歸其喪。

translations.literal: When his chest was opened, there was only four taels of silver; colleagues and friends provided a coffin and escorted his body home.
translations.idiomatic: When his chest was opened, there were only four taels of silver; colleagues and friends provided a coffin and escorted his body home.

sentences.zh: 汝芳，字維德，南城人。

translations.literal: Rufang, courtesy name Weide, was a native of Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Rufang, styled Weide, was a native of Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-second year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-second year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 除太湖知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed Magistrate of Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Magistrate of Taihu.

sentences.zh: 召諸生論學，公事多決於講座。

translations.literal: He summoned students to discuss learning, and many official matters were decided at the lecture hall.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned students to discuss learning, and many official matters were decided at the lecture hall.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部主事，歷寧國知府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a Director in the Ministry of Justice and later served as Prefect of Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to be a Director in the Ministry of Justice and later served as Prefect of Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 民兄弟爭產，汝芳對之泣，民亦泣，訟乃已。

translations.literal: When brothers among the people quarreled over property, Rufang wept before them; the people wept too, and the lawsuit ended.
translations.idiomatic: When brothers among the people quarreled over property, Rufang wept before them; the people wept as well, and the lawsuit ended.

sentences.zh: 創開元會，罪囚亦令聽講。

translations.literal: He founded the Kaiyuan Assembly, and even condemned prisoners were allowed to listen to the lectures.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the Kaiyuan Assembly, and even condemned prisoners were allowed to listen to the lectures.

sentences.zh: 入覲，勸徐階聚四方計吏講學。

translations.literal: When he came to court for an audience, he urged Xu Jie to gather accounting officials from the four quarters for lectures on learning.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to court for an audience, he urged Xu Jie to gather accounting officials from the four quarters for lectures on learning.

sentences.zh: 階遂大會於靈濟宮，聽者數千人。

translations.literal: Xu Jie then held a great assembly at the Lingji Palace, and several thousand people came to listen.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jie then held a great assembly at the Lingji Palace, and several thousand people came to listen.

sentences.zh: 父艱，服闋，起補東昌，移雲南屯田副使，進參政，分守永昌，坐事為言官論罷。

translations.literal: When his father died he observed mourning; when mourning ended he was recalled to serve at Dongchang, then moved to be Vice Commissioner of Military Colonies in Yunnan, promoted to Administration Commissioner, and assigned to guard Yongchang; he was dismissed after censorial officials impeached him over an affair.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he observed mourning; when mourning ended he was recalled to serve at Dongchang, then moved to be Vice Commissioner of Military Colonies in Yunnan, promoted to Administration Commissioner, and assigned to guard Yongchang; he was dismissed after censorial officials impeached him over an affair.

sentences.zh: 初，汝芳從永新顏鈞講學，後鈞系南京獄當死，汝芳供養獄中，鬻產救之，得減戍。

translations.literal: Earlier, Rufang had studied under Yan Jun of Yongxin; later Jun was imprisoned in Nanjing and faced death, and Rufang supported him in prison, sold property to rescue him, and obtained a commuted sentence of frontier guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Rufang had studied under Yan Jun of Yongxin; later Jun was imprisoned in Nanjing and faced death, and Rufang supported him in prison, sold property to rescue him, and obtained a commuted sentence of frontier guard duty.

sentences.zh: 汝芳既罷官，鈞亦赦歸。

translations.literal: After Rufang was dismissed from office, Jun was also pardoned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After Rufang was dismissed from office, Jun was also pardoned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 汝芳事之，飲食必躬進，人以為難。

translations.literal: Rufang served him; food and drink he always presented in person—a thing people found hard to do.
translations.idiomatic: Rufang served him, always presenting food and drink in person—a thing people found hard to do.

sentences.zh: 鈞詭怪猖狂，其學歸釋氏，故汝芳之學亦近釋。

translations.literal: Jun was eccentric, strange, and wildly unrestrained; his learning returned to Buddhism, and so Rufang's learning also drew near to Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was eccentric, strange, and wildly unrestrained; his learning returned to Buddhism, and so Rufang's learning also drew near to Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 楊起元、周汝登，皆萬歷五年進士。

translations.literal: Yang Qiyuan and Zhou Rudeng both passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qiyuan and Zhou Rudeng both passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 起元，歸善人。

translations.literal: Qiyuan was a native of Guishan.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyuan was a native of Guishan.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，適汝芳以參政入賀，遂學焉。

translations.literal: Selected as a Hanlin Bachelor, he happened to study under Rufang when Rufang entered the capital as Administration Commissioner to offer congratulations, and so he became his pupil.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a Hanlin Bachelor, he happened to study under Rufang when Rufang entered the capital as Administration Commissioner to offer congratulations, and so became his pupil.

sentences.zh: 張居正方惡講學，汝芳被劾罷，而起元自如，累官吏部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng was then hostile to lecture gatherings; Rufang was impeached and dismissed, but Qiyuan went on as before and rose in office to Left Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng was then hostile to lecture gatherings; Rufang was impeached and dismissed, but Qiyuan went on as before and rose in office to Left Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 拾遺被劾，帝不問。

translations.literal: When he submitted a memorial of remonstrance he was impeached, but the Emperor did not inquire into it.
translations.idiomatic: When he submitted a memorial of remonstrance he was impeached, but the Emperor did not pursue the matter.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追謚文懿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was posthumously granted the title Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianqi he was posthumously granted the title Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 汝登，嵊人。

translations.literal: Rudeng was a native of Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Rudeng was a native of Sheng.

sentences.zh: 初為南京工部主事，榷稅不如額，謫兩淮鹽運判官，累官南京尚寶卿。

translations.literal: At first he served as a Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Works; because tax collection fell short of quota he was demoted to Salt Transport Judge of the Two Huai circuits, and rose in office to become Nanjing Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as a Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Works; because tax collection fell short of quota he was demoted to Salt Transport Judge of the Two Huai circuits, and rose in office to Nanjing Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 起元清修誇節，然其學不諱禪。

translations.literal: Qiyuan was pure in conduct and prided himself on integrity, yet his learning did not shrink from Chan Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyuan was pure in conduct and prided himself on integrity, yet his learning did not shrink from Chan Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 汝登更欲合儒釋而會通之，輯《聖學宗傳》，盡采先儒語類禪者以入。

translations.literal: Rudeng wished even more to unite Confucianism and Buddhism and harmonize them; he compiled the 《Lineage of the Sage Learning》, gathering in every utterance of earlier Confucians that resembled Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Rudeng wished even more to unite Confucianism and Buddhism and harmonize them; he compiled the 《Lineage of the Sage Learning》, gathering in every utterance of earlier Confucians that resembled Chan.

sentences.zh: 蓋萬歷世士大夫講學者，多類此。

translations.literal: Thus among scholar-officials who lectured in the Wanli era, many were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: Thus among scholar-officials who lectured in the Wanli era, many were of this sort.

sentences.zh: 蔡悉，字士備，合肥人。

translations.literal: Xi, courtesy name Shibei, was a native of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, styled Shibei, was a native of Hefei.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 授常德推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Push Officer of Changde.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Push Officer of Changde.

sentences.zh: 築郭外六堤以免水患。

translations.literal: He built six dikes outside the city wall to avert flooding.
translations.idiomatic: He built six dikes outside the city wall to avert flooding.

sentences.zh: 擢南京吏部主事，累官南京尚寶卿，移署國子監。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, rose in office to Nanjing Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and was transferred to serve concurrently at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, rose in office to Nanjing Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and was transferred to serve concurrently at the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 嘗請立東宮，又極論礦稅之害。

translations.literal: He once petitioned to establish the Eastern Palace and also spoke forcefully against the harm of mining taxes.
translations.idiomatic: He once petitioned to establish the Eastern Palace and also spoke forcefully against the harm of mining taxes.

sentences.zh: 有學行，恬宦情。

translations.literal: He had learning and conduct, and was indifferent to office and emolument.
translations.idiomatic: He had learning and conduct, and was indifferent to office and emolument.

sentences.zh: 仕五十年，家食強半。

translations.literal: In fifty years of service, half his life was lived at home without salary.
translations.idiomatic: In fifty years of service, half his life was lived at home without salary.

sentences.zh: 清操亮節，淮西人宗之。

translations.literal: With pure integrity and bright principles, people west of the Huai looked to him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: With pure integrity and bright principles, people west of the Huai looked to him as their model.

sentences.zh: 歐陽德，字崇一，泰和人。

translations.literal: Ouyang De, courtesy name Chongyi, was a native of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang De, styled Chongyi, was a native of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 甫冠舉鄉試。

translations.literal: While still in his teens he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: While still in his teens he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 之贛州，從王守仁學。

translations.literal: Going to Ganzhou, he studied under Wang Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: Going to Ganzhou, he studied under Wang Shouren.

sentences.zh: 不應會試者再。

translations.literal: Twice he declined to take the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he declined to take the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年策問陰詆守仁，德與魏良弼等直發師訓無所阿，竟登第。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing the palace examination's policy question covertly denigrated Shouren; De, with Wei Liangbi and others, straightforwardly expounded their master's teaching without any flattery, and in the end placed on the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiajing the palace examination's policy question covertly denigrated Shouren; De, with Wei Liangbi and others, straightforwardly expounded their master's teaching without any flattery, and in the end placed on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 除知六安州，建龍津書院，聚生徒論學。

translations.literal: He was appointed Prefect of Lu'an, built the Longjin Academy, and gathered students to discuss learning.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Prefect of Lu'an, built the Longjin Academy, and gathered students to discuss learning.

sentences.zh: 入為刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as an Associate Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as an Associate Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 六年詔簡朝士有學行者為翰林，乃改德編修。

translations.literal: In the sixth year an edict selected court scholars of learning and conduct for the Hanlin Academy, and De was changed to Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year an edict selected court scholars of learning and conduct for the Hanlin Academy, and De was changed to Compiler.

sentences.zh: 遷南京國子司業，作講亭，進諸生與四方學者論道其中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Nanjing Directorate of Education, built a lecture pavilion, and led students and scholars from the four quarters in discussing the Way there.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Nanjing Directorate of Education, built a lecture pavilion, and led students and scholars from the four quarters in discussing the Way there.

sentences.zh: 尋改南京尚寶卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Nanjing Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was changed to Nanjing Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 召為太仆少卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to be Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 以便養，復改南京鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: To facilitate supporting his parents, he was again changed to Nanjing Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: To facilitate supporting his parents, he was again changed to Nanjing Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 父憂，服闋，留養其母，與鄒守益、聶豹、羅洪先日講學。

translations.literal: When his father died he observed mourning; when mourning ended he stayed to support his mother, and daily lectured with Zou Shouyi, Nie Bao, and Luo Hongxian.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he observed mourning; when mourning ended he stayed to support his mother, and daily lectured with Zou Shouyi, Nie Bao, and Luo Hongxian.

sentences.zh: 以薦起故官。

translations.literal: On recommendation he was recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he was recalled to his former office.

sentences.zh: 累遷吏部左侍郎兼學士，掌詹事府。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Left Vice Minister of Personnel and Academician, directing the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Left Vice Minister of Personnel and Academician, directing the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，服未闋，即用為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When his mother died he returned home; before mourning had ended he was immediately appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he returned home; before mourning had ended he was immediately appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 喪畢之官，命直無逸殿。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete he took office and was ordered to attend at the Hall of No Dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning was complete he took office and was ordered to attend at the Hall of No Dissipation.

sentences.zh: 時儲位久虛，帝惑陶仲文「二龍不相見」之說，諱言建儲，德懇請。

translations.literal: At that time the heir apparent had long been vacant; the Emperor was misled by Tao Zhongwen's saying that "the two dragons must not meet," avoided speaking of establishing an heir, and De earnestly petitioned.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the heir apparent had long been vacant; the Emperor was misled by Tao Zhongwen's saying that "the two dragons must not meet," avoided speaking of establishing an heir, and De earnestly petitioned.

sentences.zh: 會有詔，二王出邸同日婚。

translations.literal: Just then an edict went out that the two princes should leave their residences for weddings on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Just then an edict went out that the two princes should leave their residences for weddings on the same day.

sentences.zh: 德以裕王儲貳不當出外，疏言：「曩太祖以父婚子，諸王皆處禁中。

translations.literal: De held that the Crown Prince, as heir, ought not leave the palace, and memorialized: "In the past the founding Emperor, when fathers married off sons, kept all princes within the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: De held that the Prince of Yu, as heir designate, ought not leave the palace, and memorialized: "In the past the founding Emperor, when fathers married off sons, kept all princes within the forbidden precinct.

sentences.zh: 宣宗、孝宗以兄婚弟，始出外府。

translations.literal: The Xuande and Hongzhi Emperors, when elder brothers married off younger brothers, were the first to send them to outer residences.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuande and Hongzhi Emperors, when elder brothers married off younger brothers, were the first to send them to outer residences.

sentences.zh: 今事與太祖同，請從初制。

translations.literal: Today's affair is the same as the founding Emperor's; I ask that the original system be followed.
translations.idiomatic: Today's affair is the same as the founding Emperor's; I ask that the original system be followed.

sentences.zh: 」帝不許。

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor did not assent.

sentences.zh: 德又言：「《會典》醮詞，主器則曰承宗，分藩則曰承家。

translations.literal: De spoke again: "In the liturgical texts of the 《Collected Regulations》, for the chief vessel of sacrifice it says 'to inherit the lineage,' but for a prince granted a separate fief it says 'to inherit the house.'
translations.idiomatic: De spoke again: "In the liturgical texts of the 《Collected Regulations》, for the chief vessel of sacrifice it says 'to inherit the lineage,' but for a prince granted a separate fief it says 'to inherit the house.'

sentences.zh: 今裕王當何從？

translations.literal: For the Prince of Yu now, which shall it be?
translations.idiomatic: For the Prince of Yu now, which shall it be?

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅曰：「既雲王禮，自有典制。

translations.literal: " The Emperor, displeased, said: "Since this concerns princely rites, there are statutes of their own.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor, displeased, said: "Since this concerns princely rites, there are statutes of their own.

sentences.zh: 如若言，何不竟行冊立耶？

translations.literal: If it is as you say, why not go ahead and perform the investiture outright?
translations.idiomatic: If it is as you say, why not go ahead and perform the investiture outright?

sentences.zh: 」德即具冊立儀上。

translations.literal: " De thereupon submitted the full rites of investiture as a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " De thereupon submitted the full rites of investiture as a memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝滋不悅，然終諒其誠，婚亦竟不同日。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew still more displeased, yet in the end made allowance for his sincerity, and the weddings were not held on the same day after all.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grew still more displeased, yet in the end made allowance for his sincerity, and the weddings were not held on the same day after all.

sentences.zh: 裕王母康妃杜氏薨，德請用成化朝紀淑妃故事，不從。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yu's mother, Consort Kang of the Du clan, died, De asked that the precedent of Consort Ji of the Chenghua reign be followed, but this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yu's mother, Consort Kang of the Du clan, died, De asked that the precedent of Consort Ji of the Chenghua reign be followed, but this was not granted.

sentences.zh: 德遇事侃侃，裁制諸宗藩尤有執。

translations.literal: De met affairs with upright forthrightness, and in restraining the various princely fiefs he was especially firm.
translations.idiomatic: De met affairs with upright forthrightness, and in restraining the various princely fiefs he was especially firm.

sentences.zh: 或當利害，眾相顧色戰，德意氣自如。

translations.literal: When interests were at stake and the rest looked on in fear, De's spirit was as calm as ever.
translations.idiomatic: When interests were at stake and the rest looked on in fear, De's spirit was as calm as ever.

sentences.zh: 當是時，德與徐階、聶豹、程文德並以宿學都顯位。

translations.literal: At that time De, with Xu Jie, Nie Bao, and Cheng Wende, were all renowned elder scholars holding high office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time De, with Xu Jie, Nie Bao, and Cheng Wende, were all renowned elder scholars holding high office.

sentences.zh: 於是集四方名士於靈濟宮，與論良知之學。

translations.literal: He thereupon gathered noted men from the four quarters at the Lingji Palace and with them discussed the learning of innate knowing.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon gathered noted men from the four quarters at the Lingji Palace and with them discussed the learning of innate knowing.

sentences.zh: 赴者五千人。

translations.literal: Five thousand people came.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand people came.

sentences.zh: 都城講學之會，於斯為盛。

translations.literal: Among lecture gatherings in the capital, none in this period was grander.
translations.idiomatic: Among lecture gatherings in the capital, none in this period was grander.

sentences.zh: 德器宇溫粹，學務實踐，不尚空虛。

translations.literal: De's bearing was warm and pure; in learning he sought practical action and did not prize empty abstraction.
translations.idiomatic: De was warm and pure in bearing; in scholarship he pursued real practice and scorned hollow speculation.

sentences.zh: 晚見知於帝，將柄用，而德遽卒。

translations.literal: In his later years he won the Emperor's recognition and was about to be entrusted with power, but De suddenly died.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life he won the Emperor's trust and was on the verge of high appointment, when De died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚文莊。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and honored with the posthumous title Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 族人瑜，字汝重，亦學於守仁。

translations.literal: His clansman Yu, styled Ruzhong, also studied under Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Yu, styled Ruzhong, likewise studied under Shouren.

sentences.zh: 守仁教之曰：「常舀然無自是而已。

translations.literal: Shouren taught him, saying: "Always be earnest and humble in manner, and never cling to self-righteousness—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren instructed him: "Be ever earnest and unassuming, and never take yourself to be in the right—that is all there is to it.

sentences.zh: 」瑜終身踐之。

translations.literal: " Yu practiced this all his life.
translations.idiomatic: " Yu lived by that teaching to the end of his days.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉，不就會試，曰：「老親在，三公不與易也。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination but did not take the metropolitan examination, saying: "With aged parents at home, I would not exchange them even for the three highest offices.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination but declined the metropolitan examination, saying, "While my aged parents live, I would not trade them even for the three highest offices in the realm.

sentences.zh: 」母死，廬墓側。

translations.literal: " When his mother died, he built a mourning hut beside her grave.
translations.idiomatic: " When his mother died, he built a hut and kept vigil beside her tomb.

sentences.zh: 虎環廬嗥，不為動。

translations.literal: Tigers circled the hut and howled, yet he did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Tigers prowled around the hut and howled, yet he never moved.

sentences.zh: 歷官四川參議，所至有廉惠聲。

translations.literal: Serving in succession as Administration Commissioner in Sichuan, wherever he went he won a reputation for integrity and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Serving in turn as Administration Commissioner in Sichuan, he left a name for integrity and kindness wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 年近九十而卒。

translations.literal: He died near the age of ninety.
translations.idiomatic: He died not far short of ninety.

sentences.zh: 羅洪先，字達夫，吉水人。

translations.literal: Luo Hongxian, styled Dafu, was a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Hongxian, styled Dafu, came from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 父循，進士。

translations.literal: His father Xun was a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun had passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部武選郎中。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Director in the Military Appointments Section of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Director in the Military Appointments Section of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 會考選武職，有指揮二十余人素出劉瑾門，循罷其管事。

translations.literal: When a selection examination for military posts was held, more than twenty commanders who had long been followers of Liu Jin were removed from their duties by Xun.
translations.idiomatic: During an examination to select military officers, Xun stripped more than twenty commanders who had long been clients of Liu Jin of their posts.

sentences.zh: 瑾怒罵尚書王敞，敞懼，歸部趣易奏。

translations.literal: Jin flew into a rage and reviled Minister Wang Chang. Chang was afraid and returned to his ministry to urge that the memorial be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin raged and cursed Minister Wang Chang. Chang, terrified, hurried back to his ministry to have the memorial revised.

sentences.zh: 循故遲之，數日瑾敗，敞乃謝循。

translations.literal: Xun deliberately delayed; within days Jin fell, and only then did Chang thank Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Xun deliberately held back; within days Jin fell from power, and only then did Chang thank him.

sentences.zh: 循歷知鎮江、淮安二府，徐州兵備副使，鹹有聲。

translations.literal: Xun served in succession as prefect of Zhenjiang and Huai'an, and as Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs for Xuzhou; in every post he won renown.
translations.idiomatic: Xun served in turn as prefect of Zhenjiang and Huai'an and as Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs for Xuzhou, winning a fine reputation in each post.

sentences.zh: 洪先幼慕羅倫為人。

translations.literal: From youth Hongxian admired Luo Lun's character.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Hongxian admired the character of Luo Lun.

sentences.zh: 年十五，讀王守仁《傳習錄》好之，欲往受業，循不可而止。

translations.literal: At fifteen he read Wang Shouren's 《Instructions for Practical Living》 and was drawn to it; he wished to go study under him, but Xun would not permit it, and he had to abandon the plan.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he read Wang Shouren's 《Instructions for Practical Living》 and was captivated; he wished to travel to study under him, but Xun forbade it, and the plan came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 乃師事同邑李中，傳其學。

translations.literal: He thereupon took Li Zhong of his own county as his master and received his teaching.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon took Li Zhong of his own county as teacher and received his doctrine.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年舉進士第一，授修撰，即請告歸。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Jiajing he placed first in the jinshi examination, was appointed a Compiler, and immediately requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Jiajing he ranked first among the jinshi, was appointed a Compiler, and at once asked leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 外舅太仆卿曾直喜曰：「幸吾婿成大名。

translations.literal: His father-in-law Zeng Zhi, Superintendent of the Court of the Imperial Stud, said with delight: "Fortunate indeed that my son-in-law has won such great renown.
translations.idiomatic: His father-in-law Zeng Zhi, Superintendent of the Court of the Imperial Stud, said with delight, "How fortunate that my son-in-law has won such fame.

sentences.zh: 」洪先曰：「儒者事業有大於此者。

translations.literal: " Hongxian said: "There are Confucian undertakings greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongxian replied, "A Confucian's calling holds greater things than this.

sentences.zh: 此三年一人，安足喜也。

translations.literal: This is one man every three years—what is there to rejoice over?
translations.idiomatic: One man in three years—what is there to celebrate?

sentences.zh: 」洪先事親孝。

translations.literal: " Hongxian was filial toward his parents.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongxian was deeply filial toward his parents.

sentences.zh: 父每肅客，洪先冠帶行酒、拂席、授幾甚恭。

translations.literal: Whenever his father received guests formally, Hongxian would don cap and sash to pour wine, brush the mat, and set out the armrest—all with great deference.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his father received guests in formal dress, Hongxian put on cap and sash to pour wine, brush the mat, and set out the armrest, all with the utmost reverence.

sentences.zh: 居二年，詔劾請告逾期者，乃赴官。

translations.literal: After two years an edict impeached those who had exceeded their leave; only then did he take up office.
translations.idiomatic: After two years an edict censured those who had overstayed their leave, and only then did he take up his post.

sentences.zh: 尋遭父喪，苫塊蔬食，不入室者三年。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he suffered his father's death and lived in a mourning hut on coarse fare, not entering his house for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his father died; he dwelled in a hut on coarse food, and for three years did not cross the threshold of his home.

sentences.zh: 繼遭母憂，亦如之。

translations.literal: When his mother died as well, he did the same.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died in turn, he observed mourning in the same way.

sentences.zh: 十八年簡宮僚，召拜春坊左贊善。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was selected from among the palace staff and summoned to serve as Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was chosen from among the palace staff and appointed Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，與司諫唐順之、校書趙時春疏請來歲朝正後，皇太子出禦文華殿，受群臣朝賀。

translations.literal: The next winter, together with Remonstrating Secretary Tang Shunzhi and Proofreader Zhao Shichun, he submitted a memorial asking that after the New Year's audience the following year, the Crown Prince appear at Wenhua Palace to receive the court's congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter, together with Remonstrating Secretary Tang Shunzhi and Proofreader Zhao Shichun, he memorialized that after the New Year's audience the following year the Crown Prince should appear at Wenhua Palace and receive the congratulations of the court.

sentences.zh: 時帝數稱疾不視朝，諱言儲貳臨朝事，見洪先等疏，大怒曰：「是料朕必不起也。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor often claimed illness and skipped court, and forbade all talk of the heir presumptive presiding over affairs; when he saw the memorial of Hongxian and the others, he flew into a rage and said: "They assume I will never rise again.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor often pleaded illness and skipped court, and would not hear of the heir presumptive holding audience; when he read the memorial of Hongxian and the others, he flew into a rage and said, "They take it for granted that I will never recover.

sentences.zh: 」降手詔百余言切責之，遂除三人名。

translations.literal: " He issued an edict in his own hand of more than a hundred words sharply rebuking them, and removed all three from office.
translations.idiomatic: " He issued a handwritten edict of more than a hundred words sharply rebuking them, and struck all three from their posts.

sentences.zh: 洪先歸，益尋求守仁學。

translations.literal: Hongxian returned home and sought Shouren's learning all the more earnestly.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxian went home and pursued Shouren's learning with redoubled zeal.

sentences.zh: 甘淡泊，煉寒暑，躍馬挽強，考圖觀史，自天文、地誌、禮樂、典章、河渠、邊塞、戰陣攻守，下逮陰陽、算數，靡不精究。

translations.literal: Content with simplicity, he trained himself through heat and cold, leapt on horseback and drew the strong bow; he studied maps and read history—from astronomy, geography, rites and music, institutions and regulations, rivers and canals, frontier defenses, and the arts of battle and siege, down to yin-yang lore and calculation—there was nothing he did not master exhaustively.
translations.idiomatic: Content with plain living, he hardened himself through heat and cold, leapt on horseback and drew the heavy bow; he studied maps and read history—from astronomy and geography, rites and music, institutions and regulations, rivers and frontiers, the arts of attack and defense, down to yin-yang lore and reckoning—there was nothing he did not pursue to the bottom.

sentences.zh: 至人才、吏事、國計、民情，悉加意諮訪。

translations.literal: As for talent, official business, state finance, and the people's conditions, he gave them all deliberate attention and inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Talent, official affairs, state revenue, and the people's circumstances—all received his deliberate inquiry.

sentences.zh: 曰：「茍當其任，皆吾事也。

translations.literal: He said: "If it falls within one's charge, it is all one's own business.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Whatever falls within one's charge is one's own affair.

sentences.zh: 」邑田賦多宿弊，請所司均之，所司即以屬。

translations.literal: " The county's land tax had many long-standing abuses; he asked the responsible office to equalize them, and that office entrusted the task to him.
translations.idiomatic: " The county's land tax was riddled with old abuses; he asked the responsible office to equalize the burden, and the office handed the matter over to him.

sentences.zh: 洪先精心體察，弊頓除。

translations.literal: Hongxian examined the matter with great care, and the abuses were swiftly removed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxian investigated with painstaking care, and the abuses vanished at once.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，移書郡邑，得粟數十石，率友人躬振給。

translations.literal: In a year of famine he wrote to the prefectures and counties and obtained several dozen shi of grain; leading his friends in person, he distributed relief.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year he wrote to the prefectures and counties and obtained several dozen shi of grain; then he and his friends went out in person to distribute relief.

sentences.zh: 流寇入吉安，主者失措。

translations.literal: When bandits entered Ji'an, those in charge were thrown into confusion.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits entered Ji'an, the officials in charge lost their heads.

sentences.zh: 為畫策戰守，寇引去。

translations.literal: He devised plans for offense and defense, and the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up plans for attack and defense, and the bandits withdrew.

sentences.zh: 素與順之友善。

translations.literal: He had long been on friendly terms with Tang Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been close to Tang Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 順之應召，欲挽之出，嚴嵩以同鄉故，擢假邊才起用，皆力辭。

translations.literal: When Shunzhi answered the summons to office, he wished to pull Hongxian out with him; Yan Song, as a fellow townsman, promoted him on pretext of frontier talent to bring him into service—Hongxian refused them all with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzhi answered the imperial summons, he tried to draw Hongxian back into office; Yan Song, as a fellow townsman, promoted him on the pretext of frontier talent—all such overtures Hongxian refused with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 洪先雖宗良知學，然未嘗及守仁門，恒舉《易大傳》「寂然不動」、周子「無欲故靜」之旨以告學人。

translations.literal: Although Hongxian adhered to the learning of innate knowing, he never actually studied at Shouren's gate; he constantly cited to his students the purport of the 《Great Commentary on the Book of Changes》, "Still and unmoved," and Zhou Dunyi's "Without desire, therefore still."
translations.idiomatic: Though Hongxian followed the school of innate knowing, he never actually studied at Shouren's gate; he constantly taught his students the purport of the 《Great Commentary on the Book of Changes》, "Still and unmoved," and Zhou Dunyi's words, "Without desire, therefore still."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「儒者學在經世，而以無欲為本。

translations.literal: He also said: "Confucian learning lies in ordering the world, yet takes freedom from desire as its root.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Confucian learning exists to order the world, yet its root is freedom from desire.

sentences.zh: 惟無欲，然後出而經世，識精而力鉅。

translations.literal: Only when one is without desire can one go forth to order the world—with penetrating insight and mighty strength.
translations.idiomatic: Only without desire can one go forth to order the world—with keen insight and great power.

sentences.zh: 」時王畿謂良知自然，不假纖毫力。

translations.literal: " At the time Wang Ji held that innate knowing is spontaneous and needs not the slightest effort.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time Wang Ji held that innate knowing is spontaneous and requires not the slightest effort.

sentences.zh: 洪先非之曰：「世豈有現成良知者耶？

translations.literal: Hongxian objected, saying: "Is there truly such a thing in this world as ready-made innate knowing?
translations.idiomatic: Hongxian objected: "Can there truly be ready-made innate knowing in this world?

sentences.zh: 」雖與畿交好，而持論始終不合。

translations.literal: " Though he and Ji were on friendly terms, their views never fully agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Though he and Ji remained friends, their views never fully aligned.

sentences.zh: 山中有石洞，舊為虎穴，葺茅居之，命曰石蓮。

translations.literal: In the mountains there was a stone cave that had once been a tiger's den; he thatched it with reeds and dwelled there, naming it Stone Lotus.
translations.idiomatic: In the mountains was a stone cave that had once been a tiger's lair; he thatched it over and lived there, calling it Stone Lotus.

sentences.zh: 謝客，默坐一榻，三年不出戶。

translations.literal: He declined visitors, sat in silence on a single couch, and for three years did not leave his door.
translations.idiomatic: He turned away visitors, sat in silence on a single couch, and for three years never left his door.

sentences.zh: 初，告歸，過儀真，同年生主事項喬為分司。

translations.literal: When he first requested leave to return home, he passed through Yizhen; his examination cohort Xu Qiao was serving there as chief secretary of the salt monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: When he first asked leave to go home, he passed through Yizhen, where his examination cohort Xu Qiao was serving as chief secretary of the salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 有富人坐死，行萬金求為地，洪先拒不聽。

translations.literal: A wealthy man sentenced to death offered ten thousand in gold to buy clemency; Hongxian adamantly refused to listen.
translations.idiomatic: A rich man condemned to death offered ten thousand in gold to buy leniency; Hongxian flatly refused to hear of it.

sentences.zh: 喬微諷之，厲聲曰：「君不聞誌士不忘在溝壑耶？

translations.literal: Qiao gently hinted at acceptance; Hongxian said in a stern voice: "Have you not heard that a man of principle never forgets he may die in a ditch?
translations.idiomatic: Qiao gently hinted that he should accept; Hongxian said sharply, "Have you never heard that a man of principle never forgets he may die in a ditch?

sentences.zh: 」江漲，壞其室，巡撫馬森欲為營之，固辭不可。

translations.literal: " When the river rose and destroyed his house, Grand Coordinator Ma Sen wished to rebuild it for him, but he firmly declined and would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: " When the river rose and wrecked his house, Grand Coordinator Ma Sen wished to rebuild it for him, but he steadfastly refused.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初卒，贈光祿少卿，謚文莊。

translations.literal: He died early in the Longqing reign and was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, with the posthumous title Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Longqing reign and was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, with the posthumous title Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 程文德，字舜敷，永康人。

translations.literal: Cheng Wende, styled Shunfu, was a native of Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Wende, styled Shunfu, came from Yongkang.

sentences.zh: 初受業章懋，後從王守仁遊。

translations.literal: At first he studied under Zhang Mao; later he associated with Wang Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: At first he studied under Zhang Mao; later he traveled in Wang Shouren's circle.

sentences.zh: 登洪先榜進士第二，授翰林編修。

translations.literal: Placing second on Hongxian's examination roster, he became a jinshi and was appointed a Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Ranking second on Hongxian's examination list, he passed as jinshi and was appointed a Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 坐同年生楊名劾汪鋐事，下詔獄，謫信宜典史。

translations.literal: Because of the impeachment of Wang E by his examination cohort Yang Ming, he was sent to the Imperial Prison and demoted to Record Keeper of Xinyi.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated in his examination cohort Yang Ming's impeachment of Wang E, he was sent to the Imperial Prison and demoted to Record Keeper of Xinyi.

sentences.zh: 鋐罷，量移安福知縣，遷兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Wang E was dismissed, he was transferred laterally to serve as magistrate of Anfu and was promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang E fell, he was transferred to serve as magistrate of Anfu and was promoted to Assistant Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 父憂，廬墓側，終喪不入內。

translations.literal: When his father died, he built a hut beside the grave and did not enter his home throughout the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he built a hut beside the tomb and did not enter his home for the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 起兵部郎中，擢廣東提學副使，未赴，改南京國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Rising to Director in the Ministry of War, he was promoted to Vice Education Commissioner of Guangdong; before he could take up the post he was transferred to Chancellor of the Nanjing Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Director in the Ministry of War, he was next made Vice Education Commissioner of Guangdong; before he could take up that post he was transferred to Chancellor of the Nanjing Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 母憂，服闋，起禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When his mother died and mourning ended, he was recalled as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death and the end of mourning, he was recalled as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 俺答犯京師，分守宣武門，盡納鄉民避寇者。

translations.literal: When Altan Khan attacked the capital, he was assigned to hold the Xuanyang Gate and took in all the local people fleeing the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Altan Khan attacked the capital, he was assigned to hold the Xuanyang Gate and sheltered all the local people fleeing the raiders.

sentences.zh: 調吏部為左。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel as Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel as Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 已，改掌詹事府。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was reassigned to head the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was reassigned to head the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，供事西苑。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he served in the Western Park.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he served in the Western Park.

sentences.zh: 所撰青詞，頗有所規諷，帝銜之。

translations.literal: The azure-phrase compositions he drafted contained considerable remonstrance by implication, and the Emperor bore a grudge against him.
translations.idiomatic: The azure-phrase compositions he drafted carried pointed admonition, and the Emperor nursed a grievance against him.

sentences.zh: 會推南京吏部尚書，帝疑文德欲遠己，命調南京工部右侍郎。

translations.literal: When he was recommended for Minister of Personnel in Nanjing, the Emperor suspected Wende wished to keep his distance from him and ordered him transferred to Right Vice Minister of Works in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: When he was recommended for Minister of Personnel in Nanjing, the Emperor suspected Wende meant to keep his distance and ordered him transferred to Right Vice Minister of Works in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 文德疏辭，勸帝享安靜和平之福。

translations.literal: Wende submitted a memorial requesting dismissal and urged the Emperor to enjoy the blessings of peace and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Wende memorialized to resign and urged the Emperor to enjoy the blessings of peace and quiet.

sentences.zh: 帝以為謗訕，除其名。

translations.literal: The Emperor judged this slander and removed him from the register.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took this for slander and struck his name from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 既歸，聚徒講學。

translations.literal: After returning home he gathered disciples and lectured.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he gathered disciples and lectured.

sentences.zh: 卒，貧不能殮。

translations.literal: When he died, his family was too poor to provide a coffin.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his family was too poor even to provide a coffin.

sentences.zh: 萬歷間，追贈禮部尚書，謚文恭。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign he was posthumously granted Minister of Rites and given the posthumous title Wengong.
