translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he was posthumously made Minister of Rites and honored with the posthumous title Wengong.

sentences.zh: 吳悌，字思誠，金溪人。

translations.literal: Wu Ti, styled Sicheng, was a native of Jinxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ti, styled Sicheng, came from Jinxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十一年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the eleventh year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 除樂安知縣，調繁宣城，征授御史。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Le'an, he was transferred to the demanding post of Xuancheng and was then called up as a censor.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed magistrate of Le'an, he was transferred to the difficult post of Xuancheng and was then summoned as a censor.

sentences.zh: 十六年，應天府進試錄，考官評語失書名，諸生答策多譏時政。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, at the prefectural examination for the Jiangnan capital region, the chief examiners' evaluative comments omitted the candidates' names, and many answers satirized current policy.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, at the metropolitan region's provincial examination, the chief examiners' evaluative comments omitted the candidates' names, and many examination essays satirized current policy.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，逮考官諭德江汝璧、洗馬歐陽衢詔獄，貶官，府尹孫懋等下南京法司，尋得還職，而停舉子會試。

translations.literal: The Emperor was furious; the chief examiners Lecturer-in-Waiting Jiang Rubi and Reader-in-Waiting Ouyang Qu were sent to the Imperial Prison and demoted; the prefect Sun Mao and others were handed over to the Nanjing judicial offices; they were eventually restored to office, but the provincial graduates' metropolitan examination was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious; chief examiners Lecturer-in-Waiting Jiang Rubi and Reader-in-Waiting Ouyang Qu were sent to the Imperial Prison and demoted; Prefect Sun Mao and others were handed over to the Nanjing judicial offices. They were eventually restored, but the provincial graduates' metropolitan examination was suspended.

sentences.zh: 悌為舉子求寬，坐下詔獄，出視兩淮鹽政。

translations.literal: Ti pleaded for leniency on behalf of the graduates, was sent to the Imperial Prison, and then released to inspect the salt administration of the two Huai regions.
translations.idiomatic: Ti pleaded for leniency on the graduates' behalf, was sent to the Imperial Prison, and was then released to inspect the salt administration of the two Huai regions.

sentences.zh: 海溢，沒通、泰民廬，悌先發漕振之而後奏聞。

translations.literal: When the sea overflowed and submerged the homes of the people of Tong and Tai, Ti first dispatched grain transport relief and only afterward reported to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: When the sea overflowed and drowned the homes of the people of Tong and Tai, Ti first dispatched grain-transport relief and only afterward reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 尋引疾歸，還朝，按河南。

translations.literal: Soon he cited illness and returned home; after returning to court he conducted investigations in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he cited illness and went home; after returning to court he conducted investigations in Henan.

sentences.zh: 伊王典楧驕橫，憚悌，遺書稱為友。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yi, Dian Mu, was arrogant and overbearing; he feared Ti and sent a letter calling him friend.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yi, Dian Mu, was proud and overbearing; he feared Ti and sent a letter calling him friend.

sentences.zh: 悌報曰：「殿下，天子親藩，非悌所敢友。

translations.literal: Ti replied: "Your Highness is a prince of the Son of Heaven—I dare not be your friend.
translations.idiomatic: Ti replied, "Your Highness is a prince of the Son of Heaven—I dare not call myself your friend.

sentences.zh: 悌，天子憲臣，非殿下所得友。

translations.literal: I, Ti, am an inspecting minister of the Son of Heaven—Your Highness cannot befriend me.
translations.idiomatic: I, Ti, am an inspecting minister of the Son of Heaven—Your Highness cannot befriend me.

sentences.zh: 」王愈憚之。

translations.literal: " The Prince feared him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince feared him all the more.

sentences.zh: 夏言、嚴嵩當國，與悌鄉里。

translations.literal: When Xia Yan and Yan Song held power, they were Ti's fellow townspeople.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Yan and Yan Song held power, they were Ti's fellow townspeople.

sentences.zh: 嘗謁言，眾見言新服宮袍，競前譽之，悌卻立不進。

translations.literal: Once when calling on Xia Yan, Ti saw everyone rushing forward to praise Yan's new palace robe; Ti stood back and would not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Once, calling on Xia Yan, he saw everyone rush forward to praise Yan's new palace robe; Ti hung back and would not join them.

sentences.zh: 言問故，徐曰：「俟談少間，當以政請。

translations.literal: Yan asked why; he said calmly: "When we have spoken a little, I will take up matters of state.
translations.idiomatic: Yan asked why; Ti said calmly, "When we have spoken a little, I will raise matters of state.

sentences.zh: 」言為改容。

translations.literal: " Yan's manner changed.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan's manner changed at once.

sentences.zh: 及嵩擅政，悌惡之，引疾家居垂二十年。

translations.literal: When Yan Song monopolized power, Ti detested him, cited illness, and remained at home for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Song monopolized power, Ti detested him, pleaded illness, and remained at home for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 嵩敗，起故官，一歲中累遷至南京大理卿。

translations.literal: When Yan Song fell, Ti was restored to his former office and within a single year was promoted in succession to Vice President of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Song fell, Ti was restored to his former office and within a single year rose in succession to Vice President of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 時吳嶽、胡松、毛愷並以耆俊為卿貳，與悌稱「南都四君子」。

translations.literal: At the time Wu Yue, Hu Song, and Mao Kai were all elder worthies serving as vice presidents, and together with Ti they were called the Four Worthies of the Southern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wu Yue, Hu Song, and Mao Kai were all elder worthies serving as vice presidents; together with Ti they were called the Four Worthies of the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年就遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing he was immediately promoted to Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longqing he was immediately promoted to Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 明年卒。

translations.literal: He died the next year.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 悌為王守仁學，然清修果介，反躬自得為多。

translations.literal: Ti followed Wang Shouren's learning, yet in personal conduct he was pure, austere, resolute, and upright, and devoted himself chiefly to turning inward and finding satisfaction within.
translations.idiomatic: Ti followed Wang Shouren's learning, yet in personal conduct he was pure, austere, resolute, and upright, devoting himself chiefly to turning inward and finding satisfaction within.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，子仁度請恤。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign his son Ren Du petitioned for posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign his son Ren Du petitioned for posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書孫丕揚曰：「悌，理學名臣，不宜循常格。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Sun Piyang said: "Ti was an eminent Neo-Confucian minister and should not be treated by the usual rules.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Sun Piyang said, "Ti was an eminent Neo-Confucian minister and ought not be judged by ordinary precedent.

sentences.zh: 」遂用黃孔昭例，贈禮部尚書，謚文莊。

translations.literal: " Accordingly, following the precedent of Huang Kongzhao, [Ti] was posthumously granted the title Minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: " Accordingly, following the precedent of Huang Kongzhao, he was posthumously made Minister of Rites and honored with the posthumous name Wenzhuang.

sentences.zh: 鄉人建祠，與陸九淵、吳澄、吳與弼、陳九川並祀，曰五賢祠，學者稱疏山先生。

translations.literal: His fellow townsmen built a shrine where he was worshipped together with Lu Jiuyuan, Wu Cheng, Wu Yubi, and Chen Jiuchuan; it was called the Shrine of the Five Worthies, and scholars called him Master Shushan.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow townsmen built a shrine in which he was worshipped together with Lu Jiuyuan, Wu Cheng, Wu Yubi, and Chen Jiuchuan. It was called the Shrine of the Five Worthies, and scholars called him Master Shushan.

sentences.zh: 仁度，字繼疏。

translations.literal: Ren Du, styled Jishu.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Du, styled Jishu.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十七年進士。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he became a presented scholar.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he passed as a presented scholar.

sentences.zh: 授中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed a drafter in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a drafter in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三王並封議起，抗疏爭之。

translations.literal: When the debate over enfeoffing all three princes arose, he submitted a memorial in protest.
translations.idiomatic: When the controversy over enfeoffing all three princes erupted, he submitted a memorial in protest.

sentences.zh: 久之，擢吏部主事，歷考功郎中。

translations.literal: After some time he was promoted to a principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel and served successively as a director in the Merit Review Section.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was promoted to principal secretary in the Ministry of Personnel and rose through the Merit Review Section to director.

sentences.zh: 稽勛郎中趙邦清被劾，疑同官鄧光祚等嗾言路，憤激力辨。

translations.literal: When Merit Verification Director Zhao Bangqing was impeached, he suspected his colleague Deng Guangzuo and others of stirring the censorial remonstrators to attack him; infuriated, he argued his case forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: When Merit Verification Director Zhao Bangqing was impeached, he suspected his colleague Deng Guangzuo and others of inciting the remonstrators against him. Infuriated, he argued his case with all his force.

sentences.zh: 章下考功，仁度欲稍寬邦清罰，給事中梁有年遂劾仁度黨比。

translations.literal: When the memorial was referred to the Merit Review Section, Ren Du wished to lighten Bangqing's punishment somewhat; supervising secretary Liang Younian thereupon impeached Ren Du for factional collusion.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the Merit Review Section, Ren Du wished to soften Bangqing's punishment slightly; supervising secretary Liang Younian thereupon impeached Ren Du for factional collusion.

sentences.zh: 時光祚引疾去，而仁度代為文選，御史康丕揚復劾仁度傾光祚而代之，詔改調之南京。

translations.literal: At that time Guangzuo pleaded illness and departed, while Ren Du took over as director of Appointments; censor Kang Piyang again impeached Ren Du for forcing Guangzuo out in order to replace him, and an edict transferred him to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzuo then pleaded illness and left office, while Ren Du took over as director of Appointments. Censor Kang Piyang again impeached Ren Du for driving Guangzuo out so as to replace him, and an edict transferred him to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 自邦清被論後，言路訐不已，都御史溫純恚甚，請定國是，以剖眾疑，而深為仁度惜。

translations.literal: After Bangqing came under attack, the remonstrators kept up their accusations without end; Censor-in-Chief Wen Chun was greatly angered and requested that the state's right course be settled to dispel the crowd's doubts, and he deeply regretted what had befallen Ren Du.
translations.idiomatic: After Bangqing came under attack, the remonstrators kept up their accusations without end. Censor-in-Chief Wen Chun was greatly angered and asked that the state's right course be settled to dispel public doubt, and he deeply regretted what had befallen Ren Du.

sentences.zh: 仁度尋補南京刑部郎中，擢太仆少卿，進右僉都御史，巡撫山西。

translations.literal: Before long Ren Du was appointed director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, was promoted to vice minister of the Imperial Stud, advanced to vice censor-in-chief, and served as grand coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ren Du was appointed director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice, promoted to vice minister of the Imperial Stud, advanced to vice censor-in-chief, and made grand coordinator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 砥廉隅，務慈愛，與魏允貞齊名。

translations.literal: He honed his rectitude and devoted himself to benevolence, winning a reputation equal to Wei Yunzhen's.
translations.idiomatic: He honed his integrity and devoted himself to benevolence, winning a reputation equal to Wei Yunzhen's.

sentences.zh: 居四年，以疾歸。

translations.literal: After four years in office he retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After four years in office he retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 熹宗初，起大理卿，進兵部右侍郎，復稱疾去。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xizong's reign he was recalled as chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review, was promoted to vice minister of the right in the Ministry of War, and again pleaded illness and resigned.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xizong's reign he was recalled as chief minister of the Court of Judicial Review, promoted to vice minister of the right in the Ministry of War, and again pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 再起工部左侍郎。

translations.literal: He was recalled again as vice minister of the left in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled again as vice minister of the left in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年，魏忠賢以仁度與趙南星、楊漣等善，勒令致仕，尋卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianqi, Wei Zhongxian, because Ren Du was on good terms with Zhao Nanxing, Yang Lian, and others, compelled him to retire; he soon died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianqi, Wei Zhongxian, because Ren Du was on good terms with Zhao Nanxing, Yang Lian, and others, forced him to retire; he soon died.

sentences.zh: 仁度，名父子，克自振勵，鄒元標亟稱之。

translations.literal: Ren Du was a famous father-and-son pair; he was able to rouse himself to strive, and Zou Yuanbiao repeatedly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Du formed a famous father-and-son pair with his father; he exerted himself to improve, and Zou Yuanbiao repeatedly praised him.

sentences.zh: 守仁之門，從遊者恒數百，浙東、江西尤眾，善推演師說者稱弘綱、廷仁及錢德洪、王畿。

translations.literal: At Shouren's gate, followers numbered in the hundreds; eastern Zhejiang and Jiangxi were especially numerous. Those skilled at elaborating their master's doctrine were called Honggang, Tingren, as well as Qian Dehong and Wang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: At Shouren's gate, followers numbered in the hundreds, with eastern Zhejiang and Jiangxi especially well represented. Those most skilled at elaborating their master's doctrine were Honggang, Tingren, Qian Dehong, and Wang Ji.

sentences.zh: 時人語曰：「江有何、黃，浙有錢、王。

translations.literal: People said at the time: "In Jiangxi there are He and Huang; in Zhejiang there are Qian and Wang.
translations.idiomatic: People said at the time, "In Jiangxi there are He and Huang; in Zhejiang there are Qian and Wang.

sentences.zh: 」然守仁之學，傳山陰、泰州者，流弊靡所底極，惟江西多實踐，安福則劉邦采，新建則魏良政兄弟，其最著雲。

translations.literal: " Yet where Shouren's learning was transmitted in Shanyin and Taizhou, its abuses knew no limit; only in Jiangxi was practice generally earnest—in Anfu it was Liu Bangcai, in Xinjian it was the Wei Liangzheng brothers; these were the most eminent.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet where Shouren's learning spread in Shanyin and Taizhou, its abuses knew no bottom; only in Jiangxi was practice generally earnest—in Anfu it was Liu Bangcai, in Xinjian it was the Wei Liangzheng brothers. These were the most eminent.

sentences.zh: 邦采，字君亮。

translations.literal: Bangcai, styled Junliang.
translations.idiomatic: Bangcai, styled Junliang.

sentences.zh: 族子曉受業守仁，歸語邦采，遂與從兄文敏及弟侄九人謁守仁於裏第，師事焉。

translations.literal: His clansman Xiao had studied under Shouren; returning home he spoke of it to Bangcai, and Bangcai together with his older cousin Wenmin and nine younger brothers and nephews went to pay respects to Shouren at his private residence and took him as their master.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Xiao had studied under Shouren; returning home he told Bangcai of it, and Bangcai together with his older cousin Wenmin and nine younger brothers and nephews went to Shouren's private residence to pay their respects and took him as their master.

sentences.zh: 父憂，蔬水廬墓。

translations.literal: During his father's mourning he lived on vegetables and water in a hut by the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: During his father's mourning he lived on vegetables and water in a hut beside the tomb.

sentences.zh: 免喪，不復應舉。

translations.literal: After the mourning period ended, he no longer sought to enter the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period ended, he no longer sought to enter the examinations.

sentences.zh: 提學副使趙淵檄赴試，御史儲良才許以常服入闈，不解衣檢察，乃就試，得中式。

translations.literal: Education intendant Zhao Yuan summoned him to take the exam; censor Chu Liangcai promised he might enter the examination hall in ordinary dress without having his clothes searched—only then did he take the exam and pass.
translations.idiomatic: Education intendant Zhao Yuan summoned him to take the examination; censor Chu Liangcai promised he might enter the hall in ordinary dress without being searched—only then did he sit for the exam and pass.

sentences.zh: 久之，除壽寧教諭，擢嘉興府同知，棄官歸。

translations.literal: After some time he was appointed instructor of Shouning, was promoted to vice prefect of Jiaxing Prefecture, then abandoned his office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed instructor of Shouning, promoted to vice prefect of Jiaxing Prefecture, then abandoned his office and returned home.

sentences.zh: 邦采識高明，用力果銳。

translations.literal: Bangcai had clear and lofty insight and applied himself with decisive sharpness.
translations.idiomatic: Bangcai had clear and lofty insight and applied himself with decisive sharpness.

sentences.zh: 守仁倡良知為學的，久益敝，有以揣摩為妙悟，縱恣為自然者，邦采每極言排斥焉。

translations.literal: Shouren had advocated innate knowing as the aim of learning, but over time this grew stale; some took crafty imitation for subtle enlightenment and unrestrained behavior for naturalness—Bangcai always spoke out forcefully to repudiate such views.
translations.idiomatic: Shouren had made innate knowing the aim of learning, but over time the teaching grew stale; some took crafty imitation for subtle enlightenment and unrestrained behavior for naturalness—Bangcai always spoke out forcefully against such views.

sentences.zh: 文敏，字宜充。

translations.literal: Wenmin, styled Yichong.
translations.idiomatic: Wenmin, styled Yichong.

sentences.zh: 父喪除，絕意科舉。

translations.literal: After his father's mourning period ended, he abandoned all thought of the civil examinations.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's mourning period ended, he abandoned all thought of the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「學者當循本心之明，時見己過，刮磨砥礪，以融氣稟，絕外誘，征諸倫理、事物之實，無一不慊於心，而後為聖門正學，非困勉不可得入也。

translations.literal: He once said: "Scholars should follow the brightness of the original mind, constantly recognize their own faults, scrape, polish, and hone themselves to merge the qi endowed by nature, cut off external enticements, and verify against the reality of ethical principle and concrete affairs—only when nothing fails to satisfy the heart may one enter the orthodox learning of the sage's gate; without striving through effort one cannot enter.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Scholars should follow the brightness of the original mind, constantly see their own faults, scrape and polish themselves to merge the qi endowed by nature, cut off external enticements, and test everything against the reality of ethical principle and concrete affairs. Only when nothing fails to satisfy the heart does one enter the orthodox learning of the sage's gate; without striving through effort one cannot enter.

sentences.zh: 高談虛悟，炫未離本，非德之賊乎？

translations.literal: Lofty talk and empty enlightenment, display that has never left the root—is this not the enemy of virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Lofty talk and empty enlightenment, display that has never left the root—is this not the enemy of virtue?

sentences.zh: 」曉，字伯光。

translations.literal: Xiao, styled Boguang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao, styled Boguang.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉，後為新寧知縣，有善政。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination and later served as magistrate of Xinning, with good policies.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination and later served as magistrate of Xinning, where his policies won praise.

sentences.zh: 良政，字師伊。

translations.literal: Liangzheng, styled Shiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzheng, styled Shiyi.

sentences.zh: 守仁撫江西，與兄良弼，弟良器、良貴，鹹學焉。

translations.literal: When Shouren administered Jiangxi, he studied together with his elder brother Liangbi and younger brothers Liangqi and Lianggui—all of them studied under Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouren governed Jiangxi, he and his elder brother Liangbi and younger brothers Liangqi and Lianggui all studied under him.

sentences.zh: 提學副使邵銳、巡按御史唐龍持論與守仁異，戒諸生勿往謁，良政兄弟獨不顧，深為守仁所許。

translations.literal: Education intendant Shao Rui and touring censor Tang Long held views differing from Shouren's and warned the students not to go pay respects; the Liangzheng brothers alone paid no heed and were deeply approved by Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: Education intendant Shao Rui and touring censor Tang Long held views at odds with Shouren's and warned the students not to visit him; the Liangzheng brothers alone paid no heed and won Shouren's deep approval.

sentences.zh: 良政功尤專，孝友敦樸，燕居無惰容，嘗曰：「不尤人，何人不可處；

translations.literal: Liangzheng's effort was especially concentrated; filial, fraternal, and plain in character, in daily life at home he showed no slackness. He once said: "If one does not blame others, what person cannot one live with?
translations.idiomatic: Liangzheng's effort was especially concentrated. Filial, fraternal, and plain in character, he showed no slackness even in daily life at home. He once said, "If one does not blame others, what person cannot one live with?

sentences.zh: 不累事，何事不可為。

translations.literal: If one does not burden affairs, what affair cannot one undertake.
translations.idiomatic: If one does not burden affairs, what affair cannot one undertake?

sentences.zh: 」舉鄉試第一而卒。

translations.literal: " He placed first in the provincial examination and then died.
translations.idiomatic: " He placed first in the provincial examination and then died.

sentences.zh: 良弼嘗言，「吾夢見師伊，輒汗浹背」，其為兄憚如此。

translations.literal: Liangbi once said, "Whenever I dream of Shiyi, sweat soaks through my back"—such was the awe he felt as elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi once said, "Whenever I dream of Shiyi, sweat soaks through my back"—such was the awe he felt as elder brother.

sentences.zh: 良器，字師顏。

translations.literal: Liangqi, styled Shiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Liangqi, styled Shiyan.

sentences.zh: 性超穎絕人，雖宗良知，踐履務平實。

translations.literal: His nature was surpassingly keen; though he revered innate knowing, in practice he strove for plain solidity.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was surpassingly keen; though he revered innate knowing, in practice he strove for plain solidity.

sentences.zh: 良弼，自有傳。

translations.literal: Liangbi has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 良貴，官右副都御史。

translations.literal: Lianggui served as vice censor-in-chief of the right.
translations.idiomatic: Lianggui served as vice censor-in-chief of the right.

sentences.zh: 王時槐，字子植，安福人。

translations.literal: Wang Shihuai, styled Zizhi, was a native of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shihuai, styled Zizhi, came from Anfu.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十六年進士。

translations.literal: Presented scholar in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed as a presented scholar in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 授南京兵部主事。

translations.literal: Appointed principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 歷禮部郎中、福建僉事。

translations.literal: He served successively as director in the Ministry of Rites and as surveillance commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as director in the Ministry of Rites and as surveillance commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 累官太仆少卿，降光祿少卿。

translations.literal: After successive promotions he reached vice minister of the Imperial Stud, then was demoted to vice minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: After successive promotions he rose to vice minister of the Imperial Stud, then was demoted to vice minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 隆慶末，出為陜西參政。

translations.literal: At the end of Longqing he went out as administration commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Longqing he went out as administration commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 張居正柄國，以京察罷歸。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng held power, he was dismissed and sent home in the capital inspection.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng held power, he was dismissed and sent home in the capital inspection.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，南贛巡撫張嶽疏薦之。

translations.literal: In the Wanli era, Grand Coordinator Zhang Yue of southern Ganzhou memorialized recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli era, Grand Coordinator Zhang Yue of southern Ganzhou memorialized recommending him.

sentences.zh: 吏部言：「六年京察，祖制也。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel said: "The capital inspection every six years is an ancestral institution.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel said, "The capital inspection every six years is an ancestral institution.

sentences.zh: 若執政有所驅除，非時一舉，謂之閏察。

translations.literal: If the ruling faction removes people on its own initiative outside the regular schedule, it is called an intercalary inspection.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruling faction removes people on its own initiative outside the regular schedule, it is called an intercalary inspection.

sentences.zh: 時槐在閏察中，群情不服，請召時槐，且永停閏察。

translations.literal: Shihuai was caught in an intercalary inspection and public sentiment was not satisfied; please summon Shihuai and permanently halt intercalary inspections.
translations.idiomatic: Shihuai was caught in an intercalary inspection and public sentiment was not satisfied. We ask that Shihuai be summoned and that intercalary inspections be permanently halted.

sentences.zh: 」報可。

translations.literal: " The reply granted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The reply granted it.

sentences.zh: 久之，陸光祖掌銓，起貴州參政，旋擢南京鴻臚卿，進太常，皆不赴。

translations.literal: After some time Lu Guangzu took charge of appointments, recalled him as administration commissioner of Guizhou, then quickly promoted him to chief minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainment and advanced to chief minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices—he accepted none of these.
translations.idiomatic: After some time Lu Guangzu took charge of appointments, recalled him as administration commissioner of Guizhou, then quickly raised him to chief minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainment and chief minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in turn—he accepted none of them.

sentences.zh: 時槐師同縣劉文敏，及仕，遍質四方學者，自謂終無所得。

translations.literal: Shihuai's teacher was Liu Wenmin of the same county; once in office he questioned scholars everywhere but declared in the end that he had gained nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Shihuai's teacher was Liu Wenmin of the same county. Once in office he questioned scholars everywhere, yet in the end declared he had gained nothing.

sentences.zh: 年五十，罷官，反身實證，始悟造化生生之幾，不隨念慮起滅。

translations.literal: At age fifty he left office, turned inward to verify through practice, and only then realized the subtle stirring of creation's ceaseless generation—it does not rise and fall with thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: At fifty he left office, turned inward to verify through practice, and only then realized the subtle stirring of creation's ceaseless generation—it does not rise and fall with thoughts.

sentences.zh: 學者欲識真幾，當從慎獨入。

translations.literal: For scholars who wish to discern the true subtle stirring, one should enter through watchfulness in solitude.
translations.idiomatic: For scholars who wish to discern the true subtle stirring, the way in is watchfulness in solitude.

sentences.zh: 其論性曰：「孟子性善之說，決不可易。

translations.literal: On human nature he said: "Mencius's doctrine that nature is good absolutely cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: On human nature he said, "Mencius's doctrine that nature is good absolutely cannot be changed.

sentences.zh: 使性中本無仁義，則惻隱羞惡更何從生。

translations.literal: If benevolence and righteousness were not originally in nature, from what would compassion and shame and dislike arise?
translations.idiomatic: If benevolence and righteousness were not originally in nature, from what would compassion and shame and dislike arise?

sentences.zh: 且人應事接物，如是則安，不如是則不安，非善而何？

translations.literal: Moreover, when people respond to affairs and meet things, if they do so in this way they are at ease; if not, they are ill at ease—if this is not good, then what is?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when people respond to affairs and meet things, acting thus they are at ease; acting otherwise they are ill at ease—if this is not good, then what is?

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「居敬、窮理，二者不可廢一。

translations.literal: He also said: "Reverent attentiveness and investigating principle—the two cannot have one abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Reverent attentiveness and investigating principle—the two cannot have one abandoned.

sentences.zh: 要之，居敬二字盡之。

translations.literal: In essence, the two words 'reverent attentiveness' exhaust the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In essence, the two words 'reverent attentiveness' exhaust the matter.

sentences.zh: 自其居敬之精明了悟而言，謂之窮理，即考索討論，亦居敬中之一事。

translations.literal: Speaking from the clarity and enlightenment attained in reverent attentiveness, this is called investigating principle; even examination, inquiry, and discussion are one matter within reverent attentiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking from the clarity and enlightenment attained in reverent attentiveness, this is called investigating principle; even examination, inquiry, and discussion are one matter within reverent attentiveness.

sentences.zh: 敬無所不該，敬外更無余事也。

translations.literal: Reverent attentiveness embraces all things; beyond reverent attentiveness there is nothing else to be done.
translations.idiomatic: Reverent attentiveness embraces all things; beyond reverent attentiveness there is nothing else to be done.

sentences.zh: 」年八十四卒。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 廬陵陳嘉謨，字世顯，與時槐同年進士。

translations.literal: Chen Jiamo of Luling, styled Shixian, was a presented scholar in the same year as Shihuai.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jiamo of Luling, styled Shixian, passed as a presented scholar in the same year as Shihuai.

sentences.zh: 為給事中，不附嚴嵩，出之外。

translations.literal: As a supervising secretary he did not attach himself to Yan Song and was sent out of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: As a supervising secretary he refused to attach himself to Yan Song and was sent out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 歷湖廣參政，乞休歸，專用力於學。

translations.literal: He served successively as administration commissioner of Huguang, requested retirement, and devoted himself wholly to learning.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as administration commissioner of Huguang, requested retirement, and devoted himself wholly to learning.

sentences.zh: 凡及其門者，告之曰：「有塘南在，可往師之。

translations.literal: All who came to his gate were told: "With Tangnan still here, you may go study under him.
translations.idiomatic: All who came to his gate were told, "With Tangnan still here, you may go study under him.

sentences.zh: 」塘南，時槐別號也。

translations.literal: " Tangnan was Shihuai's style name.
translations.idiomatic: " Tangnan was Shihuai's style name.

sentences.zh: 年八十三卒。

translations.literal: He died at age eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 許孚遠，字孟中，德清人，受學同郡唐樞。

translations.literal: Xu Fuyuan, styled Mengzhong, was a native of Deqing and studied under Tang Shu of the same prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fuyuan, styled Mengzhong, came from Deqing and studied under Tang Shu of the same prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十一年成進士，授南京工部主事，就改吏部。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Jiajing he became a presented scholar, was appointed principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Works, and was soon transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of Jiajing he passed as a presented scholar, was appointed principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Works, and was soon transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 已，調北部。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to the northern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to the northern capital.

sentences.zh: 尚書楊博惡孚遠講學，會大計京朝官，黜浙人幾半，博鄉山西無一焉。

translations.literal: Minister Yang Bo disliked Fuyuan's lecturing on learning; when the great assessment of capital officials came around, nearly half the Zhejiang men were dismissed while not a single man from Bo's native Shanxi was touched.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yang Bo disliked Fuyuan's lecturing on learning. When the great assessment of capital officials came around, nearly half the Zhejiang men were dismissed while not a single man from Bo's native Shanxi was touched.

sentences.zh: 孚遠有後言，博不悅，孚遠遂移疾去。

translations.literal: Fuyuan had words of criticism afterward; Bo was displeased, and Fuyuan thereupon resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyuan spoke critically afterward; Bo was displeased, and Fuyuan thereupon resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，高拱薦起考功主事，出為廣東僉事，招大盜李茂、許俊美，擒倭黨七十余輩以降，錄功，賚銀幣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, Gao Gong recommended him and recalled him as principal secretary in the Merit Review Section; he went out as surveillance commissioner of Guangdong, recruited the great bandits Li Mao and Xu Junmei, and captured over seventy Japanese-affiliate ringleaders to surrender; his merit was recorded and he was rewarded with silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing, Gao Gong recommended him and recalled him as principal secretary in the Merit Review Section. He went out as surveillance commissioner of Guangdong, recruited the great bandits Li Mao and Xu Junmei, and captured over seventy Japanese-affiliate ringleaders to surrender. His merit was recorded and he was rewarded with silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 旋移福建。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，拱罷政，張居正議逐拱黨，復大計京官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, Gao Gong was dismissed from power; Zhang Juzheng proposed purging Gao's faction and again conducted a great assessment of capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, Gao Gong was dismissed from power. Zhang Juzheng proposed purging Gao's faction and again conducted a great assessment of capital officials.

sentences.zh: 王篆為考功，誣孚遠黨拱，謫兩淮鹽運司判官。

translations.literal: Wang Zhuan was in charge of the assessment and falsely charged Fuyuan with belonging to Gao's faction; he was demoted to assistant salt transport judge of the Two Huai circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhuan ran the assessment and falsely charged Fuyuan with belonging to Gao's faction; he was demoted to assistant salt transport judge of the Two Huai circuits.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部郎中，出知建昌府，暇輒集諸生講學，引貢士鄧元錫、劉元卿為友。

translations.literal: He served as director in the Ministry of War, went out as prefect of Jianchang Prefecture, and in his leisure gathered students to lecture on learning, taking presented scholar Deng Yuanxi and Liu Yuanqing as friends.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director in the Ministry of War, went out as prefect of Jianchang Prefecture, and in his leisure gathered students to lecture on learning, taking presented scholars Deng Yuanxi and Liu Yuanqing as friends.

sentences.zh: 尋以給事中鄒元標薦，擢陜西提學副使，敬禮貢士王之士，移書當路，並元卿、元錫薦之。

translations.literal: Before long, on the recommendation of supervising secretary Zou Yuanbiao, he was promoted to education intendant of Shaanxi, treated the presented scholar Wang Zhishi with respect, and wrote to those in power recommending Yuanqing and Yuanxi as well.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, on supervising secretary Zou Yuanbiao's recommendation, he was promoted to education intendant of Shaanxi, treated the presented scholar Wang Zhishi with respect, and wrote to those in power recommending Yuanqing and Yuanxi as well.

sentences.zh: 後三人並得征，由孚遠倡也。

translations.literal: Later all three were summoned to office—this began with Fuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later all three were summoned to office—this began with Fuyuan.

sentences.zh: 遷應天府丞，坐為李材訟冤，貶二秩，由廣東僉事再遷右通政。

translations.literal: He was transferred to assistant prefect of Shuntian Prefecture; because he pleaded Li Cai's innocence he was demoted two ranks, returning from Guangdong surveillance commissioner to vice commissioner of communications of the right.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to assistant prefect of Shuntian Prefecture; for pleading Li Cai's innocence he was demoted two ranks, returning from Guangdong surveillance commissioner to vice commissioner of communications of the right.

sentences.zh: 二十年擢右僉都御史，巡撫福建。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief and served as grand coordinator of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief and made grand coordinator of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 倭陷朝鮮，議封貢，孚遠請敕諭日本，擒斬平秀吉，不從。

translations.literal: When the Japanese invaded Korea, there was debate over enfeoffment and tribute missions; Fuyuan requested an imperial instruction to Japan to capture and execute Hideyoshi—this was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Japanese invaded Korea, there was debate over enfeoffment and tribute missions. Fuyuan requested an imperial instruction to Japan to capture and execute Hideyoshi, but this was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 呂宋國酋子訟商人襲殺其父，孚遠以聞，詔戮罪人，厚犒其使。

translations.literal: The son of a Luzon chieftain sued merchants for attacking and killing his father; Fuyuan reported it; an edict ordered the criminals executed and the envoy richly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: The son of a Luzon chieftain sued merchants for attacking and killing his father. Fuyuan reported it; an edict ordered the criminals executed and the envoy richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 福州饑，民掠官府，孚遠擒倡首者，亂稍定，而給事中耿隨龍、御史甘士價等劾孚遠宜斥，帝不問。

translations.literal: Famine struck Fuzhou; the people plundered government offices; Fuyuan arrested the ringleaders and the disorder eased somewhat—yet supervising secretaries Geng Suilong, censor Gan Shijia, and others impeached Fuyuan as deserving dismissal; the emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck Fuzhou and the people plundered government offices. Fuyuan arrested the ringleaders and the disorder eased somewhat, yet supervising secretaries Geng Suilong, censor Gan Shijia, and others impeached Fuyuan as deserving dismissal; the emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 所部多僧田，孚遠入其六於官。

translations.literal: In his jurisdiction there was much monastic land; Fuyuan had six parts of it incorporated into government holdings.
translations.idiomatic: In his jurisdiction there was much monastic land; Fuyuan had six parts of it incorporated into government holdings.

sentences.zh: 又募民墾海壇地八萬三千有奇，築城建營舍，聚兵以守，因請推行於南日、彭湖及浙中陳錢、金塘、玉環、南麂諸島，皆報可。

translations.literal: He also recruited commoners to reclaim eighty-three thousand-odd mu of tidal flat, built city walls and barracks, and gathered troops to garrison it; he then requested that this be extended to the islands of Nanri, Penghu, and in Zhejiang Chenqian, Jintang, Yuhuan, Nanji, and the like—all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also recruited commoners to reclaim more than eighty-three thousand mu of tidal flat, built city walls and barracks, and gathered troops to garrison it. He then requested that the same policy be extended to the islands of Nanri, Penghu, and in Zhejiang Chenqian, Jintang, Yuhuan, Nanji, and the like—all were approved.

sentences.zh: 居三年，入為南京大理卿，就遷兵部右侍郎，改左，調北部。

translations.literal: After three years in office he entered the capital as chief minister of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review, was immediately transferred to vice minister of the right in the Ministry of War, then vice minister of the left, and was transferred to the northern capital.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office he entered the capital as chief minister of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review, was immediately made vice minister of the right in the Ministry of War, then vice minister of the left, and was transferred to the northern capital.

sentences.zh: 甫半道，被論。

translations.literal: Halfway there he came under attack.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway there he came under attack.

sentences.zh: 乞休，疏屢上，乃許。

translations.literal: He requested retirement; after memorials were submitted repeatedly, permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement; after memorials were submitted repeatedly, permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 又數年，卒於家，贈南京工部尚書，後謚恭簡。

translations.literal: Several years later he died at home; he was posthumously granted the title Nanjing Minister of Works, and later given the posthumous name Gongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he died at home. He was posthumously made Nanjing Minister of Works and later honored with the posthumous name Gongjian.

sentences.zh: 孚遠篤信良知，而惡夫援良知以入佛者。

translations.literal: Fu Yuan deeply believed in innate knowing, yet hated those who invoked innate knowing to enter Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yuan was a firm believer in innate knowing, yet he despised those who used it as a bridge into Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 知建昌，與郡人羅汝芳講學不合。

translations.literal: When he was prefect of Jianchang, he could not agree with his fellow townsman Luo Rufang in their lectures on learning.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Jianchang, he found himself at odds with his fellow townsman Luo Rufang whenever they lectured on learning.

sentences.zh: 及官南京，與汝芳門人禮部侍郎楊起元、尚寶司卿周汝登，並主講席。

translations.literal: When he served in Nanjing, he shared the main lectern with Rufang's disciples Yang Qiyuan, Vice Minister of Rites, and Zhou Rudeng, Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in Nanjing, he shared the main lectern with Rufang's disciples Yang Qiyuan, Vice Minister of Rites, and Zhou Rudeng, Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 汝登以無善無惡為宗，孚遠作《九諦》以難之，言：「文成宗旨，原與聖門不異，以性無不善，故知無不良。

translations.literal: Rudeng took 'neither good nor evil' as his doctrine; Fu Yuan wrote 《The Nine Theses》 to challenge him, saying: 'Wencheng's essential teaching originally did not differ from the sage's school: because nature holds nothing that is not good, knowledge holds nothing that is bad.
translations.idiomatic: Rudeng made 'neither good nor evil' his creed; Fu Yuan answered with 《The Nine Theses》, arguing that 'Wencheng's essential teaching was never at odds with the sage's school—because nature knows no evil, knowledge knows no wrong.'

sentences.zh: 良知即是未發之中，立論至為明析。

translations.literal: Innate knowing is precisely the state before emotions arise—the argument is surpassingly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Innate knowing is precisely the stillness before the heart stirs—a point argued with luminous clarity.

sentences.zh: 無善無惡心之體一語，蓋指其未發時，廓然寂然者而言之，止形容得一靜字，合下三語，始為無病。

translations.literal: The phrase 'neither good nor evil is the substance of the mind' refers to that vast, silent state before it has stirred—it describes only the word 'stillness.' Joined with the three phrases that follow, the doctrine is sound.
translations.idiomatic: The line 'neither good nor evil is the substance of the mind' speaks only of that vast, silent moment before the heart moves—it captures nothing but stillness. Taken together with the three phrases that follow, the teaching stands without flaw.

sentences.zh: 今以心意知物，俱無善惡可言者，非文成之正傳也。

translations.literal: To say now that mind, intent, knowing, and things alike admit no talk of good or evil—that is not Wencheng's true transmission.
translations.idiomatic: But to claim that mind, intent, knowing, and things alike are beyond good and evil—that is not Wencheng's true transmission.

sentences.zh: 」彼此論益齟齠。

translations.literal: Their disputations grew ever more at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Their disputations grew ever sharper and more irreconcilable.

sentences.zh: 而孚遠撫福建，與巡按御史陳子貞不相得，子貞督學南畿，遂密諷同列拾遺劾之。

translations.literal: When Fu Yuan served as governor of Fujian, he did not get on with Censor-in-Chief Chen Zizhen; Zizhen had previously supervised education in the southern capital region, and secretly urged colleagues to find omissions and impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Yuan governed Fujian, he clashed with touring censor Chen Zizhen, who had once overseen education in the southern capital region and now quietly urged his colleagues to dredge up omissions and impeach him.

sentences.zh: 從孚遠遊者，馮從吾、劉宗周、丁元薦，皆為名儒。

translations.literal: Those who studied under Fu Yuan—Feng Congwu, Liu Zongzhou, and Ding Yuanying—were all renowned scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Those who studied under Fu Yuan—Feng Congwu, Liu Zongzhou, and Ding Yuanying—were all scholars of note.

sentences.zh: 尤時熙，字季美，洛陽人。

translations.literal: You Shixi, styled Jimei, was a native of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: You Shixi, styled Jimei, came from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 生而警敏不群，弱冠舉嘉靖元年鄉試。

translations.literal: He was precociously bright and stood apart from others; in his early twenties he passed the provincial examination in the first year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was quick and singular; in his early twenties he passed the provincial examination in the first year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 時王守仁《傳習錄》始出，士大夫多力排之，時熙一見嘆曰：「道不在是乎？

translations.literal: When Wang Shouren's 《Instructions for Practical Living》 first appeared, most scholar-officials fiercely opposed it—but Shixi read it once and sighed, saying: 'Is not the Way here?'
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shouren's 《Instructions for Practical Living》 first appeared, most scholar-officials fiercely rejected it—but Shixi read it once and sighed: 'Is the Way not here?'

sentences.zh: 向吾役誌詞章，末矣。

translations.literal: How misguided I was, wasting myself on literary ornament!
translations.idiomatic: All this time I have slaved over literary ornament—how petty!

sentences.zh: 」已而以疾稍從事養生家。

translations.literal: Later he took up the ways of self-cultivation on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on account of illness, he turned briefly to the arts of nourishing life.

sentences.zh: 授元氏教諭，父喪除，改官章丘，一以致良知為教，兩邑士亦知新建學。

translations.literal: Appointed Instructor at Yuanshi, he returned to office after his father's mourning and was transferred to Zhangqiu, where he made the extension of innate knowing his teaching; in both districts the gentry came to know the New Teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Instructor at Yuanshi, he returned to office after his father's mourning and was transferred to Zhangqiu, where he taught the extension of innate knowing; in both districts the local gentry came to know the New Teaching.

sentences.zh: 入為國子博士，徐階為祭酒，命六館士鹹取法焉。

translations.literal: He entered service as a Doctor of the Imperial Academy; when Xu Jie became Chancellor, he ordered the students of all six halls to take Shixi as their model.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a Doctor of the Imperial Academy; when Xu Jie became Chancellor, he ordered the students of all six halls to take Shixi as their model.

sentences.zh: 居常以不獲師事守仁為恨，聞郎中劉魁得守仁之傳，遂師事之。

translations.literal: He always regretted that he had never studied directly under Shouren; hearing that Vice Director Liu Kui had received Shouren's transmission, he took Kui as his master.
translations.idiomatic: He always regretted that he had never studied directly under Shouren; hearing that Vice Director Liu Kui had received Shouren's transmission, he took Kui as his master.

sentences.zh: 魁以直言錮詔獄，則書所疑，時時從獄中質問。

translations.literal: When Kui was imprisoned for his blunt memorials, Shixi wrote down his doubts and from time to time questioned him through the prison walls.
translations.idiomatic: When Kui was imprisoned for his blunt memorials, Shixi wrote down his doubts and from time to time sent them into the prison to be answered.

sentences.zh: 尋以戶部主事榷稅滸墅，課足而止，不私一錢。

translations.literal: Soon after, as a Principal in the Ministry of Revenue he collected taxes at Hushu; once the quota was met he stopped, never pocketing a single coin for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, as a Principal in the Ministry of Revenue, he collected taxes at Hushu; once the quota was met he stopped, never keeping a single coin for himself.

sentences.zh: 念母老，乞終養歸，遂不出，日以修己淑人為事，足未嘗涉公府。

translations.literal: Thinking of his aged mother, he asked leave to retire and care for her until her death, then never went out again, devoting himself daily to self-cultivation and nurturing others; his feet never crossed the threshold of any yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking of his aged mother, he asked leave to retire and care for her to the end; thereafter he never went out again, devoting himself daily to self-cultivation and nurturing others—his feet never crossed the threshold of any yamen.

sentences.zh: 齋中設守仁位，晨興必焚香肅拜，來學者亦令展謁。

translations.literal: In his study he set up a place for Shouren; each morning at rising he burned incense and bowed reverently, and he required newcomers to do the same.
translations.idiomatic: In his study he set up a place for Shouren; each morning at rising he burned incense and bowed with reverence, and required newcomers to do the same.

sentences.zh: 晚年，病學者憑虛見而忽躬行，甚且越繩墨自恣，故其論議切於日用，不為空虛隱怪之談。

translations.literal: In his later years, distressed that scholars indulged hollow insights and neglected personal practice—some even transgressed bounds and did as they pleased—his discourse stayed close to daily life and avoided empty talk of mystery and strangeness.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years, distressed that scholars chased hollow insight and neglected personal practice—some even overstepped all bounds and did as they pleased—he kept his discourse close to daily life and would not indulge empty talk of mystery and strangeness.

sentences.zh: 卒於萬歷八年，年七十有八，學者稱西川先生。

translations.literal: He died in the eighth year of Wanli at seventy-eight; scholars called him Master Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of Wanli, aged seventy-eight; scholars called him Master Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 其門人，孟化鯉最著，自有傳。

translations.literal: Among his disciples, Meng Huali was the most prominent and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Among his disciples, Meng Huali was the most prominent and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 張後覺，字誌仁，茌平人。

translations.literal: Zhang Houjue, styled Zhiren, was a native of Chiping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Houjue, styled Zhiren, came from Chiping.

sentences.zh: 父文祥，由鄉舉官廣昌知縣。

translations.literal: His father Wenxiang became magistrate of Guangchang through the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenxiang, a provincial examination graduate, served as magistrate of Guangchang.

sentences.zh: 後覺生有異質，事親考，居喪哀毀，三年不禦內。

translations.literal: Houjue was born with unusual gifts; he served his parents with filial care, and in mourning was so shattered he did not take a wife for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Houjue was born with unusual gifts; he served his parents with filial devotion, and in mourning was so shattered that for three years he did not take a wife.

sentences.zh: 早歲，聞良知之說於縣教諭顏鑰，遂精思力踐，偕同誌講習。

translations.literal: In his youth he heard the doctrine of innate knowing from the county instructor Yan Yao, then pondered deeply and practiced hard, studying together with like-minded companions.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he heard the doctrine of innate knowing from the county instructor Yan Yao, then pondered deeply and practiced hard, studying together with like-minded companions.

sentences.zh: 已而貴溪徐樾以王守仁再傳弟子來為參政，後覺率同誌往師之，學益有聞。

translations.literal: Later Xu Yue of Guixi, a second-generation disciple of Wang Shouren, came as Assistant Administrator; Houjue led his companions to study under him, and his learning grew ever more refined.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xu Yue of Guixi, a second-generation disciple of Wang Shouren, came as Assistant Administrator; Houjue led his companions to study under him, and his learning grew ever more refined.

sentences.zh: 久之，以歲貢生授華陰訓導，會地大震，人多傾壓死，上官令署縣事，救災扶傷，人胥悅服。

translations.literal: After a long while, as a tribute student he was appointed Assistant Instructor at Huayin; when a great earthquake struck and many were crushed, his superiors put him in charge of the county, and he relieved the disaster and tended the wounded until all were won over.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, as a tribute student he was appointed Assistant Instructor at Huayin; when a great earthquake struck and many were crushed, his superiors put him in charge of the county affairs, and he relieved the disaster and tended the wounded until all were won over.

sentences.zh: 及致仕歸，士民泣送載道。

translations.literal: When he retired and returned home, scholars and commoners wept and escorted him, filling the road.
translations.idiomatic: When he retired and returned home, scholars and commoners wept and escorted him, filling the road.

sentences.zh: 東昌知府羅汝芳、提學副使鄒善皆宗守仁學，與後覺同誌。

translations.literal: The prefect of Dongchang, Luo Rufang, and the Education Vice Commissioner Zou Shan both upheld Shouren's learning and were Houjue's companions in the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Dongchang, Luo Rufang, and the Education Vice Commissioner Zou Shan both upheld Shouren's learning and were Houjue's companions in the Way.

sentences.zh: 善為建願學書院，俾六郡士師事焉。

translations.literal: Shan built the Yuanxue Academy and had scholars from six prefectures take Houjue as master.
translations.idiomatic: Shan built the Yuanxue Academy and had scholars from six prefectures take Houjue as their master.

sentences.zh: 汝芳亦建見泰書院，時相討論。

translations.literal: Rufang also built the Jiantai Academy; they often met to debate.
translations.idiomatic: Rufang also built the Jiantai Academy; the two often met to debate.

sentences.zh: 猶以取友未廣，北走京師，南遊江左，務以親賢講學為事，門弟子日益進。

translations.literal: Still thinking his circle of friends too narrow, he went north to the capital and south through the Jiang-Zuo region, bent on drawing near to the worthy and lecturing on learning; his disciples grew daily in number.
translations.idiomatic: Still thinking his circle of friends too narrow, he went north to the capital and south through the Jiang-Zuo region, bent on drawing near to the worthy and lecturing on learning; his disciples grew daily in number.

sentences.zh: 凡吏於其土及道經茌平者，莫不造廬問業。

translations.literal: Every official who served in those parts or passed through Chiping on the road would visit his lodge to inquire after learning.
translations.idiomatic: Every official who served in those parts or passed through Chiping on the road would visit his lodge to inquire after learning.

sentences.zh: 巡撫李世達兩詣山居，病不能為禮，乃促席劇談，飽蔬食而去。

translations.literal: The governor Li Shida twice came to his mountain retreat; when Houjue was ill and could not perform full courtesies, Li simply drew close and talked earnestly, then left sated on plain vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: The governor Li Shida twice came to his mountain retreat; when Houjue was ill and could not perform full courtesies, Li simply drew close and talked earnestly, then left sated on plain vegetables.

sentences.zh: 平生不作詩，不談禪，不事著述，行孚遠近，學者稱之為弘山先生。

translations.literal: All his life he did not compose poetry, did not discuss Chan, did not write books; his conduct matched his words near and far, and scholars called him Master Hongshan.
translations.idiomatic: All his life he wrote no poetry, spoke no Chan, and published no books; his conduct matched his words near and far, and scholars called him Master Hongshan.

sentences.zh: 年七十六，以萬歷六年卒。

translations.literal: At seventy-six he died in the sixth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth year of Wanli, aged seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 其門人，孟秋、趙維新最著。

translations.literal: Among his disciples, Meng Qiu and Zhao Weixin were most prominent.
translations.idiomatic: Among his disciples, Meng Qiu and Zhao Weixin were the most prominent.

sentences.zh: 秋，自有傳。

translations.literal: Qiu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 維新，亦茌平人，年二十，聞後覺講良知之學。

translations.literal: Weixin, also of Chiping, was twenty when he heard Houjue lecture on innate knowing.
translations.idiomatic: Weixin, also of Chiping, was twenty when he heard Houjue lecture on the learning of innate knowing.

sentences.zh: 遂師事之。

translations.literal: He thereupon took Houjue as master.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon took Houjue as his master.

sentences.zh: 次其問答語，為《弘山教言》。

translations.literal: He arranged their question-and-answer sayings into 《Hongshan's Teachings》.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged their question-and-answer sayings into 《Hongshan's Teachings》.

sentences.zh: 性純孝，居喪，五味不入口，柴毀骨立，杖而後起。

translations.literal: Pure in filial nature, in mourning he took no food with the five flavors, wasted away until only bones remained, and could rise only leaning on a staff.
translations.idiomatic: Pure in filial nature, in mourning he took no food with the five flavors, wasted away until only bones remained, and could rise only leaning on a staff.

sentences.zh: 鄉人欲舉其孝行，力辭之。

translations.literal: When neighbors wished to recommend his filial conduct, he firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: When neighbors wished to recommend his filial conduct, he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 喪偶，五十年不再娶。

translations.literal: After his wife died, he did not remarry for fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: After his wife died, he did not remarry for fifty years.

sentences.zh: 嘗築垣得金一篋，工人持之去，維新不問。

translations.literal: Once when building a wall he unearthed a chest of gold; the workmen took it away, and Weixin never asked.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while building a wall, he unearthed a chest of gold; the workmen took it away, and Weixin never asked.

sentences.zh: 家貧，或並日而食，超然自得。

translations.literal: His household was poor—sometimes he ate only every other day—yet he remained utterly at ease.
translations.idiomatic: His household was poor—sometimes he ate only every other day—yet he remained utterly at ease.

sentences.zh: 亦以歲貢生為長山訓導，年九十二，無疾而終。

translations.literal: Also as a tribute student he became Assistant Instructor at Changshan; at ninety-two he died without illness.
translations.idiomatic: Also as a tribute student he became Assistant Instructor at Changshan; at ninety-two he died without illness.

sentences.zh: 鄧以贊，字汝德，新建人。

translations.literal: Deng Yizan, styled Rude, was a native of Xinjian.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yizan, styled Rude, came from Xinjian.

sentences.zh: 張元忭，字子藎，紹興山陰人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yuanbian, styled Zijin, was a native of Shanyin, Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuanbian, styled Zijin, came from Shanyin in Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 二人皆生有異質，又好讀書。

translations.literal: Both were born with unusual gifts and loved reading.
translations.idiomatic: Both were born with unusual gifts and loved reading.

sentences.zh: 以贊幼，見父與人論學，輒牽衣尾之，間出語類夙儒。

translations.literal: While still a child, Yizan would tug at his father's robe when he debated learning with others, and his occasional remarks sounded like those of a veteran scholar.
translations.idiomatic: While still a child, Yizan would tug at his father's robe when he debated learning with others, and his occasional remarks sounded like those of a veteran scholar.

sentences.zh: 父閔其勤學，嘗扃之鬥室。

translations.literal: His father, pitying his zeal, once locked him in a small room.
translations.idiomatic: His father, pitying his zeal, once locked him in a small room.

sentences.zh: 元忭素羸弱，母戒毋過勞，乃藏燈幕中，俟母寢始誦。

translations.literal: Yuanbian was naturally frail; his mother warned him not to overwork, so he hid a lamp behind the bed curtain and studied only after she slept.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbian was naturally frail; his mother warned him not to overwork, so he hid a lamp behind the bed curtain and studied only after she had fallen asleep.

sentences.zh: 十余歲時以氣節自負，聞楊繼盛死，為文遙誄之，慷慨泣下。

translations.literal: In his teens he prided himself on moral courage; when he heard of Yang Jisheng's death, he wrote a eulogy from afar and wept with passion.
translations.idiomatic: In his teens he prided himself on moral courage; when he heard of Yang Jisheng's death, he wrote a eulogy from afar and wept with passion.

sentences.zh: 父天復，官雲南副使，擊武定賊鳳繼祖有功。

translations.literal: Yizan's father Tianfu served as Vice Commissioner in Yunnan and won merit crushing the Wuding bandit Feng Jizu.
translations.idiomatic: Yizan's father Tianfu served as Vice Commissioner in Yunnan and won merit crushing the Wuding bandit Feng Jizu.

sentences.zh: 已，賊還襲武定，官軍敗績，巡撫呂光洵討滅之。

translations.literal: Later the bandits struck Wuding again; the army was routed, and the governor Lü Guangxun wiped them out.
translations.idiomatic: Later the bandits struck Wuding again; the army was routed, and the governor Lü Guangxun wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 至隆慶初，議者追理前失亡狀，逮天復赴雲南對簿，元忭適下第還，萬里護行，發盡白。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing, critics reopened the old failures; Tianfu was summoned to Yunnan for trial, and Yuanbian, having just failed the examinations, escorted him ten thousand li until his hair turned fully white.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longqing, critics reopened the old failures; Tianfu was summoned to Yunnan for trial, and Yuanbian, having just failed the examinations, escorted him ten thousand li until his hair turned fully white.

sentences.zh: 已，復馳詣闕下白冤，當事憐之，天復得削籍歸。

translations.literal: Then he galloped to court to plead innocence; the authorities took pity, and Tianfu was stripped of office and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Then he galloped to court to plead his father's innocence; the authorities took pity, and Tianfu was stripped of office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年，以贊舉會試第一，廷試第三，授編修，而元忭以廷試第一，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Longqing, Yizan placed first in the metropolitan examination and third in the palace examination, receiving appointment as Compiler; Yuanbian placed first in the palace examination and was appointed Revisionist.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Longqing, Yizan placed first in the metropolitan examination and third in the palace examination, receiving appointment as Compiler; Yuanbian placed first in the palace examination and was appointed Revisionist.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，座主張居正枋國政，以贊時有匡諫，居正弗善也，移疾歸。

translations.literal: At the start of Wanli, his chief examiner Zhang Juzheng held state power; Yizan sometimes offered corrective counsel, which Juzheng disliked, so he took sick leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wanli, his chief examiner Zhang Juzheng held state power; Yizan sometimes offered corrective counsel, which Juzheng disliked, so he took sick leave and returned home.

sentences.zh: 久之，補原官，旋引退。

translations.literal: After a long while he was restored to his former post, then soon withdrew again.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was restored to his former post, then soon withdrew again.

sentences.zh: 詔起中允，至中途復以念母返。

translations.literal: An edict recalled him as Vice Director of the Hanlin Academy, but midway he turned back out of concern for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled him as Vice Director of the Hanlin Academy, but midway he turned back out of concern for his mother.

sentences.zh: 再起南京祭酒，就擢禮部右侍郎，復就轉吏部，再疏請建儲，且力斥三王並封之非，中言：「中宮鐘愛元子，其願早正春宮，視臣民尤切。

translations.literal: Called again as Chancellor of the Nanjing Academy, he was soon promoted Vice Minister of Rites, then transferred to the Ministry of Personnel; he memorialized again asking for the heir's investiture and forcefully denounced the error of simultaneously enfeoffing three princes, writing in part: 'The empress dotes on her eldest son and wishes the Eastern Palace established early—her desire is even keener than that of officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Called again as Chancellor of the Nanjing Academy, he was soon promoted Vice Minister of Rites, then transferred to the Ministry of Personnel; he memorialized again asking for the heir's investiture and forcefully denounced the error of simultaneously enfeoffing three princes, writing in part: 'The empress dotes on her eldest son and wishes the Eastern Palace established early—her desire is even keener than that of officials and people.

sentences.zh: 陛下以厚中宮而緩冊立，殆未諒中宮心。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, seeking to indulge the empress, delays investiture—perhaps you have not grasped her heart.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, seeking to indulge the empress, delays investiture—perhaps you have not grasped her heart.

sentences.zh: 況信者，國之大寶，建儲一事，屢示更移，將使詔令不信於天下，非所以重宗廟，安社稷也。

translations.literal: Moreover trust is the great treasure of the state; to show repeated shifts on the matter of establishing the heir will make edicts untrusted under Heaven—that is no way to honor the ancestral temple and secure the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover trust is the great treasure of the state; to show repeated shifts on the matter of establishing the heir will make edicts untrusted under Heaven—that is no way to honor the ancestral temple and secure the realm.

sentences.zh: 」會廷臣多諫者，事竟寢。

translations.literal: Many court officials joined in remonstrance, and the affair was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Many court officials joined in remonstrance, and the affair was shelved.

sentences.zh: 尋召為吏部右侍郎，力辭不拜。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Vice Minister of Personnel but forcefully declined the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as Vice Minister of Personnel but forcefully declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 以贊登第二十余年，在官僅滿一考。

translations.literal: Yizan had passed the examinations more than twenty years earlier, yet held office for barely one full evaluation period.
translations.idiomatic: Yizan had passed the examinations more than twenty years earlier, yet held office for barely one full evaluation period.

sentences.zh: 居母憂，不勝喪而卒，贈禮部尚書，謚文潔。

translations.literal: In mourning for his mother he died overcome by grief; he was posthumously made Minister of Rites and given the posthumous title Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning for his mother he died overcome by grief; he was posthumously made Minister of Rites and given the posthumous title Wenjie.

sentences.zh: 元忭嘗抗疏救御史胡涍，又請進講《列女傳》於兩宮，修《二南》之化，皆不省。

translations.literal: Yuanbian had memorialized to save the censor Hu Kan, and asked that the 《Biographies of Exemplary Women》 be read before the two palaces to restore the transformation of the 《Two Souths》—all went unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbian had memorialized to save the censor Hu Kan, and asked that the 《Biographies of Exemplary Women》 be read before the two palaces to restore the transformation of the 《Two Souths》—all went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十年奉使楚府還，過家省母，既行心動，輒馳歸，僅五日，母卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Wanli, returning from an embassy to the Chu princely establishment, he stopped home to see his mother; after departing his heart misgave him, he rushed back, and within five days his mother died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Wanli, returning from an embassy to the Chu princely establishment, he stopped home to see his mother; after departing his heart misgave him, he rushed back, and within five days his mother died.

sentences.zh: 元忭奉二親疾，湯藥非口嘗弗進，居喪毀瘠，遵用古禮，鄉人多化之。

translations.literal: Yuanbian nursed both parents in illness; he never offered medicine he had not tasted himself; in mourning he wasted away and followed ancient rites, and many in his district were moved to reform.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbian nursed both parents in illness; he never offered medicine he had not tasted himself; in mourning he wasted away and followed ancient rites, and many in his district were moved to reform.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起故官，進左諭德，直經筵。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he returned to his former post, advanced to Left Tutor, and attended the Classics lectures.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he returned to his former post, advanced to Left Tutor, and attended the Classics lectures.

sentences.zh: 先是，元忭以帝登極恩，請復父官，詔許給冠帶。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the Emperor's accession amnesty, Yuanbian had asked restoration of his father's office; an edict allowed him only cap and sash.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the Emperor's accession amnesty, Yuanbian had asked restoration of his father's office; an edict allowed him only cap and sash.

sentences.zh: 至是復申前請，格不從。

translations.literal: Now he repeated the request and was refused.
translations.idiomatic: Now he repeated the request and was refused.

sentences.zh: 元忭泣曰：「吾無以下見父母矣。

translations.literal: Yuanbian wept and said, 'I have nothing with which to meet my parents beneath the earth.'
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbian wept and said, 'I have nothing with which to meet my parents beneath the earth.'

sentences.zh: 」遂悒悒得疾卒。

translations.literal: He sank into gloom, took ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He sank into gloom, took ill, and died.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追謚文恭。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was posthumously given the title Wen'gong.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianqi he was posthumously given the title Wen'gong.

sentences.zh: 以贊、元忭自未第時即從王畿遊，傳良知之學，然皆篤於孝行，躬行實踐。

translations.literal: Yizan and Yuanbian had studied under Wang Ji from before they passed the examinations, transmitting the learning of innate knowing, yet both were steadfast in filial conduct and earnest in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Yizan and Yuanbian had studied under Wang Ji from before they passed the examinations, transmitting the learning of innate knowing, yet both were steadfast in filial conduct and earnest in practice.

sentences.zh: 以贊品端誌潔，而元忭矩矱儼然，無流入禪寂之弊。

translations.literal: Yizan was upright and pure in purpose; Yuanbian was rigorously proper—not one fell into the pitfall of Chan quietism.
translations.idiomatic: Yizan was upright and pure in purpose; Yuanbian was rigorously proper—neither fell into the pitfall of Chan quietism.

sentences.zh: 元忭子汝霖，江西參議。

translations.literal: Yuanbian's son Rulin was Jiangxi Assistant Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbian's son Rulin served as Jiangxi Assistant Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 汝懋，御史。

translations.literal: Rumao was a censor.
translations.idiomatic: Rumao served as a censor.

sentences.zh: 孟化鯉，字叔龍，河南新安人。

translations.literal: Meng Huali, styled Shulong, was a native of Xin'an, Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Huali, styled Shulong, came from Xin'an in Henan.

sentences.zh: 孟秋，字子成，茌平人。

translations.literal: Meng Qiu, styled Zicheng, was from Chiping.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Qiu, styled Zicheng, came from Chiping.

sentences.zh: 化鯉年十六，慨然以聖賢自期。

translations.literal: At sixteen Huali resolved to measure himself against the sages.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen Huali resolved to measure himself against the sages.

sentences.zh: 而秋兒時受《詩》，至《桑中》諸篇，輒棄去不竟讀。

translations.literal: As a boy Qiu received the 《Classic of Poetry》; at the songs of 《Sangzhong》 and related pieces he would cast the book aside and not finish.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Qiu received the 《Classic of Poetry》; at the songs of 《Sangzhong》 and related pieces he would cast the book aside and not finish.

sentences.zh: 化鯉舉萬歷八年進士。

translations.literal: Huali passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Huali passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事，時相欲招致之，辭不往。

translations.literal: Appointed Principal in the Ministry of Revenue, the chief minister wished to win him over, but he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Principal in the Ministry of Revenue, the chief minister wished to win him over, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 榷稅河西務，與諸生講學，河西人屍祝之。

translations.literal: Collecting taxes at Hexiwu, he lectured with scholars there; the people of Hexiwu venerated him as if he were a god.
translations.idiomatic: Collecting taxes at Hexiwu, he lectured with scholars there; the people of Hexiwu venerated him as if he were a god.

sentences.zh: 南畿、山東大饑，奉命往振，全活多。

translations.literal: When great famine struck the southern capital region and Shandong, he was ordered to relieve it and saved many lives.
translations.idiomatic: When great famine struck the southern capital region and Shandong, he was ordered to relieve it and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 改吏部，歷文選郎中，佐尚書孫鑨黜陟，名籍甚。

translations.literal: Transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, he rose to Director of the Civil Appointments Section and assisted Minister Sun Zuan in promotions and demotions; his reputation was great.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, he rose to Director of the Civil Appointments Section and assisted Minister Sun Zuan in promotions and demotions; his reputation was great.

sentences.zh: 時內閣權重，每銓除必先白，化鯉獨否，中官請托復不應，以故多不悅。

translations.literal: The Grand Secretariat then wielded heavy power; every appointment had to be reported there first—Huali alone refused; eunuchs' requests likewise went unanswered, so many were displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Secretariat then wielded heavy power; every appointment had to be reported there first—Huali alone refused; eunuchs' requests likewise went unanswered, so many were displeased.

sentences.zh: 都給事中張棟先以建言削籍，化鯉奏起之，忤旨，奪堂官俸，謫化鯉及員外郎項復弘、主事姜仲軾雜職。

translations.literal: Chief Ceremonial Receiving Officer Zhang Dong had earlier been stripped for memorializing; Huali memorialized to restore him, defying the throne—his superiors' salaries were cut, and Huali with Vice Director Xiang Fuhong and Section Chief Jiang Zhongshi were demoted to miscellaneous posts.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Ceremonial Receiving Officer Zhang Dong had earlier been stripped for memorializing; Huali memorialized to restore him, defying the throne—his superiors' salaries were cut, and Huali with Vice Director Xiang Fuhong and Section Chief Jiang Zhongshi were demoted to miscellaneous posts.

sentences.zh: 閣臣疏救，命以原品調外。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries memorialized in his defense; the order was to transfer them at their original rank.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries memorialized in his defense; the order was to transfer them at their original rank.

sentences.zh: 頃之，言官復交章救，帝益怒，奪言官俸，斥化鯉等為民。

translations.literal: Soon remonstrating officials again submitted joint memorials; the Emperor grew angrier, cut their salaries, and banished Huali and others to common status.
translations.idiomatic: Soon remonstrating officials again submitted joint memorials; the Emperor grew angrier, cut their salaries, and banished Huali and others to common status.

sentences.zh: 既歸，築書院川上，與學者講習不輟，四方從遊者恒數百人。

translations.literal: After returning home he built the Chuanshang Academy and never ceased lecturing with scholars; students from all quarters who came to study constantly numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he built the Chuanshang Academy and never ceased lecturing with scholars; students from all quarters who came to study constantly numbered in the hundreds.

sentences.zh: 久之卒。

translations.literal: After a long while, he died.
translations.idiomatic: After many years, he passed away.

sentences.zh: 秋舉隆慶五年進士。

translations.literal: Qiu passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu took his jinshi degree in the fifth year of Longqing.

sentences.zh: 為昌黎知縣，有善政。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Changli and administered good government.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Changli, he earned a reputation for sound governance.

sentences.zh: 遷大理評事，去之日，老稚載道泣留。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a reviewer at the Court of Review; on the day he departed, old and young packed the roads, weeping to detain him.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to reviewer at the Court of Review, he left to such an outpouring of grief that old and young filled the roads, weeping and begging him to stay.

sentences.zh: 以職方員外郎督視山海關。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of War to oversee Shanhai Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Vice Director in the Bureau of War and sent to supervise Shanhai Pass.

sentences.zh: 關政久馳，奸人出入自擅，秋禁之嚴。

translations.literal: Pass administration had long been lax, with scoundrels coming and going at will; Qiu imposed strict prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Administration at the pass had long gone slack, and ruffians passed in and out unchecked; Qiu tightened the restrictions with severity.

sentences.zh: 中流言，萬歷九年京察坐貶，歸塗與妻孥共駕一牛車，道旁觀者鹹嘆息。

translations.literal: Malicious rumors reached the court; in the ninth year of Wanli he was demoted in the metropolitan inspection of officials. On the road home he shared a single oxcart with his wife and children, and onlookers by the wayside all sighed in sympathy.
translations.idiomatic: Slander reached the capital, and in the ninth year of Wanli he was demoted in the metropolitan review of officials. On the journey home he rode in a single oxcart with his wife and children, and every passerby along the road sighed in pity.

sentences.zh: 許孚遠嘗過張秋，造其廬，見茆屋數椽，書史狼藉其中，嘆曰：「孟我疆風味，大江以南未有也。

translations.literal: Xu Fuyuan once passed Zhangqiu and visited his cottage. He saw a few thatched beams, with books and records scattered about within, and sighed: "The flavor of Meng Wojiang—south of the Great River there has never been its like.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fuyuan once traveled through Zhangqiu and called at his dwelling. He found only a few thatched rafters, books and records strewn about inside, and exclaimed, "The spirit of Meng Wojiang—nothing like it has been seen south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 」我疆者，秋別號也。

translations.literal: " Wojiang was Qiu's art name.
translations.idiomatic: " Wojiang was Qiu's style name.

sentences.zh: 後起官刑部主事，歷尚寶丞少卿，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was recalled to office as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, rose through Vice Director and Junior Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia, and died.
