translations.idiomatic: Later he was recalled as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments, advanced through Vice Director and Junior Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 秋既歿，廷臣為請謚者章數十上。

translations.literal: After Qiu's death, officials at court submitted dozens of memorials requesting a posthumous title for him.
translations.idiomatic: After Qiu died, court officials submitted dozens of memorials asking that he be granted a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，賜謚清憲。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he was granted the posthumous name Qingxian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he was posthumously honored as Qingxian.

sentences.zh: 化鯉自貢入太學，即與秋道義相勖，後為吏部郎，而秋官尚寶，比舍居，食飲起居無弗共者，時人稱「二孟」。

translations.literal: Huali entered the Imperial Academy as a tribute student and immediately joined with Qiu in mutual encouragement on the path of righteousness. Later Huali served as a secretary in the Ministry of Personnel while Qiu held office in the Court of Imperial Regalia; they lived in adjoining quarters and shared everything in eating, drinking, and daily life. People of the time called them "the two Mengs."
translations.idiomatic: Huali entered the Imperial Academy as a tribute student and at once joined Qiu in urging one another along the path of righteousness. Later Huali served in the Ministry of Personnel while Qiu held office in the Court of Imperial Regalia; they lived side by side and shared every meal and every hour of the day. Their contemporaries called them "the two Mengs."

sentences.zh: 化鯉之學得之洛陽尤時熙，而秋受業於邑人張後覺。

translations.literal: Huali's learning came from You Shixi of Luoyang, while Qiu studied under his fellow townsman Zhang Houjue.
translations.idiomatic: Huali received his learning from You Shixi of Luoyang; Qiu studied under Zhang Houjue, a man of his own county.

sentences.zh: 時熙師曰劉魁，後覺則顏鑰、徐樾弟子也。

translations.literal: You's teacher was Liu Kui; Houjue was a disciple of Yan Yao and Xu Yue.
translations.idiomatic: You's master was Liu Kui; Houjue had studied under Yan Yao and Xu Yue.

sentences.zh: 來知德，字矣鮮，梁山人。

translations.literal: Lai Zhide, courtesy name Yixian, was a native of Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Zhide, styled Yixian, came from Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 幼有至行，有司舉為孝童。

translations.literal: From childhood he displayed supreme virtue, and the authorities nominated him as a filial youth.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he showed extraordinary moral conduct, and the local authorities nominated him as a filial youth.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十一年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year of Jiajing he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year of Jiajing he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 二親相繼歿，廬墓六年，不飲酒茹葷。

translations.literal: Both parents died in succession; he lived by their graves for six years, neither drinking wine nor eating meat.
translations.idiomatic: His parents died one after the other; he kept vigil at their graves for six years, taking neither wine nor meat.

sentences.zh: 服除，傷不及祿養，終身麻衣蔬食，誓不見有司。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, grieving that he had not been able to support his parents with official salary, he wore hemp garments and ate plain food for the rest of his life and swore never to appear before the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, anguished that he had never been able to support his parents on an official salary, he wore hemp and ate plain food for the rest of his life and vowed never again to present himself before the magistrates.

sentences.zh: 其學以致知為本，盡倫為要。

translations.literal: His learning took extending knowledge as its foundation and fulfilling human relations as its essential aim.
translations.idiomatic: His scholarship rested on extending knowledge and took the full fulfillment of human relations as its essential aim.

sentences.zh: 所著有《省覺錄》、《省事錄》、《理學辨疑》、《心學晦明解》諸書，而《周易集註》一篇用功尤篤。

translations.literal: Among his writings are 《Records of Self-Reflection》, 《Records of Simplifying Affairs》, 《Disputing Doubts in Neo-Confucian Learning》, and 《Clarifying the Obscure in Heart-Mind Learning》, but his single work 《Collected Commentaries on the Book of Changes》 commanded his deepest devotion.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote 《Records of Self-Reflection》, 《Records of Simplifying Affairs》, 《Disputing Doubts in Neo-Confucian Learning》, and 《Clarifying the Obscure in Heart-Mind Learning》, among other works, but it was his 《Collected Commentaries on the Book of Changes》 alone that held his deepest devotion.

sentences.zh: 自言學莫邃於《易》。

translations.literal: He said himself that no learning runs deeper than the 《Book of Changes》.
translations.idiomatic: He declared that no learning runs deeper than the 《Book of Changes》.

sentences.zh: 初，結廬釜山，學之六年無所得。

translations.literal: At first he built a hut on Mount Fu and studied there for six years without gaining anything.
translations.idiomatic: At first he built a hut on Mount Fu and studied there for six years without result.

sentences.zh: 後遠客求溪山中，覃思者數年，始悟《易》象。

translations.literal: Later he lodged as a distant guest in the mountains of Qiuxi and pondered deeply for several years before he first grasped the imagery of the 《Changes》.
translations.idiomatic: Later he withdrew as a guest to the mountains of Qiuxi and brooded for years before he first grasped the imagery of the 《Changes》.

sentences.zh: 又數年始悟文王《序卦》、孔子《雜卦》之意。

translations.literal: Several years more passed before he grasped the meaning of King Wen's 《Sequence of the Hexagrams》 and Confucius's 《Miscellaneous Hexagrams》.
translations.idiomatic: Several years more passed before he understood the intent of King Wen's 《Sequence of the Hexagrams》 and Confucius's 《Miscellaneous Hexagrams》.

sentences.zh: 又數年始悟卦變之非。

translations.literal: Several years more passed before he realized that hexagram change was mistaken doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Several years more passed before he saw through the error of hexagram-change theory.

sentences.zh: 蓋二十九年而後書成。

translations.literal: In all, twenty-nine years passed before the book was finished.
translations.idiomatic: In all, twenty-nine years elapsed before the book was complete.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十年，總督王象乾、巡撫郭子章合詞論薦，特授翰林待詔。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Wanli, Governor-General Wang Xiangqian and Provincial Governor Guo Zizhang jointly memorialized recommending him, and he was specially appointed Hanlin Attendant Draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Wanli, Governor-General Wang Xiangqian and Provincial Governor Guo Zizhang jointly recommended him, and he was specially appointed Hanlin Attendant Draftsman.

sentences.zh: 知德力辭，詔以所授官致仕，有司月給米三石，終其身。

translations.literal: Zhide firmly declined. An edict granted him retirement at the rank conferred and ordered the authorities to supply him three shi of rice monthly for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Zhide refused firmly. An edict allowed him to retire with the rank offered and ordered the local authorities to supply three shi of rice each month for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 鄧元錫，字汝極，南城人。

translations.literal: Deng Yuanxi, courtesy name Ruji, was a native of Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Yuanxi, styled Ruji, came from Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 十五喪父，水漿不入口。

translations.literal: At fifteen he lost his father and took no food or drink.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he lost his father and refused all food and drink.

sentences.zh: 十七行社倉法，惠其鄉人。

translations.literal: At seventeen he implemented the community granary system and brought benefit to his fellow townsmen.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he put the community granary system into practice and brought relief to his neighbors.

sentences.zh: 已為諸生，遊邑人羅汝芳門，又走吉安，學於諸先達。

translations.literal: After becoming a licentiate, he studied at the gate of Luo Rufang, a fellow townsman, then traveled to Ji'an to learn from various elder scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had become a licentiate, he studied under Luo Rufang, a fellow townsman, then traveled to Ji'an to learn from several elder masters.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三十四年舉於鄉，復從鄒守益、劉邦采、劉陽諸宿儒論學。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year of Jiajing he passed the provincial examination, then again pursued learning in discussion with such venerated scholars as Zou Shouyi, Liu Bangcai, and Liu Yang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year of Jiajing he passed the provincial examination, then resumed his studies in debate with such senior scholars as Zou Shouyi, Liu Bangcai, and Liu Yang.

sentences.zh: 後不復會試，杜門著述，逾三十年，《五經》皆有成書，閎深博奧，學者稱潛谷先生。

translations.literal: Afterward he no longer took the metropolitan examination. He shut his door to write for more than thirty years, completing works on all Five Classics—vast, deep, and profound—and scholars called him Master Qian'gu.
translations.idiomatic: He never again sat for the metropolitan examination. Shutting his door to write for more than thirty years, he produced finished works on all Five Classics—vast, deep, and abstruse—and scholars honored him as Master Qian'gu.

sentences.zh: 休寧範淶知南城時，重元錫。

translations.literal: When Fan Cai of Xiuning served as magistrate of Nancheng, he held Yuanxi in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Cai of Xiuning was magistrate of Nancheng, he held Yuanxi in the highest regard.

sentences.zh: 後為南昌知府，萬歷十六年入覲，薦元錫及劉元卿、章潢於朝。

translations.literal: Later, as prefect of Nanchang, he presented himself at court in the sixteenth year of Wanli and recommended Yuanxi, Liu Yuanqing, and Zhang Huang to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as prefect of Nanchang, he came to court in the sixteenth year of Wanli and recommended Yuanxi, Liu Yuanqing, and Zhang Huang to the throne.

sentences.zh: 南京祭酒趙用賢亦請征聘，如吳與弼、陳獻章故事。

translations.literal: Zhao Yongxian, Chancellor of the Nanjing Imperial Academy, also requested their summons and appointment on the precedent of Wu Yubi and Chen Xianzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yongxian, Chancellor of the Nanjing Imperial Academy, also petitioned for their summons on the precedent of Wu Yubi and Chen Xianzhang.

sentences.zh: 得旨，有司起送部試，元錫固辭。

translations.literal: An edict was received ordering the authorities to summon and send them for the Ministry examination; Yuanxi firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: An edict came down ordering the authorities to summon them and send them to the Ministry for examination; Yuanxi refused outright.

sentences.zh: 明年，御史王道顯復以元錫、元卿並薦，且請仿祖宗征辟故事，無拘部試。

translations.literal: The following year Censor Wang Daoxian again jointly recommended Yuanxi and Yuanqing and asked that the ancestral practice of imperial summons be followed, without requiring the Ministry examination.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Censor Wang Daoxian again recommended Yuanxi and Yuanqing together and asked that the old imperial practice of direct summons be restored, free of the Ministry examination.

sentences.zh: 詔令有司問病，痊可起送赴部，竟不行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the authorities to inquire after his health and, once recovered, to summon and send him to the Ministry; in the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: An edict instructed the authorities to inquire after his health and, once he was well, to summon and escort him to the Ministry—but in the end he never went.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，巡按御史秦大夔復並薦二人，詔以翰林待詔征之，有司敦遣上道，甫離家而卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, touring censor Qin Dakui again jointly recommended the two men. An edict appointed Yuanxi Hanlin Attendant Draftsman and summoned him. The authorities pressed him to depart, but he had barely left home when he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year touring censor Qin Dakui again recommended both men together. An edict appointed Yuanxi Hanlin Attendant Draftsman and summoned him to court. The authorities pressed him to set out, but he had scarcely left home when he died.

sentences.zh: 鄉人私謚文統先生。

translations.literal: His fellow townsmen privately bestowed on him the posthumous title Master Wentong.
translations.idiomatic: His neighbors privately honored him with the posthumous title Master Wentong.

sentences.zh: 元錫之學，淵源王守仁，不盡宗其說。

translations.literal: Yuanxi's learning took its source from Wang Shouren, but he did not wholly adopt his doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxi's learning traced its roots to Wang Shouren, though he did not follow every tenet of the school.

sentences.zh: 時心學盛行，謂學惟無覺，一覺即無余蘊，九容、九思、四教、六藝皆桎梏也。

translations.literal: At the time Heart-Mind Learning was widely practiced. Some held that learning consisted only in non-awareness, that a single moment of awakening left nothing else to be cultivated, and that the Nine Appearances, Nine Thoughts, Four Teachings, and Six Arts were all shackles.
translations.idiomatic: Heart-Mind Learning was then in full sway. Some held that true learning lay in forgetting all awareness, that one flash of awakening left nothing further to cultivate, and that the Nine Appearances, Nine Thoughts, Four Teachings, and Six Arts were nothing but fetters.

sentences.zh: 元錫力排之，故生平博極群書，而要歸於《六經》。

translations.literal: Yuanxi vigorously rejected this view. Accordingly he read exhaustively through all books in his lifetime, yet always returned to the 《Six Classics》 as his essential aim.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxi fought this view with all his strength. He read exhaustively through every book in his lifetime, yet always brought his learning back to the 《Six Classics》.

sentences.zh: 所著《五經繹》、《函史上下編》、《皇明書》，並行於世。

translations.literal: His works 《Commentaries on the Five Classics》, the upper and lower compilations of 《Histories in a Box》, and 《The Ming Dynasty Record》 all circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His 《Commentaries on the Five Classics》, the upper and lower volumes of 《Histories in a Box》, and 《The Ming Dynasty Record》 all circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 元卿，字調父，安福人。

translations.literal: Yuanqing, courtesy name Tiaofu, was a native of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing, styled Tiaofu, came from Anfu.

sentences.zh: 舉隆慶四年鄉試，明年會試，對策極陳時弊，主者不敢錄。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination in the fourth year of Longqing. The following year, in the metropolitan examination, his policy essay candidly set forth the ills of the age, and the examiners dared not pass him.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the fourth year of Longqing. The next year, in the metropolitan examination, his policy essay laid bare the ills of the age with unsparing candor, and the examiners dared not pass him.

sentences.zh: 張居正聞而大怒，下所司申飭，且令人密诇之，其人反以情告，乃獲免。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng heard of it he flew into a rage, ordered the responsible officials to reprimand him, and sent someone to spy on him secretly; the spy instead revealed the plot to him, and so he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng, hearing of it, flew into a rage, ordered the responsible offices to rebuke him, and sent a man to watch him in secret; the watcher instead confided the scheme to him, and so he escaped unscathed.

sentences.zh: 既歸，師同邑劉陽，王守仁弟子也。

translations.literal: After returning home he took as teacher Liu Yang of his native place, a disciple of Wang Shouren.
translations.idiomatic: Back home, he took Liu Yang of his own county as teacher—Liu Yang was a disciple of Wang Shouren.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二年，會試不第，遂絕意科名，務以求道為事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli he failed the metropolitan examination and thereafter abandoned all ambition for official rank, devoting himself to seeking the Way.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wanli he failed the metropolitan examination, abandoned all thought of office, and devoted himself wholly to seeking the Way.

sentences.zh: 既累被薦，乃召為國子博士。

translations.literal: After repeated recommendations, he was summoned to serve as Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended again and again, he was finally summoned to serve as Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 擢禮部主事，疏請早朝勤政，又請從祀鄒守益、王艮於文廟，厘正外蕃朝貢舊儀。

translations.literal: He was promoted to principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites. In memorials he requested early morning audiences and diligent governance, also asked that Zou Shouyi and Wang Gen be admitted to sacrifice in the Confucian temple, and sought to rectify the old ceremonial for foreign tributary missions.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites, he memorialized asking for early audiences and diligent governance, petitioned that Zou Shouyi and Wang Gen be admitted to sacrifice in the Confucian temple, and called for a correction of the old ceremonial for foreign tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 尋引疾歸，肆力撰述，有《山居草》、《還山續草》、《諸儒學案》、《賢弈編》、《思問編》、《禮律類要》、《大學新編》諸書。

translations.literal: Soon he cited illness to return home and devoted his strength to writing. His works include 《Mountain Dwelling Drafts》, 《Further Drafts on Returning to the Mountains》, 《Records of Various Confucian Schools》, 《Worthy Go Compositions》, 《Inquiries and Responses》, 《Essentials of Rites and Law》, and 《New Compilation of the Great Learning》.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he pleaded illness and returned home, throwing all his energy into writing. Among his books are 《Mountain Dwelling Drafts》, 《Further Drafts on Returning to the Mountains》, 《Records of Various Confucian Schools》, 《Worthy Go Compositions》, 《Inquiries and Responses》, 《Essentials of Rites and Law》, and 《New Compilation of the Great Learning》.

sentences.zh: 潢，字本清，南昌人。

translations.literal: Huang, courtesy name Benqing, was a native of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang, styled Benqing, came from Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，哀毀血溢。

translations.literal: While observing mourning for his father, his grief was so devastating that blood seeped from him.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his father, his grief was so extreme that blood seeped from his body.

sentences.zh: 構此洗堂，聯同誌講學。

translations.literal: He built the Cixi Hall and gathered fellow-minded scholars to lecture together.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Cixi Hall and gathered like-minded scholars to lecture together.

sentences.zh: 輯群書百二十七卷，曰《圖書編》。

translations.literal: He compiled one hundred twenty-seven juan of books from various sources, entitled 《Compilation of Diagrams and Writings》.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled one hundred twenty-seven juan drawn from many books, calling the work 《Compilation of Diagrams and Writings》.

sentences.zh: 又著《周易象義》、《時經原體》、《書經原始》、《春秋竊義》、《禮記劄言》、《論語約言》諸書。

translations.literal: He also wrote 《Image-Meanings of the Book of Changes》, 《Original Substance of the Seasonal Classic》, 《Original Foundations of the Book of Documents》, 《Private Meanings of the Spring and Autumn Annals》, 《Incisive Words on the Record of Rites》, and 《Concise Words on the Analects》.
translations.idiomatic: He also authored 《Image-Meanings of the Book of Changes》, 《Original Substance of the Seasonal Classic》, 《Original Foundations of the Book of Documents》, 《Private Meanings of the Spring and Autumn Annals》, 《Incisive Words on the Record of Rites》, and 《Concise Words on the Analects》.

sentences.zh: 從遊者甚眾。

translations.literal: Those who followed him to study were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Students who came to study under him were exceedingly numerous.

sentences.zh: 數被薦，從吏部侍郎楊時喬請，遙授順天訓導，如陳獻章、來知德故事，有司月給米三石贍其家。

translations.literal: Recommended on several occasions, he was at the request of Vice Minister of Personnel Yang Shiqiao remotely appointed Instructor of Shuntian on the precedent of Chen Xianzhang and Lai Zhide, and the authorities supplied his household three shi of rice monthly.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended many times, he was at the request of Vice Minister of Personnel Yang Shiqiao remotely appointed Instructor of Shuntian on the precedent of Chen Xianzhang and Lai Zhide, with the local authorities supplying his household three shi of rice each month.

sentences.zh: 卒於萬歷三十六年，年八十二。

translations.literal: He died in the thirty-sixth year of Wanli at the age of eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirty-sixth year of Wanli, aged eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 其鄉人稱潢自少迄老，口無非禮之言，身無非禮之行，交無非禮之友，目無非禮之書，乃私謚文德先生。

translations.literal: His fellow townsmen said that from youth to old age Huang's lips held no unseemly words, his person no unseemly conduct, his companions no unseemly friends, and his eyes no unseemly books; they therefore privately bestowed on him the posthumous title Master Wende.
translations.idiomatic: His neighbors said that from youth to old age Huang never spoke an unseemly word, never committed an unseemly act, never kept unseemly company, and never read an unseemly book; they therefore privately honored him with the posthumous title Master Wende.

sentences.zh: 自吳與弼後，元錫、元卿、潢並蒙薦辟，號「江右四君子」。

translations.literal: After Wu Yubi, Yuanxi, Yuanqing, and Huang were all honored with recommended summons and were styled the "Four Gentlemen of Jiangyou."
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Yubi, Yuanxi, Yuanqing, and Huang were all summoned by imperial recommendation and came to be known as the "Four Gentlemen of Jiangyou."
